# Helios results ledger

Current status (2026-09-13): the historical symbolic B1–B10 endpoint is complete,
integrated and audited; see the maintained [blueprint](helios-proof-blueprint.md).
Section 4 of [task list.md](../../task%20list.md) remains active. The concrete
proof-reuse attack, repair correctness, interactive proof prerequisites, adaptive
simulation, raw replay extraction and programmed-cache interpretation are
checked. Actual sampled honest-ballot constructor correspondence and request
provenance now also check. The latest entries below record exact scope and
integration evidence. Board-decision composition, full election integration and
all-PPT computational ballot secrecy remain open. The unified root project
uses Lean/Mathlib 4.33.1 and pinned VCVio; the symbolic endpoint is preserved.

The following ledger is chronological. Earlier open-premise statements describe
their checkpoint, not the current completed symbolic theorem.

## Historical finite-model milestone

The first milestone establishes replay and permutation counterexamples in a
finite symbolic model. It also checks that ciphertext-component weeding blocks
these witnesses while accepting fresh ballots. The [historical symbolic foundations](helios-symbolic.md) now extend the
term and observation vocabulary beyond the finite experiment. There is no
general Helios ballot secrecy theorem or computational security reduction in
this artifact.

At this checkpoint, [global confluence modulo E0](helios-confluence.md#global-confluence)
is machine-checked. The [full candidate-substitution reconstruction](helios-candidate-substitutions.md)
also completes source Lemma 9 with the authorised tail guard, including honest
abstention and arbitrary E-equivalent ground representatives. Earlier investigation
sections retain their historical open-premise and scope-gap statements; the
subsequent results discharge them. Static equivalence and full protocol privacy
remain open.

## Claim ledger

All declarations below are in `ExplainableCrypto.Helios`. The trusted definitions are in
[Model.lean](../../ExplainableCrypto/Helios/Model.lean): `valid`, `check`, `secrets`, `plaintext`,
`tally`, `run`, `RestrictedPrivacy` and the restricted `Recipe` interface.
The [model specification](helios-model.md) records the abstraction boundary,
source sections and independently derived arithmetic fixtures.

| Claim | Status | Formal oracle | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Original policy hides the swapped choices | Refuted, machine-checked | `original_not_private`, `replay_accepted`, `replay_tallies`, `replay_distinguishes` | One fixed replay recipe and public tally test |
| Whole-ballot duplicate rejection hides the choices | Refuted, machine-checked | `wholeBallot_not_private`, `permutation_accepted`, `permutation_tallies`, `permutation_distinguishes` | One fixed permutation recipe |
| Swapping preserves the ideal validity check | Machine-checked | `swap_preserves_validity` | Every `Ballot` in this model; not a cryptographic proof-system theorem |
| Component weeding blocks selected attacks | Machine-checked | `components_block_replay`, `components_block_permutation` | Both worlds and either honest target |
| Fresh ballots remain acceptable | Machine-checked | `fresh_ballots_accepted`, `ordinary_tallies`, `fresh_abstention_tallied` | Three finite policies; fresh symbolic allocations |
| Controls exclude degenerate implementations | Machine-checked | `ordinary_not_rejected`, `tally_not_constant`, `malformed_rejected`, `malformed_not_tallied`, `component_rejection_not_invalid_proof` | Reject-all, constant-tally and wrong-rejection explanations |
| Valid vote encoding contributes at most one | Machine-checked | `issued_aggregate_at_most_one` | All finite private vote assignments |
| Full repaired protocol preserves privacy | Unresolved | No theorem | See [repair discrepancy](helios-repair-ambiguity.md) |

The falsifiers use three voters and two candidates. Copying Alice contributes
her vote twice; swapping her components contributes the opposite candidate.
The positive controls publish `(2,1)` for a fresh X vote and `(1,1)` for fresh
abstention. These expectations come from the source protocol's one-hot encoding
and arithmetic, not from the Lean evaluator. The abstract public ciphertext
handles do not change across swapped worlds; only the final tally distinguishes
the attack runs.

## Property-based refutation gate

[Experiments.lean](../../ExplainableCrypto/Helios/Experiments.lean) uses Plausible's decorated
binders and explicitly inspects `TestResult`. Unexpected failure, `gaveUp`, or
success of the known-broken claim causes an evaluation error and build failure.

The negative control runs first, seed 1: equality of the public replay test in
the two worlds. It finds a counterexample at `w = true`, with zero shrinks.
The named `replay_distinguishes` theorem retains the decisive witness.

Three positive campaigns use seeds 1, 7 and 42, each configured for 500 instances
and maximum size 40. All nine runs succeed, with `gaveUp = 0`:

- swapping preserves validity for generated submissions;
- fresh ballots are accepted by generated policies;
- component weeding rejects either selected attack against either target.

Natural numbers are reduced modulo 3 or 4 to generate finite votes, policies
and recipe forms; Booleans generate worlds and targets. There are no premise
filters. These distributions are not claimed to be uniform over elections or
to cover arbitrary symbolic adversaries. The malformed constructor is an
intentional negative-control submission. Deterministic backstops are
`recipe_swap_validity`, `fresh_ballots_accepted`, `components_block_replay` and
`components_block_permutation`. Successful campaigns are validation evidence,
not proofs of secrecy.

## Reproduction and trust audit

Validation: the finite milestone originally passed in 3269 jobs; the renamed
library plus symbolic foundations and documented correction pass in 3277 jobs. Run from the
repository root, with the pinned Lean/Mathlib 4.33.1 (migrated from 4.32.0):

```sh
lake build
lake env lean ExplainableCrypto/Helios/Experiments.lean
lake env lean ExplainableCrypto/Helios/Audit.lean
```

[Audit.lean](../../ExplainableCrypto/Helios/Audit.lean) checks the public types and prints the
axioms of every theorem in Replay, Permutation and SPOT. Reported dependencies
are subsets of `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`; none reports
`sorryAx` or a custom cryptographic axiom. The attack privacy refutations use
only `propext`. The property-test harness is executable validation outside
these theorem proofs. No theorem uses `native_decide`.

Residual assumptions include ideal certificates, distinct symbolic allocations,
the fixed voter order, trusted tallying, two candidates and the restricted
recipe language. No equivalence to the full applied-pi process, concrete
ElGamal implementation or full decryption transcript has been proved. Upstream
VCVio/CatCrypt builds and the computational library decision remain separate
open tasks.


## Symbolic variable overlaps

Claim: a root-rule instance and a competing step inside one occurrence of a
substituted variable join after synchronising its other occurrences.
Status: machine-checked.
Formal oracle: `variable_peak_joined` in `Symbolic/VariableOverlap.lean`;
`lake build` and `lake env lean ExplainableCrypto/Helios/Symbolic/Audit.lean`.
Falsifier: a repeated-variable instance whose two branches cannot join.
Positive control: `VariableOverlapSPOT.decrypt_variable_peak`,
`partial_decrypt_variable_peak`, `check_zero_variable_peak`,
`check_one_variable_peak`, and the independent `remaining_copy_reduces` trace.
Negative control: `one_copy_changed_no_root_match` excludes immediate raw
matching after changing only one key copy.
PBT gate: `VariableOverlapExperiments.lean`, directed projection substitutions
and depth-0–3 syntax; seeds 1, 7 and 42, each configured for 500 instances at
maximum size 40, all successful with `gaveUp=0`; deterministic inputs 0–255
pass. The expected negative fails at `n=0`, seed 1, zero shrinks.
Trusted definitions: the fixed term signature, substitution, schema contexts,
root rules and reduction relations.
Reality oracle: the checksum-verified Cortier–Smyth paper, §5.2.1 E1, E2,
E5–E9 and Appendix B.2.2; fixture outputs derive from those rules.
Residual assumptions and unsupported cases: the explicit variable-position
premise does not cover fixed-constructor overlaps or arbitrary E0 alignments.
Full local confluence, structural secrecy lemmas and ballot secrecy remain open.
`lake build` passes (3290 jobs), including the new modules, controls, campaigns
and public-type audit. The final log contains no warnings, errors or `sorryAx`;
reported axioms are subsets of `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.
See the [confluence record](helios-confluence.md).

## Background constructor structure investigation

Claim: E0 preserves a term's rigid outer constructor and each of its arguments;
its AC operators require separate treatment. In particular, E0-equal
ciphertexts have E0-equal keys, nonces and plaintexts.
Status: machine-checked.
Formal oracle: `BaseEq.head_eq`, `BaseEq.argument`, and constructor
inversion lemmas in `BaseStructure.lean`.
Falsifier: one E0 equality identifying different rigid constructors or changing
an argument outside E0; commutativity already refutes unrestricted argument
injectivity for multiplication.
Positive control: ciphertext nonce composition can commute while ciphertext
shape and the other arguments remain fixed.
Negative control: multiplication of names 0 and 1 commutes, although those
names are not E0-equal. A constant head observation must also fail name separation.
PBT gate: `BaseStructureExperiments.lean` tests observations over all eight
generating E0 fixtures with seeds 1, 7 and 42, each configured for 500 instances
and maximum size 40; all succeed with `gaveUp=0`. Deterministic inputs 0–255
pass. Raw constructor preservation under E3 fails at `n=0`, seed 1, zero shrinks.
`addition_can_change_root` retains that counterexample. The head observation
separates distinct names and ciphertext/proof roots, excluding a constant observer.
Trusted definitions: `BaseEquation`, `BaseEq`, and the fixed term signature.
Reality oracle: Cortier–Smyth §5.2.1 E3/E4 and Appendix B.2.2's choice of E0;
only addition on zero/one changes an outer constructor, and only the three
listed AC operators can rearrange their arguments.
Residual assumptions and unsupported cases: these claims concern E0, not full
E equality. Normal-form constructor arguments, nonce non-deducibility, exhaustive
overlap coverage and ballot secrecy still require further proofs.

Related claim (machine-checked): two root-rule instances with E0-equal left
sides have E0-equal right sides when the root is not homomorphic multiplication.
The formal oracle is `rigid_root_outputs_base` in `RigidRootOverlap.lean`. Projections and decryption
return fixed paths through rigid arguments; both proof checks return `ok`.
A falsifier would require E0 to change such a path, or a root rule to return
another value. Positive controls use projection/decryption fixtures; the
negative raw-equality control uses zero versus zero+zero as projection outputs.
This is a finite rule-case consequence of the argument lemmas, not a claim
that arbitrary contextual overlaps or multiplication peaks are covered.

`rigid_root_peak_joined` exposes both steps from the same source and their join.
`decrypt_partial_sources_not_base` excludes simultaneous ordinary and partial
root decryption by E0 weight invariance and strict containment of the repeated
key. These are unconditional metatheorems about the specified relation; they
do not assume global confluence. `BaseEq.penc_shape` additionally exposes the
shape of an arbitrary E0-equivalent ciphertext representative.

The observations `headTag` and `rigidArgument` are metatheory functions, not
new operations in the public-recipe signature. They do not grant ciphertext
argument access to the adversary. E0 does not identify different rigid roots;
full E also contains destructor reductions and requires separate reasoning.
The combined structure/root increment passes `lake build` (3295 jobs), including
the public-type and axiom audit. The final log contains no warnings, errors or
`sorryAx`; only subsets of the three standard axioms are reported.

## Homomorphic root matching investigation

Claim: E0-equal two-ciphertext products match their ciphertext factors in the
same order or swapped, modulo E0. Consequently any two homomorphic root-rule
instances with E0-equal left sides have E0-equal outputs.
Status: machine-checked.
Formal oracle: `BaseEq.mul_factors`, `ciphertext_product_pairing` and
`homomorphic_root_outputs_base` in `HomomorphicRootOverlap.lean`.
Falsifier: E0 equality of two such products whose ciphertext factors admit
neither pairing, or whose resulting nonce/plaintext combinations are not E0-equal.
Positive control: swapping two ciphertext factors commutes both the nonce
composition and plaintext sum in the result.
Negative control: the ordered list of factors changes under commutativity;
an unordered multiset, not a list, is required. Distinct names must remain
separated in the quotient.
PBT gate: `HomomorphicRootExperiments.lean` checks the unordered factor-tag
invariant over every generating E0 fixture. Seeds 1, 7 and 42, each configured
for 500 instances at maximum size 40, pass with `gaveUp=0`; deterministic inputs
0–255 pass. The ordered-factor negative fails at `n=0`, seed 1, zero shrinks.
The executable tags are an approximation, not an E0 decision procedure.
Trusted definitions: E0 congruence, its quotient, top-level multiplication
flattening, and the unchanged E7 rule.
Reality oracle: E7 and the multiplication/nonce/addition AC laws in
Cortier–Smyth §5.2.1 and Appendix B.2.2.
Residual assumptions and unsupported cases: root matching is not all contextual
confluence. E0 alignment of nested redex positions remains a coverage obligation.

`HomomorphicRootSPOT.swapped_ciphertexts_join` retains the two independently
derived E7/commutativity routes, their join and unequal raw outputs.
`ordered_factors_not_invariant` retains the negative control for actual E0
quotient classes, using checked name separation. `baseClass_eq_iff` proves that
the quotient identifies exactly E0-equivalent terms; no new equality is assumed.

Combining this result with rigid root analysis gives `root_outputs_base` and
`root_peak_joined` for all seven root-rule schemata. The latter exposes both
steps from the same source and a join, with E0 equality of the two raw rule
sources as its only alignment premise. `JoinModulo.context` transports the
join through a common outer context. Arbitrary differing redex placements
remain unclassified. The general factor and root proofs ran after the directed
refutation gate. `lake build` passes (3295 jobs), including controls and the
public-type/axiom audit; no warnings, errors, custom axioms or `sorryAx` occur.

## Raw contextual normalization investigation

Claim: bottom-up normalization of the raw syntax is reachable by ordinary
contextual rewriting and invariant under every ordinary contextual rewrite.
This would join all ordinary contextual peaks, including nested and disjoint
positions, without enumerating pairs of syntax paths.
Status: machine-checked.
The proposed extension of this normalizer to modulo-E0 matching is refuted.
Formal oracle: `normalizeRaw_reachable`, `RootStep.normalize_eq`,
`RewriteStep.normalize_eq`, `ordinary_rewriting_confluent`, and
`raw_contextual_peak_joined` in `RawNormalization.lean`.
Falsifier: a root or contextual source-rule instance with different normalized
endpoints, or an output not reachable from its source.
Positive control: nested projection/decryption returns the independently chosen
name after normalizing its plaintext. All seven source-rule fixtures are tested.
Negative control: a decryption whose key matches only after E3 remains raw-stuck,
although it has a modulo step to its plaintext. Raw normalization is therefore
not proposed as a decision procedure for E0 or full E equality.
PBT gate: `RawNormalizationExperiments.lean` checks raw-rule/context invariance
and idempotence. Seeds 1, 7 and 42, each configured for 500 instances at maximum
size 40, pass with `gaveUp=0`; deterministic inputs 0–255 pass. The known-broken
E0-decryption claim fails at `n=0`, seed 1, zero shrinks.
Trusted definitions: raw root matching, ordinary contextual rewrite closure,
term constructors and bottom-up recursion.
Reality oracle: E1/E2/E5–E9, and E3 for the negative control, in Cortier–Smyth
§5.2.1. The expected nested fixture follows projection and decryption directly.
Residual assumptions and unsupported cases: E0 rearrangement can create new
matches, so ordinary contextual confluence alone does not discharge
`LocalConfluentModulo`. AC redex placement and background alignment remain open.

`RawReduces` is the reflexive-transitive closure of `RewriteStep`, which applies
root rules in ordinary syntax contexts. It differs from the existing `Reduces`
closure, whose steps include E0 changes. `normalizeRaw_reachable` gives actual
ordinary traces; rule invariance lifts through every `Context` constructor.
These proofs establish idempotence, raw irreducibility, and a literal common
descendant for any two ordinary reduction sequences. The public confluence
statement is unconditional for arbitrary variable types and terms.

Independent positive controls expose literal common descendants for disjoint
projections and decryption versus projection nested in its plaintext.
`RawNormalizationSPOT.raw_normalization_incomplete_modulo` retains a stronger
negative result than unequal raw representatives: an E0-only key match permits
a modulo step from a raw-irreducible source, and its normalized endpoints are
not even E0-equal. The proof uses the independently derived E3/decryption route
and the checked E0 constructor invariant.

The refutation gate ran before the general normalization proof. `lake build`
passes (3298 jobs), including the controls, campaigns, public theorem types and
axiom audit. The final log contains no warnings, errors or `sorryAx`; all
reported axioms are subsets of `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.
Confluence modulo E0 and the full privacy obligations remain open.

## Multiplication factor completeness investigation

Claim: equality of `Term.mulFactors` is equivalent to E0 equality, and a
selected pair of ciphertext factors plus a represented remainder yields an
actual homomorphic modulo step from any source with those factors.
Status: machine-checked.
Formal oracle: `baseEq_iff_mulFactors`, `Term.mulFactors_product`,
`homomorphic_step_of_factors`, and the empty-remainder counterpart.
Falsifier: equal quotient factor multisets with non-E0-equal product terms,
or a selected factor pair that cannot be exposed by E0 to perform E7.
Positive control: select two ciphertexts separated by an unrelated factor in
a nested product; preserve that remainder after combining the ciphertexts.
Negative controls: repeated factors must retain multiplicity; appending the
constant zero must not act as a multiplicative unit. An empty bookkeeping
product is not a term or an added E0 axiom.
PBT gate: `FactorReconstructionExperiments.lean` checks flatten/rebuild and
selection mechanics plus two independent key groups. Each property passes
seeds 1, 7 and 42, configured for 500 instances at maximum size 40, with
`gaveUp=0`; both deterministic backstops pass inputs 0–255. The false zero-unit
control fails at `n=0`, seed 1, zero shrinks.
The decidable syntax tests check representation mechanics; quotient completeness
requires the general theorem, not equality of factor head tags.
Trusted definitions: `BaseEq`, its existing quotient, top-level factor flattening,
and an auxiliary unit adjoined only to the quotient semigroup for finite folds.
Reality oracle: multiplication AC and E7 in Cortier–Smyth §5.2.1; no source
multiplicative unit equation is introduced.
Residual assumptions and unsupported cases: `homomorphic_selection_reachable`
constructs the remainder representation, including a separate empty case.
Exhaustive classification of arbitrary competing selections and internal
E0-dependent reductions remains open.

Remainder claim (machine-checked): every nonempty submultiset of an actual term's outer
factors is itself representable by a term. Its smallest falsifier would be one
retained factor without a representative, or two representable remainders whose
product loses a factor. The existing nonempty flatten/rebuild gate tests these
representation mechanics. `Term.subfactors_representable` removes the represented-remainder
premise from homomorphic pair selection; the empty remainder remains a separate
case and must not introduce a unit term.

Disjoint-selection claim (machine-checked): when a term's factor multiset contains two
specified ciphertext pairs plus any remainder, reducing either pair produces
branches that join after reducing the other pair. Each branch must expose its
exact retained factor multiset; otherwise an existential statement could choose
the same reduction twice. The pairs may use different keys, and the remainder
may be empty. The falsifier is a lost occurrence or failure to expose the
remaining pair. The independent control interleaves pairs under keys 0 and 1;
E7 combines within each key and leaves both resulting ciphertexts present.

Shared-selection claim (machine-checked): the previously checked three-ciphertext overlap
lifts to any source with those quotient factors plus an arbitrary remainder.
The branch factor multisets specify the first-two versus last-two combination.
The existing triple refutation gate and the factor-reconstruction/selection gate
supply the directed test evidence; the same AC endpoint proof must join the
branches after their second combinations. This does not itself prove that two
arbitrary factor selections fall into the identical, shared or disjoint cases.

`Term.mulFactors_product` reconstructs the exact E0 class in an auxiliary
`WithOne` semigroup. Every actual term folds to a non-unit element;
`Term.mulFactors_nonempty` forbids an empty factor bag for any term. This gives
`baseEq_iff_mulFactors` without a new equation or a confluence assumption.
`Term.factor_representable`, `factors_representable` and
`Term.subfactors_representable` build all nonempty remainders from actual factors.
`homomorphic_selection_reachable` then returns an actual `ModuloStep` and the
exact residual factor bag after replacing the selected pair by its combination.

`disjoint_homomorphic_selections_joined` and
`shared_homomorphic_selections_joined` expose two actual first steps, their
specified branch factor multisets, and a join. Disjoint pairs may use different
keys. Shared pairs use the checked three-ciphertext endpoint association. Both
lemmas allow arbitrary remainders, including empty ones; neither silently drops
multiplicity or a residual factor.

Independent controls retain a nonadjacent pair, the two-factor no-sentinel case,
a distinct-key disjoint peak, and a shared peak with an unrelated name retained
on both branches. `zero_not_multiplication_unit`, `repeated_factor_not_erased`,
and `cross_key_pair_no_match` exclude added unit laws, set-like factor collapse,
and wrong-key fusion. The existing triple gate supplies the directed shared
endpoint test; the reconstruction and two-key gates run before their general
selection proofs.

Validation: `lake build` passes (3301 jobs), including public-type and axiom
checks, the controls and campaigns. The final log has no warnings, errors or
`sorryAx`; reported axioms are subsets of `propext`, `Classical.choice` and
`Quot.sound`. No whole-system confluence or privacy claim is added.

## Exhaustive outer-fusion joins

Claim: two two-occurrence submultisets of a common source are identical, share
one occurrence with an explicit three-occurrence source decomposition, or fit
as disjoint pairs with an explicit remainder. Multiplicity is preserved even
when one selection contains the same value twice.
Status: machine-checked.
Formal oracle: `pair_selection_cases` in `PairSelectionCases.lean`; `lake build`.
Falsifier: two valid size-two selections for which none of the three source
and selection decompositions holds.
Positive controls: identical repeated pairs; `{0,0}` versus `{0,1}` sharing one
occurrence; and disjoint repeated pairs `{0,0}` versus `{1,1}`.
Negative control: deduplicating `{n,n}` changes its cardinality from two to one.
PBT gate: reachable selections from distinct indices in generated
source lists pass seeds 1, 7 and 42, configured for 500 instances at maximum size
40, with `gaveUp=0`. The deterministic backstop passes inputs 0–255. The false
deduplication claim fails at `n=0`, seed 1, zero shrinks;
`deduplication_loses_an_occurrence` retains the checked counterexample. Every test also checks the generator's submultiset and cardinality
conditions; invalid generated selections are failures, not discarded premises.
Trusted definitions: multiset inclusion, intersection, union, difference and
cardinality. The common source is a multiset of occurrences, not a set.
Reality oracle: direct occurrence counting in the three independent fixtures;
Mathlib's multiset operations and their count equations supply the formal algebra.
Residual assumptions and unsupported cases: the theorem classifies selected
bags and provides a valid occurrence decomposition; it does not recover syntax
position identities or assert a unique decomposition. Repeated equal values can
admit several realizations. Internal E0-dependent reductions and whole-system
confluence remain open.

Fusion application claim (machine-checked): arbitrary outer-product homomorphic fusion
witnesses from one factor bag have equal results or a one-fusion diamond.
A generic bag rule must have size-two inputs, a unique output for a fixed
input bag, and the shared-input association property. These premises are
proved for the existing E7 quotient rule by `CipherFusion.rank`,
`CipherFusion.deterministic` and `CipherFusion.associate`.
The smallest falsifier is a shared-input rule pair whose second combinations
cannot agree. Existing triple, distinct-key, remainder and multiplicity controls
supply independently derived fixtures; the new pair gate covers the exhaustive
bag decomposition. Internal rewrites inside factors are outside this relation.

Boundary control (machine-checked): reducing a projection inside one ciphertext key
can enable an outer fusion, while that key-reduction step is not an
`OuterFusion`. The literal source has two ciphertext factors, with keys
`fst(pair(name 0, bottom))` and `name 0`; the target has key `name 0` in both.
Formal oracle: a checked contextual `ModuloStep`, failed/successful raw root
matches, and factor-cardinality exclusion. A falsifier is an unexpected source
root match or failure of the target E7 match. The independent oracle is the
literal projection rule followed by E7's repeated-key condition. This fixture
pins a remaining internal/mixed obligation rather than proving its join theorem.


`bag_fusion_diamond` states the generic rule laws as explicit hypotheses.
`cipher_fusion_diamond` discharges them for E7, including alignment of key,
nonce and plaintext representatives when the selected pairs share a ciphertext
class. It covers arbitrary competing fusion witnesses without a supplied case
classification or a distinct-factor assumption. `realize_cipher_fusion` turns
each abstract branch into an actual modulo step. `outer_fusion_peak_joined`
concludes both specified first steps and `JoinModulo` for their endpoints.
Its hypotheses are `OuterFusion a b` and `OuterFusion a c`; these describe
replacement of two outer ciphertext factors by their combined ciphertext,
with the exact remainder retained.

`OuterFusionSPOT.repeated_selection_peak` checks duplicated ciphertexts and
syntactically different branch terms. `background_key_peak` checks failed raw
root matching with two E0-equivalent key representatives, actual modulo steps,
and a join. `projection_is_not_outer_fusion` proves that `OuterFusion` is a
proper subrelation of `ModuloStep`. `internal_key_enables_fusion` retains the
internal-key boundary fixture above: the internal step preserves two factors,
whereas `OuterFusion.card_step` requires a decrease of one. The same fixture
checks failed source and successful target root matching. These literal controls
exclude both a trivial identical-endpoint interpretation and an unjustified
promotion to all modulo steps.

Validation: `lake build` passes (3306 jobs), including all controls, campaigns,
and the public-type/axiom audit. The final log contains no warnings, errors or
`sorryAx`. All reported axiom sets are subsets of `propext`, `Classical.choice`
and `Quot.sound`. Trusted definitions remain E0, quotient factor bags, E7 and
the existing contextual modulo reduction; no attacker operation or protocol
assumption is added. Coverage of arbitrary internal/mixed reductions, full-E
structure and protocol privacy remains open.

## Fusion versus internal ciphertext reduction investigation

Goal: discharge mixed peaks between E7 fusion and a reduction inside one of
its selected ciphertexts, including reductions that temporarily break the
repeated-key match and arbitrary outer factor remainders.
Claim (machine-checked): every modulo step from `penc(k,r,m)` changes one component
by a modulo step, with the target equal modulo E0 to the corresponding updated
ciphertext. Such a step competes joinably with fusion against `penc(k,s,n)`.
The key case must synchronize the other key copy; nonce and plaintext cases
commute through the corresponding E7 output constructor.
Falsifier: a ciphertext step outside the three component cases, or a key-copy
change whose two routes cannot reach the same synchronized ciphertext.
Formal oracle: `ModuloStep.penc_cases`, `fusion_ciphertext_peak_joined`,
`fusion_factor_peak_joined` and `outer_fusion_modulo_peak_joined`; `lake build`.
Reality oracle: E7's repeated key and component output syntax, E1 projection,
and E0's preservation of the ciphertext constructor and its argument classes.
Positive control: projection reductions in each component, retaining exact
nonconstant nonce/plaintext output expressions and an unrelated outer factor.
Negative control: reducing only one projected key copy does not preserve raw
root applicability; accepting that mismatched fusion must fail the harness.
PBT gate: generated reachable root-rule pairs in each component pass seeds
1, 7 and 42, configured for 500 cases at maximum size 40, with `gaveUp=0`.
The deterministic backstop passes inputs 0–255. The false one-key-copy claim
fails at `n=0`, seed 1, zero shrinks; `one_key_copy_blocks_fusion` retains it.
These executable checks validate raw rule outputs and synchronization fixtures;
they do not decide the general quotient join relation.
Scope: the initial component theorem joins fusion with a step in its specified
first ciphertext. The extensions below cover every competing modulo step when
one branch is an outer fusion; two factor reductions remain a separate case.

Exhaustive mixed extension (machine-checked): define a factor step by one actual modulo
step from a single outer-factor representative, retaining its exact remainder
and all factors of the new term. Any `OuterFusion` and factor step from the
same source join. If the changed factor is selected for fusion, ciphertext
inversion supplies the component cases; otherwise the two actions commute.
Duplicates allow more than one realization, but bag cancellation identifies the
same branch. A projection can expand one factor into multiple factors, so the
relation must retain the entire new factor bag rather than one new class.
Independent additional control: a disjoint projection returns a product of two
names, with both names retained after fusion. A one-output-class replacement
would lose that structure. This relation requires a single-factor source representative. The step-coverage
theorem below proves that it and outer fusion exhaust modulo steps.

Step coverage (machine-checked): every `ModuloStep` is an `OuterFusion`
or a `FactorStep`. Inspect the raw context underlying the step: multiplication
contexts extend the factor remainder; the first other constructor encloses a
single outer factor. At the root, E7 is a fusion and every other oriented source
is a single factor. E0 preserves both endpoint factor bags. The smallest
falsifier is a contextual rule instance whose selected source crosses outer
factor boundaries without being E7. Existing all-rule context campaigns and
the mixed controls test the rule/context mechanisms; the structural proof must
cover the full `Context` and `RootStep` constructors rather than infer coverage
from these finite fixtures. This is a classification theorem, not a join for
factor-step/factor-step peaks.


`ModuloStep.penc_cases` exhausts arbitrary modulo steps from a ciphertext,
including E0 changes before and after the underlying raw contextual step.
It returns a component step and an E0 equality for the whole target. In the
key case, `fusion_ciphertext_peak_joined` synchronizes the untouched ciphertext
key before applying E7. In the nonce and plaintext cases, the component step
commutes through E7's nonce composition or plaintext addition. No local
confluence premise is used.

`ModuloStep.of_factors` and `JoinModulo.of_factors` lift steps and joins through
arbitrary factor remainders. They reconstruct nonempty remainders and handle
empty ones without an object-language unit. `FactorStep` retains the selected
representative, its actual modulo step, and both exact endpoint factor bags.
Its output can be a product: `disjoint_expansion_peak` retains two output names
from a projection rather than treating that product as one factor.
`fusion_factor_peak_joined` exhausts membership of the selected factor in the
fusion pair or its remainder; ciphertext orientation and bag cancellation
handle equivalent representatives and repeated values.

`RewriteStep.factor_cases` covers every root rule and every context constructor.
Multiplication contexts extend the remainder, while any other enclosing
constructor makes the entire raw source one factor. `ModuloStep.factor_cases`
transports this result through arbitrary E0 endpoint changes. The two cases
are not claimed to be exclusive. Combining them with the earlier fusion/fusion
result gives `outer_fusion_modulo_peak_joined`: an `OuterFusion a b` and any
`ModuloStep a c` imply `JoinModulo b c`.

Independent checked controls cover a nonadjacent selected ciphertext and an
unrelated retained name, a fixed synchronized key endpoint on both routes,
nonce and plaintext steps, an E0 change in an unchanged argument at the target,
and a disjoint projection that expands into two factors. The negative controls
reject one-copy raw key matching and show that the expanding factor step cannot
be an outer fusion. They pin both component behavior and relation boundaries.

Validation: `lake build` passes (3312 jobs), including the seeded gate,
deterministic backstop, controls and public-type/axiom audit. The final log has
no warnings, errors or `sorryAx`; all reported axiom sets are subsets of
`propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The only classification inputs
are the existing `RootStep`, `Context`, E0 equality and factor definitions.
These are metatheory relations and do not add a public ciphertext destructor.
Remaining work: join arbitrary factor-step/factor-step peaks, including the
same-factor case with fixed constructors and nonlinear matches. Classifying
steps does not itself join that case or prove full-E structure or privacy.

## Factor versus factor reduction investigation

Goal: finish the outer-product overlap analysis and isolate the remaining
single-factor confluence obligation without assuming whole-system confluence.
Claim (machine-checked): two single-factor selections from one source
bag either have equal selected classes and equal residual bags, or admit a
common disjoint-occurrence remainder. Disjoint actual factor reductions commute,
even when either output expands into a product. Equal selected classes reduce
the peak to two reductions from the same single-factor representative.
Formal oracle: `singleton_selection_cases`, `disjoint_factor_reductions_joined`,
`local_confluence_iff_single_factor` and `locally_confluent_at_penc`; `lake build`.
Falsifier: a lost occurrence in the two residual decompositions, or loss of an
output factor when two disjoint reductions expand their selected terms.
Reality oracle: direct multiset occurrence accounting and two independent E1/E2
projection fixtures, with a two-name product returned by each projection.
Positive controls: distinct factor selections; repeated equal selections;
disjoint projections returning distinct two-factor products; an E0-equivalent
single-factor representative; and a nontrivial common descendant.
Negative controls: deduplicating repeated factors changes the bag; a selected
factor need not have strictly smaller crypto weight than its containing product
because multiplication by zero contributes no additional weight.
PBT gate: valid singleton selections from generated source lists check
source/residual decompositions and full two-element replacement bags. Seeds
1, 7 and 42 pass, configured for 500 cases at maximum size 40, with `gaveUp=0`.
The deterministic backstop passes inputs 0–255. The false strict-weight claim
fails at `n=0`, seed 1, zero shrinks (`1 < 1`);
`factor_weight_need_not_decrease` retains the checked counterexample.
Residual assumption: local confluence on singleton-factor sources is a new
explicit remaining obligation, not a proved fact or cryptographic axiom.

Ciphertext singleton implication (machine-checked): local confluence at each of a ciphertext's
three components implies local confluence at that ciphertext. Ciphertext-step
inversion supplies one component step and base equalities for the untouched
components. Different component changes commute; two changes in the same
component use its explicit local-confluence hypothesis. The falsifier is an
unaccounted ciphertext-root rule or wrong-component update. The independent
control changes key and nonce projections separately and retains an exact
updated ciphertext as the common endpoint. Existing component campaigns supply
the directed executable fixture gate. This implication does not establish
local confluence of arbitrary component terms.


`singleton_selection_cases` retains both residual bags. Equal selected classes
have equal residuals; the other case exposes a common disjoint remainder.
`disjoint_factor_reductions_joined` is unconditional for its two actual steps
and specified source/branch bags. Each step preserves the other selected term,
and their common descendant contains both complete output factor bags. Empty
remainders are supported by the existing factor-lifting lemmas.

`factor_peaks_joined_of_factor_local` uses the disjoint theorem or aligns equal
selected classes via E0 and invokes `FactorsLocallyConfluent source`. This
premise requires local confluence for singleton representatives actually present
in the source bag. `modulo_peaks_joined_of_factor_local` also handles the outer
fusion cases, using the earlier unconditional result.
`local_confluence_iff_single_factor` gives the exact equivalence between
`LocalConfluentModulo V` and `SingleFactorLocalConfluent V`. The latter remains
unproved; the equivalence isolates the outstanding obligation and does not
remove it from any downstream theorem.

`locally_confluent_at_penc` reduces a ciphertext's local confluence to explicit
`LocallyConfluentAt` hypotheses for its key, nonce and plaintext. Exhaustive
ciphertext inversion supplies the component cases, and
`LocallyConfluentAt.base_or_step` accounts for unchanged E0 representatives.
`ciphertext_key_nonce_steps` separately proves an unconditional diamond for
changes in different components, exposing its exact endpoint.

Independent controls use E1 and E2 projections that each return a two-name
product, with an unrelated name retained. Both branches have four factors and
the specified common descendant has five; `disjoint_routes_expected` proves
both actual second steps. `same_factor_component_peak` checks key and nonce
changes in one ciphertext, including an E0-equivalent plaintext representative,
and both steps to the same literal endpoint. The branches are syntactically
different. Repeated singleton selections retain their additional occurrence;
the weight counterexample rules out an invalid well-founded recursion argument.

Validation: `lake build` passes (3316 jobs), including the campaigns, controls,
and public-type/axiom audit. No warnings, errors or `sorryAx` occur in the final
log; reported axiom sets are subsets of `propext`, `Classical.choice` and
`Quot.sound`. The factor and local-confluence predicates are metatheory over the
unchanged symbolic rules. No public observation or attacker capability changes.
Remaining work: establish `SingleFactorLocalConfluent V`, including active-root
versus internal reductions, nonlinear matching and the remaining constructor
cases. A containing product need not have greater crypto weight than its factor;
any induction that needs strict descent must justify an appropriate measure.
Full-E structure, accepted-ballot characterisation and privacy remain open.

## Unary and rigid-binary singleton investigation

Goal: discharge projection root/internal peaks and reduce unary and passive
rigid-binary local confluence to their argument sources.
Claim (machine-checked): every modulo step from a unary term is a root
rule modulo E0 or a step in its argument; every step from a non-AC binary term
is a root rule modulo E0 or a step in one argument. Pairing and partial-decryption
constructors have no root rule. For fst/snd, a root projection competes joinably
with every reduction inside the pair, including changed or discarded members.
Formal oracle: `ModuloStep.unary_cases`, `ModuloStep.rigid_binary_cases`,
`unary_root_inner_joined`, `locally_confluent_at_unary` and
`locally_confluent_at_passive_binary`; `lake build`.
Falsifier: a non-AC argument reordered by E0, a projection-root/internal peak
without a join, or an omitted raw context case in the inversion proof.
Reality oracle: source E1/E2 select the ordered first/second member; E0 has no
pair permutation or projection equation. E5/E6 have decryption at the root,
not partial decryption, and E7 has multiplication at the root.
Positive controls: reductions in selected and discarded pair members; both
projections with distinct literal outputs; E0-expanded pair members; nontrivial
nested steps under pk; and exact common endpoints.
Negative control: fst and snd do not return the same member of an arbitrary
ordered pair. The existing pair noncommutativity and failed-root-match controls
supply nearby boundary fixtures.
PBT gate: independently expected root projection outputs before and after
reachable member changes from all seven rule families pass seeds 1, 7 and 42,
configured for 500 cases at maximum size 40, with `gaveUp=0`. The deterministic
backstop passes inputs 0–255. The false projection-equality property fails at
`n=0`, seed 1, zero shrinks, returning names 0 and 1 respectively.
`projection_outputs_differ` retains this checked counterexample.
Residual assumptions: local confluence of argument terms remains explicit.
These implications do not prove whole-system or singleton-source confluence.

Atomic base claim (machine-checked): names, variables and constants are irreducible modulo
E0. E0 cannot change a name or variable to another term shape, and constants
have zero crypto weight. The formal oracle is head preservation plus raw-step
inversion and the existing zero-weight theorem. A falsifier is any actual step
from one of these atoms. This irreducibility is used only as the base case for
local-confluence implications; positive controls must also instantiate those
implications on terms with actual competing projection steps.


`RootModuloStep` packages one root-rule instance with E0 source and target
changes. `RootModuloStep.outputs_base` derives root/root endpoint equality
from the earlier all-rule root theorem. It does not hide a contextual reduction
in its definition. `BaseEq.unary_shape` and `BaseEq.rigid_binary_shape` preserve
the outer constructor and ordered argument classes. The latter requires
`¬ AC f`; it must not be applied to multiplication, addition or composition.

`ModuloStep.unary_cases` and `ModuloStep.rigid_binary_cases` exhaust the root
and argument cases for arbitrary E0 representatives. The binary theorem includes
decryption's active root alternative. `RootModuloStep.not_passive_binary`
excludes that alternative only for pairing and partial-decryption construction.
`RootModuloStep.unary_projection_cases` shows that the only unary roots are
fst/snd on pairs. Exhaustive pair-step inversion then proves
`fst_pair_step_joined` and `snd_pair_step_joined`: changes in selected members
are followed on both routes, while changes in discarded members are erased.
`unary_root_inner_joined` includes E0 changes before and after the root rule.

`locally_confluent_at_unary` consequently covers all three unary operators
under one explicit `LocallyConfluentAt` hypothesis for the argument. Root/root
and root/internal cases are discharged; two internal changes use the argument
hypothesis. `locally_confluent_at_passive_binary` covers pairing and partial
decryption under the two argument hypotheses. Names and variables are
irreducible because E0 preserves their literal identity and raw steps cannot
start there. Constants use the earlier zero-weight irreducibility theorem.
`Irreducible.locally_confluent_at` supplies these atomic base cases only; it
is deliberately a no-peak statement.

`UnaryLocalSPOT.nested_projection_local` instantiates the constructor
implications without a remaining local-confluence premise. Its source has two
specified distinct first-step endpoints, and `nested_routes_expected` checks
both steps to the literal expected name. Further controls cover all four
selected/discarded projection-member combinations, independent E0 changes in
root and internal targets, ordered-pair noncommutativity, a real contextual step
under pk despite failed root matching, and two competing component reductions
under partial-decryption construction. The last two sources also have checked
local confluence with actual progress. These controls distinguish the useful
constructor implications from the vacuous atomic base cases.

Validation: `lake build` passes (3321 jobs), including the gate, deterministic
backstop, controls and public-type/axiom audit. The final log has no warnings,
errors or `sorryAx`; reported axiom sets are subsets of `propext`,
`Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. All constructor and step observations remain
metatheory; no new ciphertext observation or public-recipe operation is added.
Remaining cases include proof construction, active decryption and proof checking,
and the AC constructor analysis needed to discharge `SingleFactorLocalConfluent V`.
The checked constructor implications do not establish their arbitrary argument
hypotheses, full-E structure, accepted-ballot characterisation or privacy.

## Active decryption singleton investigation

Goal: discharge E5/E6 root/internal peaks and derive local confluence at active
decryption from explicit local-confluence hypotheses for its two arguments.
Claim (machine-checked): every root decryption modulo E0 is an E5 or E6
instance. A competing step in either argument can be joined by synchronizing
all remaining key/ciphertext copies and applying the same rule at the updated
parameters. Plaintext updates are followed from the original root output too.
Formal oracle: `ModuloStep.keyCiphertext_parameters`, the four canonical
E5/E6 overlap theorems in `DecryptionOverlap.lean`,
`RootModuloStep.decryption_cases`, `decryption_root_left_joined`,
`decryption_root_right_joined` and `locally_confluent_at_decryption`; `lake build`.
Falsifier: a ciphertext public-key step not induced by its private-key argument,
an omitted E6 copy that cannot be synchronized, or an output unrelated to the
updated plaintext.
Reality oracle: source E5/E6 syntax, including the three private-key occurrences
and two ciphertext occurrences in E6; E0 preserves pk, penc, partialDecrypt and
dec constructors and their ordered component classes.
Positive controls: changes in key, nonce and plaintext; changes on either side
of active decryption; all E6 key copies restored; literal updated plaintext
endpoints; independent E0 changes in ciphertext representatives.
Negative control: changing only one repeated ciphertext in E6 does not retain
raw root applicability. This is a matching control, not a privacy claim.
PBT gate: generated reachable parameter changes from all seven root-rule
families check independently expected E5/E6 outputs before and after
synchronization. Seeds 1, 7 and 42 pass, configured for 500 cases at maximum
size 40, with `gaveUp=0`. The deterministic backstop passes 0–255. The false
one-copy matching property fails at `n=0`, seed 1, zero shrinks;
`distinct_ciphertext_copies_no_match` retains its checked counterexample.
These checks cover executable synchronization fixtures, not general quotient
joinability. Initial parser failures from reserved identifiers were proof
engineering errors, corrected before the successful positive campaign.
Residual assumptions: root/internal joins are unconditional for the supplied
steps. The final constructor implication requires local confluence of its two
argument sources; those hypotheses do not establish whole-system confluence.


`ModuloStep.pk_cases` proves that every public-key constructor step originates
in its argument. `ModuloStep.keyCiphertext_parameters` combines that result with
ciphertext inversion to give an E0-equivalent target ciphertext and reductions
of the private-key, nonce and plaintext parameters. The abbreviation
`keyCiphertext` is the existing E5/E6 pattern, not a new constructor or a public
extraction operation.

`decrypt_key_step_joined` and `decrypt_ciphertext_step_joined` cover E5's two
argument positions. `partial_decrypt_left_step_joined` covers changes in E6's
explicit key or left ciphertext; `partial_decrypt_right_step_joined` covers the
right ciphertext. The untouched copies follow the same parameter reductions.
If plaintext changes, the old root result follows that reduction too. The
common result is the synchronized plaintext, not an arbitrary witness chosen
by local confluence.

`RootModuloStep.decryption_cases` exhausts active decryption roots as E5 or E6,
with source-component and result equalities modulo E0. The two generic
`decryption_root_*_joined` theorems therefore cover arbitrary root/internal
peaks in either argument, including different E0 representatives.
`locally_confluent_at_rigid_binary` keeps its root/internal obligations explicit;
`locally_confluent_at_decryption` discharges both for decryption. Its only
remaining hypotheses are `LocallyConfluentAt a` and `LocallyConfluentAt b`.
They remain necessary inputs for two internal reductions in the same argument.

Independent controls check all three ciphertext fields in either E6 copy, plus
the explicit E6 key: seven locations with actual first steps and joins. They
also check E5's four locations. The three field targets are proved distinct.
`all_three_keys_required` rejects the branches with one or two updated key
occurrences and checks matching after the third update. `right_key_routes_expected`
then checks the actual synchronization sequence, E6 reduction, and final
plaintext projection to name 2. `plaintext_copy_routes_expected` fixes the
updated-plaintext endpoint after a one-copy change.
`e6_locally_confluent_nonvacuous` instantiates the constructor implication on
three independently reducible parameters, with no remaining local-confluence
premise and two distinct actual endpoints. `background_decryption_peak` checks
an E0-only key match alongside an independent nonce step, despite failed raw
root matching.

Validation: `lake build` passes (3325 jobs), including the gate, deterministic
backstop, controls and public-type/axiom audit. The final log has no warnings,
errors or `sorryAx`; reported axiom sets are subsets of `propext`,
`Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The trusted definitions are the unchanged
E5/E6 patterns, E0 constructor structure and contextual reduction. Parameter
inversion remains metatheory and grants no private-key or ciphertext observation
to public recipes.
Remaining work: proof construction, active proof checking, the AC constructor
cases and a global argument discharging the component hypotheses. Full-E
structure, accepted-ballot characterisation and privacy remain open.

## Proof construction and checking singleton investigation

Goal: discharge proof-constructor and E8/E9 checking cases in the remaining
singleton-source local-confluence obligation.
Claim (machine-checked): proof construction has only component steps.
Every checking root is a zero/one rule; a competing step in its external key,
ballot ciphertext or proof can synchronize the repeated key, nonce and bound
ciphertext and return ok. Zero/one fields have no oriented reductions, including
from E0 representatives. Constructor local confluence then follows from the
explicit component hypotheses, with no remaining root/internal premise.
Formal oracle: `ModuloStep.spk_cases`, `ModuloStep.ternary_cases`,
`ModuloStep.bitProof_parameters`, `RootModuloStep.proof_check_cases`,
`proof_check_root_inner_joined`, `locally_confluent_at_spk` and
`locally_confluent_at_checkspk`; `lake build`.
Reality oracle: source E8/E9 bind the proof to its ciphertext; the key appears
four times and the nonce three times. E0 preserves the ordered proof and checking
constructors, and zero/one constants have zero crypto weight.
Falsifier: a proof-root step, an unsynchronized copy that prevents the asserted
join, a changed vote field, or acceptance with a mismatched bound ciphertext.
Positive controls: both zero/one checking branches, changes at each key/nonce
occurrence, fixed ok endpoints and E0-equivalent field representations.
Negative controls: changing the proof's bound ciphertext breaks raw matching;
a fully matching ok/bottom-valued proof is still not an E8/E9 instance.
PBT gate: synchronized key/nonce changes from all seven reachable root-rule
families check independently expected ok outcomes for both bits, mismatched
bound-ciphertext rejection and non-bit rejection. Seeds 1, 7 and 42 pass,
configured for 500 cases at maximum size 40, with `gaveUp=0`; the deterministic
backstop passes 0–255. The false bound-ciphertext-insensitivity claim fails at
`n=0`, seed 1, zero shrinks. `mismatched_bound_ciphertext_no_match` retains the
checked counterexample. These executable fixtures do not decide general
quotient joinability.
Residual assumptions: the final constructor implications retain component local
confluence; the AC cases and global discharge remain separate obligations.

Root-matching corollary (machine-checked): if a checking source has an E8/E9 root step
to ok modulo E0, every competing single-step endpoint reduces to ok. Root/root
outputs are E0-equal; root/internal joins plus ok's irreducibility force the
common descendant to be E0-equal to ok. Thus such a matching source is locally
confluent without component-local-confluence hypotheses. This stronger result
is restricted to sources with an actual checking-root witness; malformed or
nonmatching sources still use the general constructor implication.


`BaseEq.spk_shape` and `ModuloStep.spk_cases` cover all four proof components
across E0 representatives. There is no oriented rule at proof construction's
root. `locally_confluent_at_spk` therefore requires only the four component
local-confluence hypotheses. General ternary inversion separately retains a
root-rule alternative and `TernaryArgumentStep`, which records one actual
argument step and the full target's E0 equality.

`ModuloStep.bitCiphertext_parameters` excludes any change in a constant vote
field using its proved irreducibility. `ModuloStep.bitProof_parameters` handles
changes in proof metadata or the bound ciphertext. Its conclusion is a reduction
to a synchronized proof, rather than an unjustified claim that the immediate
target already matches. The three canonical checking lemmas synchronize external
keys, ballots and proof copies and expose an actual reduction to ok. Their
zero/one premise is explicit.

`RootModuloStep.proof_check_cases` exhausts E8/E9 and retains the bit guard,
component equalities and bound-ciphertext pattern. `proof_check_root_inner_joined`
therefore joins every checking root with every argument step, with the fixed
common result ok and no local-confluence hypothesis.
`locally_confluent_at_checkspk` discharges the generic ternary root/internal
premise; its three component hypotheses remain for arbitrary nonmatching sources.
`proof_check_step_reaches_ok` proves that every single-step endpoint from a source
with an actual checking-root witness reduces to ok. Consequently,
`locally_confluent_at_matching_check` needs that root witness but no component
local-confluence hypotheses. It does not claim every checking source matches.

Independent controls enumerate all four key occurrences and all three nonce
occurrences, prove their sources and distinct target lists, and check actual
steps followed by reductions to ok for either bit. `last_bound_key_required`
checks failed matching with the final proof-bound key still old, its actual
update, and the subsequent checking rule. Both literal bits instantiate local
confluence with actual root steps. Negative controls reject a mismatched bound
ciphertext, wrong-bit proof and fully matching non-bit proof.
`background_vote_representatives` uses expanded zero in all three vote fields,
retains failed raw matching, and checks both the E0-enabled root and a competing
external key update. `arbitrary_proof_component_peak` independently exercises
reducible third and fourth fields in a general proof constructor, with two
actual steps to a fixed proof-term endpoint. It is not an E8/E9 well-formedness
claim about those arbitrary fields.

Validation: `lake build` passes (3331 jobs), including the gate, deterministic
backstop, controls and public-type/axiom audit. The final log has no warnings,
errors or `sorryAx`; reported axiom sets are subsets of `propext`,
`Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The aliases `bitCiphertext` and `bitProof`
expand to the existing source patterns. All parameter and context observations
remain metatheory and add no public access to proof or ciphertext components.
Remaining confluence work: the AC constructor analysis, especially addition's
zero/one equations and nonce composition, and a global argument discharging
all component hypotheses. Every non-AC constructor now has its component
implication, but `SingleFactorLocalConfluent V` and full confluence remain open.
Accepted-ballot characterisation, full-E structure and privacy are not implied.

## Nonce-composition factor investigation

Goal: discharge outer nonce-composition overlap analysis without adding a unit
or treating composition as ciphertext multiplication.
Claim (machine-checked): the multiset of outer composition factors, each
an exact E0 class, is complete for E0 equality. Every modulo step replaces one
such factor by its complete output bag; there is no composition-root rule.
Disjoint replacements commute, and equal selected classes reduce to the local
confluence of their shared representative. The same-factor premise remains
explicit until the global induction is supplied.
Formal oracle: `baseEq_iff_composeFactors`,
`Term.compose_subfactors_representable`, `ModuloStep.of_compose_factors`,
`ModuloStep.compose_factor`, `disjoint_compose_reductions_joined` and
`locally_confluent_at_of_compose_factors`; `lake build`.
Reality oracle: E0 gives composition AC and no unit or idempotence; E7 applies
to multiplication, not composition. Direct projection fixtures return a pair
of composed names and preserve an unrelated remainder.
Positive controls: flatten/rebuild, nonadjacent selection, repeated factors,
disjoint expanding projections, empty remainder without a sentinel, and E0
representatives inside composition factors.
Negative control: zero is not a composition unit. Ciphertext multiplication
and nonce composition must remain distinct operations.
PBT gate: executable raw composition flatten/rebuild, AC permutations, exact
multiplicity and expanding projection outputs pass seeds 1, 7 and 42, configured
for 500 cases at maximum size 40, with `gaveUp=0`. The deterministic backstop
passes 0–255. The false zero-unit property fails at `n=0`, seed 1, zero shrinks;
`zero_not_composition_unit` retains the checked E0 counterexample. This tests
representation mechanics, not a decision procedure for quotient equality.
Trusted definitions: the existing E0 quotient and composition constructor.
A local auxiliary semigroup/fold reconstructs the bag. Its instance is scoped
to reconstruction and does not replace exported quotient multiplication;
`multiplication_instance_unchanged` checks the latter definitionally. The fold
identity has no object-language term.
Residual assumptions: local confluence at selected factors, addition's special
zero/one equations and a justified global induction remain open.


`Term.composeFactors` flattens only outer nonce composition and retains exact
E0 classes. `BaseEq.compose_factors` proves invariance, including E0 changes
inside factors and addition equations occurring there. A local commutative
semigroup uses composition on the existing quotient, and a private `WithOne`
fold reconstructs the source class. `baseEq_iff_composeFactors` gives both
directions; `Term.composeFactors_nonempty` excludes the auxiliary identity as
an actual term. Every nonempty subbag has a term representative.

`ModuloStep.of_compose_factors` and `JoinModulo.of_compose_factors` lift specified
steps and joins through arbitrary remainders. `ComposeFactorStep` retains the
selected singleton representative, its actual step and its complete output bag.
`RewriteStep.compose_factor` covers every rule and context: composition contexts
extend the remainder, while other contexts form one composition factor. Every
root-rule source is a singleton composition factor, including E7's multiplication
source. `ModuloStep.compose_factor` transports this result through E0 changes.
There is no additional composition-root case.

`disjoint_compose_reductions_joined` commutes disjoint replacements, including
expanding outputs. `compose_factor_peaks_joined` classifies equal versus disjoint
selected classes using the checked singleton-selection theorem. The equal case
uses the explicit `ComposeFactorsLocallyConfluent source` premise.
`locally_confluent_at_of_compose_factors` covers all source peaks under that
premise. `compose_factors_local_of_representatives` supplies a representative
interface, and `irreducible_of_compose_factors` handles families of irreducible
factors. Neither assumes local confluence of arbitrary factors globally.

Independent controls retain two expanding projections, an unrelated name and
both exact second steps to a five-factor endpoint. They cover empty remainders
without a sentinel, E0 changes inside a selected factor, repeated factors and
the absence of a zero unit. E7 matches a multiplication of ciphertexts but not
their composition; a multiplication step inside a composition context is checked
as one factor replacement and preserves the outer factor count. The exported
multiplication instance still unfolds to multiplication after importing the
composition proof. `composition_source_locally_confluent` instantiates the
factor premise on independently locally confluent projections, with distinct
actual first-step endpoints. Its composed-name base cases are proved irreducible.

Validation: `lake build` passes (3336 jobs), including campaigns, controls and
the public-type/axiom audit. The final log has no warnings, errors or `sorryAx`;
reported axiom sets are subsets of `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.
The composition bag and fold remain metatheory and add no public operation.
Remaining work: addition's zero/one factor analysis and a global argument
discharging the component and factor-local hypotheses. Crypto weight alone
does not justify every factor descent. Full confluence, full-E structure,
accepted-ballot characterisation and privacy remain open.

## Addition summary investigation

Goal: represent E0 addition without inventing a global zero identity, erasing
non-numeric occurrences or saturating repeated ones.
Claim (machine-checked): an addition term is completely represented modulo
E0 by a multiset of non-numeric outer factors and an optional natural-number
numeric part. `none` means no numeric summand; `some 0` means an actual zero
summand; `some n` for positive n counts ones. Combining present numeric parts
adds their counts, while absence is only a bookkeeping identity. Exact E0
classes represent all other factors. Equal summaries of actual terms are
equivalent to E0 equality.
Formal oracle: `BaseEq.add_summary`, `baseEq_iff_addSummary`,
`Term.addSummary_ne_empty` and `add_summary_representable`; reproduce with
`lake build` and the public-type/axiom checks in `Symbolic/Audit.lean`.
Reality oracle: E0's AC addition, zero+zero=zero and zero+one=one. There is no
zero+arbitrary-term identity, no one+one=one equation and no modulo tally arithmetic.
Falsifier: loss of numeric presence, loss of a repeated one/non-numeric factor,
or two actual terms with equal summaries but different E0 classes.
Positive controls: repeated zero, repeated one, mixed zero/one, an unrelated
non-numeric factor retained alongside zero, and independent flat-token counts.
Negative controls: zero as a global identity and positive counts saturated to one.
PBT gate: arbitrary abstract summaries and reachable flat zero/one/atom token
lists, checking associative/commutative combination, bookkeeping empty cases,
independent numeric presence/count and exact atom multiplicity. Seeds 1, 7 and
42, configured for 500 cases at maximum size 40, plus inputs 0–255.
Trusted definitions: optional numeric counts and exact E0 factor classes. A
private reconstruction fold may adjoin a bookkeeping identity; no term denotes it.
Residual assumptions: summary completeness does not yet classify addition steps,
join them or discharge the global component/factor local-confluence hypotheses.

The gate passed before the general reconstruction proof: seeds 1, 7 and 42,
configured for 500 cases at maximum size 40, all report `gaveUp=0`; inputs 0–255
pass the deterministic backstop. Both deliberately false properties fail at
`n=0`, seed 1, with zero shrinks. These finite algebra and token-list checks do
not decide quotient equality. `AdditionSummarySPOT.lean` retains both failures
as checked E0 counterexamples, alongside literal numeric, multiplicity, mixed
summand, nested representative and exported-multiplication controls.

`addNumerals_combine` reconstructs present numeric counts using only E0.
`baseEq_iff_addSummary` proves both directions for actual terms via a private
quotient fold. Its auxiliary identity has no term representative. The locally
scoped addition semigroup leaves exported quotient multiplication unchanged.
`Term.add_atom_representable` produces valid non-numeric representatives of
atoms occurring in an actual summary. `add_summary_representable` requires
nonemptiness and valid atom representatives; it does not assert that every
abstract summary is valid. `Term.add_subsummary_representable` supplies these
representatives from an atom submultiset of an actual term; any optional numeric
count is allowed because numeric representatives exist independently.

Intermediate failures were proof engineering: omitted phantom type annotations,
fold accumulator inference, indentation, and a private helper name shadowed by
its public theorem. No candidate equation was weakened. The final `lake build`
passes (3342 jobs), including controls, campaigns and 445 axiom reports. Reported
axioms are only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`; the final log has
no warnings, errors or `sorryAx`. Summary observations remain metatheory and do
not extend public recipes. Addition-step classification, replacement joins and
the global confluence argument remain open.

## Addition replacement investigation

Goal: classify every modulo step as reduction of one non-numeric outer addition
factor and join disjoint replacements, then reduce same-factor peaks to an
explicit local-confluence premise.
Claim (machine-checked): addition has no root rewrite. Every step selects
one atom occurrence, replaces it by the complete output summary and retains a
remainder. Selecting the same atom class forces equal remainders; selecting
different classes exposes a common remainder. Only atom cancellation is claimed:
numeric combination itself is not cancellative because zero+one=one.
Formal oracle: `ModuloStep.add_factor`, `AddSummary.atom_selection_cases`,
`disjoint_add_reductions_joined` and `locally_confluent_at_of_add_summaries`;
reproduce with `lake build` and the public-type/axiom audit.
Falsifier: a reachable step losing numeric presence or multiplicity, a disjoint
replacement diamond failing to commute, or an invalid numeric cancellation.
Reality oracle: the seven source-oriented rules have no addition root; E0 has
AC addition and the two specific zero/one equations. Independent controls use
projections returning one and zero, with a retained name and zero remainder.
PBT gate: generated atom selections, arbitrary output summaries and retained
numeric presence; seeds 1, 7, 42, configured 500 cases at size 40 and inputs
0–255. A false numeric-cancellation claim must fail before the general proof.
Trusted definitions: existing E0, contexts, modulo steps and addition summaries.
Residual assumptions: same-factor joins require factor local confluence. This
increment does not supply the global induction or a protocol privacy theorem.

The replacement gate passed before the general step and join proofs. Seeds
1, 7 and 42, configured for 500 cases at maximum size 40, report success with
`gaveUp=0`; 256 deterministic inputs pass. The false numeric-cancellation
control fails at n=0, seed 1, with zero shrinks. Its checked counterpart
`AddSummary.numeric_cancellation_refuted` explicitly retains equal combined
numeric parts and different inputs. The gate checks abstract summary mechanics,
not a decision procedure for E0 or coverage of arbitrary protocol executions.

`ModuloStep.of_add_summaries` and `JoinModulo.of_add_summaries` lift an actual
step or join through a specified remainder. Nonempty remainders are reconstructed
from valid atoms in the endpoint summary; empty remainders require no unit term.
`AddFactorStep` retains the selected non-numeric representative, actual step,
complete output summary and remainder. `RewriteStep.add_factor` exhausts all
rules and contexts; `ModuloStep.add_factor` transports the classification through
E0. Numeric fields cannot supply a rewrite root.

`AddSummary.atom_selection_cases` derives the two cases from multiset selection
and equality of numeric remainder fields. `disjoint_add_reductions_joined`
commutes replacements with arbitrary output summaries. Same-class peaks use
`AddFactorsLocallyConfluent source`; `add_factor_peaks_joined` and
`locally_confluent_at_of_add_summaries` retain that premise. The representative
interface does not establish it globally. `irreducible_of_add_atoms_empty` and
`addNumeral_irreducible` prove irreducibility for summaries with no non-numeric
atoms, including every numeric representative.

`AdditionReplacementSPOT.lean` supplies two independent projections returning
one and zero, a retained name and a zero remainder. It proves both actual first
steps, both second steps to the fixed expected one+name term, distinct branches,
and the intermediate numeric presence/counts. The expected term cannot erase
the name. Additional controls cover an empty remainder, output expansion to two
atoms with retained zero, and an E0-expanded zero inside a selected projection.
The same source instantiates the factor-local premise using independently
locally confluent projection factors, proving a nontrivial actual instance.

An intermediate failure was proof engineering: numeric field projections needed
explicit simplification to avoid elaboration choosing an unintended equality.
No candidate was weakened. `lake build` passes (3347 jobs), including all gates,
controls and 470 axiom reports. Reported axiom sets contain only `propext`,
`Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`; the final log has no warnings, errors or
`sorryAx`. All non-AC component implications and all three AC factor analyses
are now available. The global argument discharging their hypotheses remains
open; equal crypto weight for a product and factor still rules out that simple
induction. Full confluence, full-E structure and privacy remain open.

## Global local-confluence investigation

Goal: discharge all component and factor-local premises, then apply checked
termination to establish confluence modulo E0.
Claim (machine-checked): structural induction simultaneously proves
local confluence of a term and existence of locally confluent representatives
for all its multiplication factors, composition factors and non-numeric
addition atoms. At an AC constructor, factor representatives come from the
children's induction hypotheses. At other constructors each relevant factor
collection is a singleton containing the newly proved term. Numeric constants
have no addition atoms. E0 transport supplies arbitrary representatives of each
class; it does not require induction on those representatives.
Formal oracle: `locally_confluent_at`, `local_confluence_modulo`,
`confluence_modulo`, `normal_forms_unique_modulo`, `eqE_iff_join` and
`irreducible_eqE_iff_base` in `GlobalConfluence.lean`.
Falsifier: an AC factor class lacking an inherited child representative, a
constructor implication requiring an undisclosed global premise, or a modulo
peak that cannot join. Smallest adverse cases include multiplication by zero,
addition numeric absorption and alternating AC constructors.
Reality oracle: existing exhaustive rule/context analyses and source E0/rule
schemas; independent mixed-constructor and E0-only decryption controls.
PBT gate: raw representative inheritance and strict raw child containment for
generated AC nodes, including alternating constructors and numeric omission;
seeds 1, 7, 42 with 500 configured cases at size 40 and inputs 0–255. The false
strict crypto-weight descent claim must fail. This mechanics gate does not
itself test arbitrary modulo confluence.
Trusted definitions: the existing symbolic relations and factor observations.
Residual scope: confluence of this symbolic model does not establish full-E
constructor restrictions, nonce non-deducibility or ballot secrecy by itself.

The mechanics gate passed before the general proof. Seeds 1, 7 and 42,
configured for 500 cases at maximum size 40, report success with `gaveUp=0`;
256 deterministic inputs pass. The false strict crypto-weight descent claim
fails at n=0, seed 1, zero shrinks, and `factor_weight_not_strict` retains the
failure for every name. These tests check raw representative inheritance and
containment, not the unbounded local-confluence statement.

The private simultaneous predicate contains four propositions: local confluence
of the current term, and locally confluent representative existence for each
of its three factor collections. At multiplication, inherited representatives
supply `FactorsLocallyConfluent`; the exhaustive outer-fusion analysis handles
all other peaks. Composition and addition use their checked factor analyses.
Other constructors use their component implications and then supply the term
itself as the singleton representative. Zero and one have no addition atoms.
E0 transport handles every representative of a selected class. The proof uses
ordinary structural induction on the raw input term, never a strict crypto-weight
comparison with a factor and never recursive calls on arbitrary representatives.

`local_confluence_modulo` has no local-confluence premise.
`single_factor_local_confluence` closes the earlier equivalent obligation.
`confluence_modulo` applies the existing termination argument;
`normal_forms_unique_modulo` retains only the actual reduction and irreducibility
hypotheses. `eqE_iff_join` characterizes full E equality by common reduction, and
`irreducible_eqE_iff_base` characterizes equality of irreducible endpoints.
These are relational theorems; no executable E0 matcher or equality decision
procedure is claimed.

`GlobalConfluenceSPOT.lean` applies the theorem to a concrete peak spanning
multiplication, composition and addition. One branch uses the retained E0-only
decryption match and the other a projection. It checks distinct first-step
endpoints and both second steps to an independently specified common term with
its zero remainder intact. Raw normalization still misses the E0-only match.
Full E does not equate distinct names or zero and one, checked using the new
irreducible equality theorem. These controls exclude universal equality and a
raw-normalization substitution for the modulo relation.

Intermediate failures were proof engineering: a reserved field identifier and
`decide` on a statement with a free name parameter. The corrected weight control
is definitional equality. No theorem hypothesis was added to close the proof.
Validation: `lake build` passes (3350 jobs), including all campaigns, controls
and 484 public axiom reports. All reported axiom sets are subsets of `propext`,
`Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`; the final log has no warnings, errors or
`sorryAx`. No cryptographic axiom, signature change or public recipe was added.
The next work is the full-E structural and non-deducibility analysis required by
Lemma 9, followed by the remaining frames/process/privacy obligations.

## Full-E constructor structure investigation

Goal: establish the constructor equalities used to compare accepted ciphertexts
and proof terms in Appendix B.3, Lemma 9 (source pp. 45–46), and the ciphertext
component comparison in Lemma 11 (p. 48).
Claim (machine-checked): full E equality between two penc constructors
is equivalent to full E equality of their three ordered components; likewise
for the four spk components and the two components of pairing/partial-decryption
construction. Ciphertexts and proof constructions cannot be full-E equal.
The inputs need not be irreducible: reductions preserve these passive outer
constructors and reduce their components. Confluence then supplies a common
reduct whose E0 constructor decomposition compares corresponding components.
Formal oracle: `ReducesModulo.penc_components`, `.spk_components`,
`.passive_binary_components` in `PassiveReduction.lean` and the public
`EqE.*_iff`, separation and irreducible-shape theorems in `FullStructure.lean`.
Falsifier: an oriented path losing one of these outer constructors, or E-equal
passive constructors with unequal corresponding components. General head
preservation for all symbols is deliberately false: decryption can return a name.
Reality oracle: E1–E9 have no roots at penc, spk, pair or partialDecrypt;
Lemma 9 uses their structure, whereas dec and projections are active destructors.
