PBT gate: bottom-up raw reductions of generated components under these passive
constructors, compared with separately normalized components; seeds 1, 7, 42,
500 configured cases at size 40, inputs 0–255. The false universal head-preserving
claim must fail on decryption before general proofs. Raw tests are a limited
semantics check, not a full-E equality oracle.
Residual scope: no arbitrary raw-head inversion under full E, no minimal-recipe
or nonce non-deducibility theorem, and no accepted-ballot/privacy theorem yet.

The structural claim also includes the following normal-form corollary: if an
irreducible term is E-equal to a ciphertext or proof construction, it has that
literal constructor with E-equal components. Irreducibility is load-bearing;
the decryption head-change control rules out dropping it.

The gate passed before the general proofs. Seeds 1, 7 and 42, configured for
500 cases at maximum size 40, report success with `gaveUp=0`; the deterministic
backstop passes all 256 inputs. The false universal head-preservation property
fails at n=0, seed 1, with zero shrinks. This gate checks raw passive-constructor
semantics only; the general path and confluence proofs cover arbitrary E0
representatives and full E equality.

`PassiveReduction.lean` inducts over arbitrary modulo paths, retaining an E0
relation to the passive constructor and actual reduction paths for every
ordered component. The zero-step case retains its E0 endpoint change.
`FullStructure.lean` applies `eqE_iff_join` to obtain a common reduct, decomposes
both paths and compares the resulting components using E0 constructor
injectivity. `EqE.penc_iff`, `EqE.spk_iff`, `EqE.pair_iff` and
`EqE.partialDecrypt_iff` have no irreducibility or recipe premise.
`EqE.passive_binary_iff` also compares the binary symbol. Ciphertexts, proof
constructions and the two passive binary forms are separated as stated by
`penc_not_eqE_spk`, `penc_not_eqE_passive_binary` and
`spk_not_eqE_passive_binary`. `EqE.name_iff` retains exact name identity.
The two irreducible-shape corollaries require an irreducible target and return
literal constructor shape with E-equal components.

`FullStructureSPOT.lean` checks ciphertext equality with reducible key/message
components and a commuted nonce, while ruling out E0 equality of those same
inputs. It tracks two actual component steps and an E0 endpoint change.
Changing the resulting message fails; changing the proof's fourth binding
component fails. Pair and partial-decryption argument order remains significant.
The normal-form shape corollary has a literal irreducible positive fixture.
A projection returning a ciphertext gives an E-equal reducible target with the
wrong literal constructor, proving the irreducibility premise cannot be dropped.
Decryption returning a name separately refutes universal head preservation.

One intermediate failure was proof engineering: a stand-alone step fixture
needed an explicit variable type annotation. No constructor or equality claim
was weakened. Validation: `lake build` passes (3354 jobs), including all controls,
campaigns and 511 public axiom reports. All reported axiom sets are subsets of
`propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`; no warnings, errors or `sorryAx`
appear. These structural observations are metatheory and grant recipes no access
to ciphertext nonces or proof fields. Public-key/remaining projection structure,
nonce non-deducibility, minimal-recipe reasoning, Lemma 9 and privacy remain open.

## Public-key and projection paths investigation

Goal: extend the full-E structure needed by the minimal-recipe argument without
confusing public-key injectivity with extraction of its argument.
Claim (machine-checked): public-key paths preserve a reduced argument and
full E equality of public keys is argument equality. Projection paths either
retain the projection head while reducing its argument, or reduce that argument
to a pair and continue reducing the selected member. Thus a projection E-equal
to a ciphertext must have an argument reducible to a pair; this is not a claim
that the original argument has literal pair shape.
Formal oracle: `ReducesModulo.pk_components`, `EqE.pk_iff`,
`ReducesModulo.projection_cases` and `EqE.projection_penc_inversion` in
`ProjectionPaths.lean`.
Falsifier: a pk path changing its outer constructor, a projection path outside
the two cases, or a nested projection wrongly forced to have an initial pair.
Reality oracle: E1/E2 select ordered pair members; no rule removes pk at its root.
The source's minimal-recipe argument in Appendix B.3 distinguishes reducible
arguments and projections of public handles; this increment does not prove that
recipe-minimality assertion.
PBT gate: generated component reductions under pk and projections with a pair
revealed by another projection, plus stuck name arguments. Seeds 1, 7, 42,
500 configured cases at size 40, inputs 0–255. A false initial-pair-shape claim
must fail before the general proof.
Residual assumptions: no public key inversion recipe, no nonce non-deducibility,
no minimal-recipe substitution classification or accepted-ballot theorem.

The gate passed before the general path proof: seeds 1, 7 and 42, configured
for 500 cases at maximum size 40, report success with `gaveUp=0`; 256
deterministic inputs pass. The false initial-pair-shape claim fails at n=0,
seed 1, zero shrinks. Its witness has a pair revealed by an inner projection,
and the permanent SPOT checks the actual reduction and the absent initial shape.
A harness elaboration failure required expressing the negative property through
a Boolean shape test; this did not change the candidate theorem or its falsifier.

`ReducesModulo.pk_components` tracks the public-key argument through arbitrary
modulo paths. `EqE.pk_iff` uses confluence to prove injectivity on arbitrary
inputs; it does not produce a public recipe for the argument.
`EqE.pk_irreducible_shape` requires an irreducible target and returns a literal
pk constructor with an E-equal argument. `pk_not_eqE_penc` separates public keys
from ciphertexts without an irreducibility premise.

`ReducesModulo.projection_cases` exhausts paths from fst/snd. Either the path
retains the unary constructor with an argument path and E0 endpoint, or the
argument reduces to an actual pair and the selected member reduces to the
endpoint. The latter exposes both actual reduction paths, not just existence
of a pair with unrelated components. The alternatives need not be disjoint.
`EqE.projection_penc_inversion` uses confluence and ciphertext path preservation
to rule out the retained-head case for an E-equal ciphertext result. It returns
the argument's pair-producing path and E equality of the selected member.
No claim forces an initial literal pair or a projection of a public handle.

`ProjectionPathSPOT.lean` checks public-key equality on a reducible input where
E0 equality fails, unequal named keys, key/ciphertext separation, and a normal
public-key shape instance. Both fst and snd follow a pair revealed by an inner
projection to independently specified outputs. The ciphertext branch
instantiates the general inversion theorem. A name argument cannot produce that
ciphertext, and a zero-step stuck projection exercises the retained-head case.

Validation: `lake build` passes (3357 jobs), including all campaigns, controls
and 527 axiom reports. Reported axiom sets contain only `propext`,
`Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`; no warnings, errors or `sorryAx` appear.
These observations remain metatheory. Nonce non-deducibility and the
minimal-recipe/substitution classification needed by Lemma 9 are still open.

## Protected-name non-deducibility investigation

Goal: prove that public recipes cannot deduce a restricted nonce exposed only
in ciphertext randomness, proof construction or public-key arguments.
Claim (machine-checked): a syntactic protection invariant allows arbitrary
contents under pk and spk, and ignores only the randomness argument of penc;
it checks both remaining ciphertext arguments and all arguments of other
constructors. E0 preserves this invariant and oriented contextual reductions
preserve it forward. If all frame values satisfy it, every public recipe result
satisfies it. Confluence and irreducibility of names then exclude full-E equality
with a protected name.
The invariant is not claimed invariant under full E: reversing a projection can
introduce an unprotected name in a discarded field. Nor may ciphertext plaintext
be ignored; decryption with a public key argument would expose such a name.
Formal oracle: `BaseEq.nonce_safe`, `ReducesModulo.nonce_safe`,
`Term.nonce_safe_subst`, `nonce_safe_not_eqE_name` and
`Frame.nonce_not_deducible` in `NonceNonDeducibility.lean`.
Falsifier: a safe source reducing to an unsafe result, a safe frame/public recipe
that deduces a protected name, or accidental protection of plaintext positions.
Reality oracle: E5/E6 return plaintext, E7 combines nonce and plaintext separately,
E8/E9 return ok, and there are no pk/spk-field or ciphertext-randomness destructors.
Positive controls: public key, encrypted bit, proof, projection of a published
ballot and known-key decryption of an encrypted public bit.
Negative controls: protected-name plaintext leakage and reversed projection
introducing an exposed restricted name. Seeds 1, 7, 42, 500 configured cases at
size 40, inputs 0–255; general proofs follow the executable gate.
Residual scope: only frames satisfying the explicit invariant; no blanket frame
secrecy, composed-nonce exclusion, minimal-recipe classification or privacy proof.

The executable gate passed before the general proofs. Seeds 1, 7 and 42,
configured for 500 cases at maximum size 40, report success with `gaveUp=0`;
256 deterministic inputs pass. Both false properties fail at n=0, seed 1,
zero shrinks. The plaintext fixture actually decrypts to the protected name;
the reversed-projection fixture is E-equal to one while exposing the name in a
discarded field. The SPOT retains both as kernel-checked counterexamples.

`Term.nonceSafe` checks name occurrences except beneath pk/spk and in the
randomness position of penc. It still checks ciphertext keys and plaintext,
all binary arguments and checkspk arguments. `BaseEq.nonce_safe` preserves the
Boolean exactly. `RootStep.nonce_safe`, `RewriteStep.nonce_safe`,
`ModuloStep.nonce_safe` and `ReducesModulo.nonce_safe` preserve truth forward.
The context proof covers every signature position, including ignored positions.
`Term.Public.nonce_safe` and `Term.nonce_safe_subst` show that arbitrary public
recipe substitution over protected handles preserves the invariant.

`nonce_safe_not_eqE_name` uses the already checked full-E join characterization.
A common reduct of a protected term and a restricted name is protected, while
irreducibility of the name forces E0 equality with that same name, contradicting
its membership in the protected set. This proof does not transport protection
backwards through arbitrary E equations. `Frame.nonce_not_deducible` quantifies
over all public recipes and retains the per-handle protection and name-membership
premises explicitly. It is a logical non-deducibility theorem for that frame
family, not a bounded search result or a secrecy claim about arbitrary frames.

`NonceProtectionSPOT.lean` exposes a public key, encrypted bit, proof, and a
one-candidate tuple simultaneously. Its quantified theorem excludes the nonce
for every public recipe. Independent controls actually project the ciphertext
from the tuple and decrypt the public bit with its known key. Removing the frame
invariant lets a handle reveal the name; removing the public-recipe restriction
lets a recipe name it directly. The ciphertext-plaintext and reverse-E controls
retain the intended abstraction limits.

Validation: `lake build` passes (3361 jobs), including campaigns, controls and
545 public axiom reports. All reported axiom sets are subsets of `propext`,
`Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`; the final log has no warnings, errors or
`sorryAx`. No symbolic equation, public recipe operation or protocol observation
was changed. The individual-name result still needs extension to composed nonce
terms containing restricted factors, plus application to the parametrized
historical frames and the minimal-recipe proof for Lemma 9.

## Composed-nonce exclusion investigation

Goal: exclude public deduction of nonce compositions containing any restricted
name factor, as required by Appendix B.3's r ◦ R arguments.
Claim (machine-checked): every modulo reduction preserves membership of
an individual name's E0 class among outer composition factors. A selected factor
E0-equal to a name cannot reduce, so the name remains in the remainder; other
factor reductions may expand or contract. Protected terms cannot have restricted
name classes among these factors. Confluence then excludes E equality between
a public recipe over a protected frame and any such composed-nonce target.
Formal oracle: `ModuloStep.compose_name_mem`, `ReducesModulo.compose_name_mem`,
`nonce_safe_not_eqE_name_factor`, `Frame.composed_nonce_not_deducible` and
`Frame.nonce_with_remainder_not_deducible` in `ComposedNonce.lean`.
Falsifier: a step removing an outer composition name factor, or a protected term
with a restricted name factor. Arbitrary syntactic occurrence preservation is
false: a projection may discard a name in an unselected pair component.
Reality oracle: E0 composition is AC with no unit, and none of the seven rules
has a composition root. The rules can discard components under other heads.
PBT gate: generated raw composition terms with repeated name factors and
reducible other factors; normalization preserves those occurrences. Seeds
1, 7, 42, 500 configured cases at size 40 and inputs 0–255; first refute
unrestricted syntactic occurrence preservation on a discarded pair member.
Residual scope: protected-frame premise remains explicit. This does not yet
instantiate every historical frame or prove the minimal-recipe classification.

The gate passed before the general proof. Seeds 1, 7 and 42, configured for
500 cases at maximum size 40, report success with `gaveUp=0`; all 256
deterministic inputs pass. The false arbitrary-occurrence property fails at
n=0, seed 1, zero shrinks. The executable gate additionally checks nondecreasing
raw counts of repeated name factors; the general theorem claims persistence of
membership, not a general multiplicity inequality.

`ModuloStep.compose_name_mem` uses exhaustive composition-step classification.
If the name class were the selected factor, name irreducibility transported
through E0 would contradict the actual factor step. Otherwise its occurrence
is retained in the remainder. `ReducesModulo.compose_name_mem` includes arbitrary
paths and E0-only endpoint changes. `Term.nonce_safe_no_name_factor` shows that
a protected term cannot have a restricted name class among its outer composition
factors. It handles opaque singleton factors using E0 protection preservation,
and composition nodes by their two protected children.

`nonce_safe_not_eqE_name_factor` transports both properties to a common reduct
using confluence, obtaining a contradiction. `Frame.composed_nonce_not_deducible`
quantifies over all public recipes, with explicit handle protection, restricted
name membership and target factor membership. The target need not be irreducible.
`Frame.nonce_with_remainder_not_deducible` specializes this result to name ◦ rest
for an arbitrary ground remainder. This also covers repeated factors and AC
representatives through the exact E0 factor observation.

Controls instantiate the published key/ciphertext/proof/tuple frame for every
public recipe and arbitrary remainder. A permuted target contains two copies
of the restricted name. A distinct target has a projection factor expanding
from one to two factors; an actual step and factor cards three/four are checked,
and the nonce still occurs afterwards. Non-deducibility applies to this
explicitly reducible target. The public ciphertext remains derivable even though
its randomness contains the restricted name: that name is not an exposed outer
composition factor. A projection discarding a restricted-name pair member
refutes extending persistence to arbitrary syntactic occurrences.

Intermediate failures were fixture elaboration: implicit name/set parameters
needed annotations, and an opened fixture name was shadowed by an existing
cipher function. No general theorem premise was weakened. Validation:
`lake build` passes (3364 jobs), including campaigns, controls and 558 axiom
reports. All reported axiom sets are subsets of `propext`, `Classical.choice`
and `Quot.sound`; no warnings, errors or `sorryAx` appear. Parametrized historical
frame instantiation and the minimal-recipe proof remain open, as do Lemma 9 and
protocol privacy. No public operation or symbolic equation was added.

## Parametrized historical-frame investigation

Goal: instantiate individual-name and composed-nonce non-deducibility for the
two honest ballots and public-key handle of Appendix B.3, Lemmas 9–10.
Claim (machine-checked): the source-shaped frame is protected for every
positive candidate count and either swapped one-hot vote assignment. Each ballot
contains candidate ciphertexts, their proofs and one aggregate proof in that
order, with nonempty folds for nonce composition, vote addition and ciphertext
multiplication. The restriction set includes the secret key, auxiliary name and
all nonce names. Every public recipe then fails to deduce any restricted name
or a composition containing one of the voter/candidate nonce factors.
Formal oracle: `Historical.frame_protected`,
`Historical.frame_restricted_name_not_deducible`,
`Historical.frame_secret_key_not_deducible`,
`Historical.frame_nonce_composition_not_deducible` and
`Historical.frame_nonce_composition_of_nonce_public`. Definitions use arbitrary name assignments; a separate
freshness predicate records the historical distinctness requirement. Protection
is stronger than needed and does not require freshness, so no name-freshness
assumption is silently used in its proof.
Falsifier: wrong field order/count, empty-fold identity, wrong swap assignment,
plaintext field containing a restricted name, or an unprotected frame handle.
Reality oracle: Appendix B.2.1 ciph/spk/aggregate/ballot formulas, B.3's three
handles and restricted set; tuple encoding uses the documented tail correction.
PBT gate: candidate counts 1–5, both swaps, independent one-hot bit counts and
field/projection fixtures; seeds 1, 7, 42, 500 configured cases at size 40 plus
inputs 0–255. A deliberately missing aggregate field must fail.
Residual scope: protection and non-deducibility only. General ballot-proof
validity, static equivalence and minimal-recipe classification are not claimed.

Scope refinement before integration: Lemma 9 explicitly requires recipes to be
free of the honest nonce names, while Lemma 10's frame also restricts the secret
key and auxiliary name. Retain both interfaces. The data protection proof can
hold for any protected-name set because all published plaintexts are constants.
Specialize composed-nonce exclusion to recipes public only with respect to the
nonce set, so the instantiation does not silently strengthen Lemma 9's premise.
A control should admit the literal secret-key name under the nonce-only policy
while rejecting it under the full frame policy.

The gate passed before the general protection proof. Candidate counts 1–5 and
both swaps are generated. Seeds 1, 7 and 42, configured for 500 cases at maximum
size 40, report success with `gaveUp=0`; all 256 deterministic inputs pass.
Independent checks count exactly one selected bit, compare ciphertext projections
with the expected component, check the three-handle mapping and reverse the
assignment between worlds. The missing-aggregate-field property fails at n=0,
seed 1, zero shrinks, and a general checked field-count inequality retains it.

`HistoricalFrames.lean` defines two voter indices, n+1 candidate indices, the
name assignment and separate `Names.Fresh` predicate, nonce-only and full
restriction sets, nonempty left-associated folds, candidate ciphertexts,
component proofs, aggregate proof and ordered tuple. Handles 0/1/2 expose the
public key and the two ballots. The Boolean swap exchanges the selected candidate
indices while preserving all names. This is the initial three-handle frame;
final partial-decryption frames and adaptive board extensions are not introduced.

`HistoricalFrameProtection.lean` proves field count and the corrected tail guard,
then proves protection of each ciphertext, field list, tuple and frame. Protection
holds for any protected-name set because published plaintexts are bit constants
and all names occur in protected positions. The full restriction interface
excludes every restricted name, including the secret key, and nonce compositions.
The nonce-only interface uses `r.Public ns.nonceNames`, matching Lemma 9's
explicit nonce-freedom condition even when a recipe names the key or auxiliary
name. All claims quantify over arbitrary positive candidate counts, both swaps,
all public recipes and arbitrary nonce remainders. Name freshness is recorded
but is not needed by these protection proofs; no freshness premise is inferred
from the unvalidated data constructor.

Literal two-candidate controls check all five fields, including the exact nonce,
vote and ciphertext aggregate expressions. The name fixture is checked fresh;
left/right values exchange votes and remain syntactically distinct. Public key
and ciphertext-projection recipes work. The non-deducibility theorem is
instantiated in both worlds. The nonce-only policy admits a literal key name
that the full frame policy forbids, and still excludes the nonce composition.
The one-candidate boundary is definitionally the earlier ballot and inherits
its checked corrected acceptance. General `ProofValid`/`Accepted` for n+1
candidates is not claimed by these protection results.

Intermediate failures were proof engineering: a missing finite-set import,
list-membership decomposition and unfolding decidable fixture predicates.
The restriction-interface refinement removes an accidental strengthening of
the intended Lemma 9 premise; it does not weaken non-deducibility. Validation:
`lake build` passes (3368 jobs), including all campaigns, controls and 584 axiom
reports. Reported axiom sets contain only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and
`Quot.sound`; no warnings, errors or `sorryAx` appear. Minimal-recipe structure,
general honest-ballot proof validity, Lemma 9 and static equivalence remain open.

## General honest-ballot validity investigation

Goal: prove the parametrized historical ballot's component and aggregate proof
checks, and corrected acceptance on an empty board, for every positive candidate
count and selected candidate.
Claim (machine-checked): the nonempty ciphertext product is E-equal to an
encryption under the same key of the nonce-composition fold and vote-addition
fold. The one-hot vote fold is E0-equal to one. Tuple projections select every
component/proof/aggregate field; E8/E9 then validate the bound proof terms.
Formal oracle: `Historical.foldCandidates_ciphertexts`, `Historical.vote_sum_one`,
`Historical.honest_proofs_valid`, `Historical.honest_empty_board_accepts` and
`Historical.honest_accepts_after_other`.
Falsifier: wrong fold order, aggregate key/nonce/plaintext disagreement, an
incorrect field offset, or a multi-one vote sum collapsing to one. Empty-board
acceptance must not imply acceptance after replay on a nonempty board.
Reality oracle: source E7–E9, one-hot candidate substitutions and field order;
the tuple tail uses the previously authorized correction.
PBT gate: counts 1–5 and all selected positions, comparing raw E7 folding with
independently assembled aggregate components and numeric one-hot counts, plus
proof field projections. Seeds 1, 7, 42, 500 configured cases at size 40 and
inputs 0–255. A two-selected-vote numeric normalization must be rejected.
Residual scope: honest ballots only; not the accepted-adversarial-ballot
characterization, static equivalence or minimal-recipe theorem.

Additional candidate corollary: under `Names.Fresh`, the ballot of one honest
voter is accepted after the other voter's ballot, for arbitrary selected
candidates. Full-E ciphertext injectivity and nonce-name injectivity discharge
component weeding. The freshness premise is necessary for this corollary;
a repeated ballot or colliding-name fixture must remain rejected. This extends
the acceptance result without asserting acceptance on arbitrary boards.

The executable gate passed before the general proofs. It covers candidate counts
1–5 and every selected position in each generated count, comparing the raw E7
fold with separately assembled nonce and vote folds and all proof-field offsets.
Seeds 1, 7 and 42, configured for 500 cases at maximum size 40, report success
with `gaveUp=0`; all 256 deterministic inputs pass. The two-one collapse property
fails at n=0, seed 1, zero shrinks; a checked full-E counterexample retains it.
The raw gate does not implement E0 normalization of the vote sum.

`HistoricalAggregation.lean` proves homomorphic folding for arbitrary term
components under one key. A separate numeric-summary induction counts occurrences
of the selected candidate in the nonempty vote fold. Each candidate appears once
in `List.finRange`, so `vote_sum_one` establishes E0 equality with one. It does
not invoke a global zero identity or a saturating one+one equation.
`ciphertext_product` combines the fold and sum results.

`HistoricalValidity.lean` proves each ciphertext, component-proof and aggregate
projection at its actual tuple offset. `ballot_aggregate_ciphertext` relates the
board's product of projections to the constructor's ciphertext fold.
`honest_proofs_valid` aligns the aggregate proof's key, nonce, sum and bound
ciphertext with E9 and selects E8/E9 for each zero/one component.
`honest_empty_board_accepts` adds the checked corrected tail guard and vacuous
empty-board weeding. `fresh_voters_no_reuse` uses full-E ciphertext injectivity,
name equality and `Names.Fresh` to reject every cross-voter component collision.
`honest_accepts_after_other` therefore accepts the second honest ballot after
the first, retaining freshness and different-voter hypotheses explicitly.

Controls apply acceptance to both selected positions in a two-candidate election
and both swapped worlds for the second voter. They preserve replay rejection
and rejection when distinct voter indices reuse colliding nonce assignments.
The first and last positions in a three-candidate sum reduce to one, and an
aggregate ciphertext has the independently specified key, nonce composition and
one plaintext. A full-E proof confirms that two ones remain distinct from one.
No acceptance claim is made for an arbitrary board.

Intermediate issues were proof engineering: an unused simplification lemma and
an over-expanded literal collision fixture. The latter is checked directly by
decidable term equality. Validation: `lake build` passes (3372 jobs), including
all campaigns, controls and 603 axiom reports. All reported axiom sets are
subsets of `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`; no warnings, errors or
`sorryAx` appear. Minimal-recipe structure, accepted-adversarial-ballot
characterization, static equivalence and privacy remain open.

## Minimal public recipes: candidate and refutation gate

Goal: establish the size-minimal replacement facts needed by Appendix B,
Lemma 9's recipe argument, with the allowed names and handles explicit.
Claim: for a fixed substitution and restricted-name set, every public recipe
has a public E-equivalent recipe of minimum raw `nodeCount`. Every one-hole
subterm of a minimum recipe is minimum under the same substitution and policy.
Such recipes have no ordinary contextual rewrite step. A decrypt whose explicit
ciphertext key evaluates to the decryption key's public key cannot be minimum;
its public plaintext is a smaller equivalent recipe.
Status: conjectured.
Formal oracle: `MinimalRecipes.lean`, public theorem types and axiom audit,
`lake build`.
Falsifier: a root rule that does not shrink raw syntax, a context that reverses
size order, loss of publicness on forward rewriting, or an equivalent smaller
public subterm replacement that does not give a smaller whole recipe.
Positive control: minimum one-node handles and constants, contextual subterm
inheritance, and a decrypt with keys equal only after substitution.
Negative control: a one-node handle can evaluate to a reducible term; minimum
recipe size does not imply an irreducible substituted value. Raw E0 syntax size
is not invariant, as retained by the zero+zero counterexample.
PBT gate: all seven raw root families with bounded arbitrary components, all
one-hole constructor positions, seeds 1, 7, 42 and inputs 0–255. Test raw size
shrinkage and the false substitution-normality generalization before proofs.
Trusted definitions: `Term.Public`, `Term.subst`, `Term.nodeCount`, `EqE`,
`Context.fill`, `RewriteStep`; the handle type fixes available variables.
Reality oracle: the extracted Cortier–Smyth Appendix B, Lemma 9, page 45 uses
minimum syntax size among recipes with the same substituted E-value. Its
nonce-freedom condition is retained as a parameter, not silently replaced by
full-frame name restriction.
Residual assumptions and unsupported cases: existence is logical, not an
executable minimizer. This candidate does not assert modulo-E0 irreducibility
or the historical substitution's destructor-head classification (*). Those
claims require further work; raw syntax size is not E0-invariant. Tuple
projection notation in the source is encoded by the existing binary selectors.

The gate passed before the general proofs: seeds 1, 7, 42, configured for 500
cases at size 40, all report success and `gaveUp=0`; the deterministic backstop
passes all 256 inputs. The false handle-evaluation-normality property fails at
n=0 with zero shrinks. The gate tests raw size mechanics, not decidability of
minimum recipes or the historical classification (*).

Additional cancellation candidate: a product of two explicit ciphertext recipes
whose keys are E-equal after substitution cannot be minimum. E7 gives a public
smaller recipe by retaining one key and composing the two nonce and message
recipes. An explicit partial decryption followed by decryption also cannot be
minimum when its key and ciphertext matches hold after substitution. These
are local replacement facts, not an exhaustive analysis of destructor inputs.

The minimum-recipe candidate and additional local cancellation claims are now
machine-checked in `MinimalRecipes.lean`. The [claim ledger](helios-minimal-recipes.md)
records exact declarations, trusted definitions and remaining scope. The proof
selects the least inhabited raw size, preserves publicness through one-hole
replacement, and uses E5–E7 to eliminate semantically matching explicit
constructors. Every subterm shares the original policy and substitution.

Controls check a non-atomic public-key minimum using full-E shape to exclude all
size-one competitors, and instantiate its minimum subterm. A restricted literal
name is excluded at size one. The minimized PBT counterexample is checked as an
actual minimum handle with a raw step in its substituted value. An ordinarily
irreducible decrypt is nonminimum under a substitution that supplies its key;
E7 and E6 controls similarly retain semantic-only matching. A public reducible
projection has an equivalent minimum, and zero+zero is nonminimum despite raw
normality. The only intermediate proof failure was Lean syntax: `public` is a
reserved structure-field token, corrected to `isPublic`. No claim was weakened.

Validation: `lake build` passes (3375 jobs). The public-type and axiom audit
contains 629 nonempty axiom reports, all using only `propext`, `Classical.choice`
and `Quot.sound`, plus 14 axiom-free reports. The final log contains no warnings,
errors or `sorryAx`.

The original minimum-recipe/substitution classification (*) remains open, as do
Lemma 9, frame static equivalence, processes, privacy and the later task-list
sections. This increment supplies replacement lemmas for that classification;
it does not establish exhaustive historical recipe shapes.

## Historical selector exception: candidate and representation gate

Goal: translate Lemma 9's minimum-recipe destructor exception to the encoded
binary tuple selectors before attempting the exhaustive classification.
Claim: in the fresh two-candidate historical frame, fst(snd(y1)) is a minimum
public recipe for voter 1's second ciphertext. It is not a single binary
selector applied to a variable. Its evaluated outer fst reduces to a ciphertext.
Status: conjectured.
Formal oracle: a full-E lower bound excluding every recipe with fewer than
three nodes, followed by a `MinimalRecipe` witness and explicit evaluated steps.
Falsifier: a size-one or size-two recipe with the same full-E value, or a wrong
field offset. The lower bound must quantify over all names, not an enumerated
finite name sample.
Positive control: the first ciphertext uses a single selector; both selected
ciphertexts have the independently allocated nonce. The frame is fresh and
honest acceptance is already checked.
Negative control: treating every source tuple projection as one binary selector
misses the second field, even for a minimum public recipe. This would refute
that literal translation, not the paper's use of indexed tuple projections.
PBT gate: generated first/second field accesses in the existing two-candidate
frame; compare evaluated output against an independently indexed ciphertext,
and test the false single-selector syntax property. Seeds 1, 7, 42, configured
500 cases at size 40 and deterministic inputs 0–255.
Trusted definitions: `Term.project`, `Term.drop`, nested `Term.tuple`, the
historical frame, raw size and full E. No new projection operation or equation.
Reality oracle: source Appendix B, page 45, exception N=π_j(x), and the existing
encoding π_(j+1)(x)=fst(snd^j(x)). A faithful exception must admit that chain.
Residual scope: a representation counterexample and size bound, not an exhaustive
historical-recipe classification. Later tuple tails and destructors remain open.

The representation gate found the false single-selector property at n=1,
seed 1, zero shrinks. Correct field evaluation passed seeds 1, 7, 42 with 500
configured cases at size 40 and `gaveUp=0`, plus all 256 deterministic inputs.
The ensuing general size bound is stronger evidence than this raw evaluation
sample: it excludes all smaller full-E competitors and quantifies over every
available name. Its handle and unary-handle exclusion premises remain explicit.
An additional positive control will establish that the first-field selector is
itself minimum at size two, showing why the unary-handle exclusion is necessary
for the size-three bound.

The historical selector candidate is machine-checked. `SmallRecipeBounds.lean`
classifies the complete size-one/two syntax and proves ciphertext recipe lower
bounds under explicit full-E exclusions for handles and unary handle images.
`HistoricalSelectorSPOT.lean` discharges those premises for the second ciphertext
in the existing fresh two-candidate frame. It proves a size-three minimum for
fst(snd(y1)) under any name policy; the lower bound quantifies over all names.
Its second nonce is 21, distinct from the first ciphertext nonces 20 and 22.

The normal-form evidence retains an actual path to the target, target
irreducibility and existence of a normal argument whose enclosing fst has a
different E0 head. The single-binary-selector translation of the exception is
therefore refuted. The source's actual indexed exception is preserved:
`indexed_projection_exception_applies` identifies the witness with π_2(y1)
(`project 1` in the encoded zero-based indexing). No change to the tuple
encoding, public operations or equations was needed.

Controls establish a size-two minimum for the first historical ciphertext and
a size-one minimum when a separate frame publishes the target itself. These
show necessity of the two lower-bound premises. The main frame is checked fresh
and its relevant ballot accepted on an empty board. Initial proof failures
were proof engineering: `decide` on goals containing free variables was replaced

relabelled as a proof.

The exhaustive historical minimum-recipe classification, Lemma 9, static
equivalence and privacy remain open. The [minimum-recipe ledger](helios-minimal-recipes.md#indexed-tuple-selectors-and-minimum-size)
records the translation constraint for the next proof.

## Decryption paths and minimum explicit-ciphertext recipes: candidate

Goal: discharge the explicit-ciphertext decryption case of the minimum-recipe
classification, including matches exposed by arbitrary argument reductions.
Claim: every modulo path from dec(a,b) either retains dec with paths from both
arguments, or reaches an E5/E6 match and then follows a path from its plaintext.
The matching ciphertext is reached from b; a reaches either its key or the
matching partial decryption. If a minimum recipe's right argument is an explicit
ciphertext, every irreducible representative of its substituted value retains
the dec head and the two substituted argument values up to E. Otherwise its
explicit public plaintext would be a strictly smaller equivalent recipe.
Status: conjectured.
Formal oracle: `DecryptionPaths.lean` and `MinimalDecryption.lean`, public type
and axiom audit, `lake build`.
Falsifier: an arbitrary path that loses the outer dec without either matched
rule, a missed E6 ciphertext copy, or a minimum explicit-ciphertext decrypt
whose normal value has a different head.
Positive control: delayed E5/E6 matches through projected keys and ciphertexts,
a reducible returned plaintext, and a minimum stuck decrypt with explicit
ciphertext under identity substitution.
Negative control: ciphertext-shaped output does not imply the original right
argument already had ciphertext syntax. Matching decrypts must remain nonminimum;
without minimum the normal-form head claim is false.
PBT gate: bounded arbitrary components and nested projection wrappers around
E5/E6 arguments; raw normal output equals the independently selected plaintext
normal output. Seeds 1, 7, 42, 500 configured cases at size 40 and inputs 0–255.
Trusted definitions: the seven root schemata, E0, modulo paths, public recipes,
substitution, syntax size and minimum recipes. No additional decryption rule.
Reality oracle: source E5/E6 and Appendix B's decryption clause in (*). Matching
partial decryptions include the entire ciphertext, not only key or nonce.
Residual scope: the explicit-ciphertext right-argument case only. Arbitrary
ciphertext-valued recipe classification, historical handle/product cases,
Lemma 9 and secrecy remain open.

The delayed-match gate passes seeds 1, 7, 42 (500 configured cases, size 40,
`gaveUp=0`) and all 256 deterministic inputs. The false initial-ciphertext-shape
property fails at n=0 with zero shrinks. An initial parser failure used Lean's
reserved `partial` keyword as a local name; it was corrected before the gate ran.

For the nonvacuity control, add the following sufficient minimum criterion:
a public irreducible term whose `cryptoWeight` equals its raw `nodeCount` is
minimum under identity substitution. Confluence supplies a path from any
E-equivalent competitor to the term up to E0; decreasing crypto-weight and
`cryptoWeight ≤ nodeCount` give the size bound. This criterion applies to a
stuck decrypt with four distinct variable leaves and supplies a concrete
minimum explicit-ciphertext recipe. It is not a necessary criterion for minimum.

Additional historical case: if any right-argument recipe evaluates to a
ciphertext with a public constant plaintext, E5/E6 matching contradicts minimum
size, regardless of that recipe's syntax. The constant itself has size one.
Instantiate this for arbitrary honest historical ciphertext components, whose
plaintexts are the public constants zero or one. Retain the full-E right-value
premise and the actual frame substitution in the public corollary. No freshness
or secret-key nondeducibility premise is needed for this replacement argument.
This does not yet cover arbitrary products whose plaintext recipes may be larger.

The normal-shape result also supports the source's exact normal-form composition
clause: for independently supplied irreducible representatives of both arguments
and the whole decrypt, the whole representative is E0-equal to dec of those two
argument representatives. Contextual irreducibility and confluence identify the
ordered components. Retain all three irreducibility and E-value premises, and
instantiate this composition result for honest historical components as well.

The decryption path and minimum-recipe candidates are machine-checked.
`DecryptionPaths.lean` proves an exhaustive retained-head/matched-plaintext path
split, full-E ciphertext inversion and normal-form composition under an explicit
no-match premise. `MinimalDecryption.lean` derives no-match from minimum size for
an explicit ciphertext argument and, separately, any ciphertext value with a
constant plaintext. The explicit case also excludes ciphertext outputs without
requiring target irreducibility. The [minimum-recipe ledger](helios-minimal-recipes.md#decryption-with-explicit-or-honest-component-ciphertext-values)
records exact public premises and remaining scope.

`HistoricalMinimalDecryption.lean` instantiates the constant-plaintext argument
for every honest component in both swapped frames and all positive candidate
counts. The right recipe has arbitrary syntax but must be E-equal to that
component. The actual frame substitution and nonce-only name policy are explicit.
The normal-form theorem retains irreducibility and E-value premises for both
arguments and the whole decrypt and concludes E0 equality with their dec
composition. Freshness and secret-key secrecy are not assumptions of this result.

Controls preserve actual delayed E5/E6 matches through projected arguments, a
reducible returned plaintext and exact final ciphertext. A full-E counterexample
refutes initial ciphertext syntax from ciphertext output. A six-node irreducible
stuck decrypt is minimum by the weight/size criterion and instantiates normal
shape, composition and no-match. A matching explicit decrypt reaches a different
normal head and is nonminimum; a reducible equivalent projection wrapper shows
why target normality matters. A historical nonce-public recipe names the secret
key, projects an honest ciphertext and returns one, but is proved nonminimum.
The latter control prevents interpreting the minimum-recipe theorem as decryption
prevention or privacy. One later proof-engineering issue retained a path witness
before destructuring the matching witness; no semantic premise was changed.

The remaining classification must handle products and arbitrary ciphertext-valued
recipes, plus the indexed projection/tail cases. Lemma 9, static equivalence,
processes, secrecy and later task-list sections remain open.

## Ciphertext-product plaintext reconstruction: candidate

Goal: discharge the homomorphic-product case of the minimum decryption argument.
Claim: a finite nonempty product built from explicit ciphertext recipes and
constant-plaintext ciphertext recipes under one E-equivalent public key has a
public plaintext recipe strictly smaller than the ciphertext recipe. Explicit
leaves retain their message recipe; constant leaves require size greater than
one; multiplication combines plaintext recipes with add and nonce values with
compose. A minimum decrypt of such a product cannot reach an E5/E6 match, and
normal-form composition follows. Instantiate honest-component leaves in the
historical frame, for all positive candidate counts and both swaps.
Status: conjectured.
Formal oracle: an inductive `CiphertextProduct` certificate, its soundness,
publicness and strict-size theorems, historical leaf instantiation, and the
minimum-recipe normal-form theorem. `lake build` and public type/axiom audit.
Falsifier: a product with no strictly smaller public plaintext recipe, a wrong
key admitted to homomorphic fusion, loss of repeated plaintext occurrences,
or an empty product silently treated as an identity.
Positive control: mixed explicit/honest leaves, both voter assignments, nested
products and repeated honest components. A successful nonce-public decrypt of
a repeated honest component returns one+one and is nonminimum.
Negative control: duplicated ciphertext factors must not collapse to one factor;
key agreement is an explicit premise. A published one-node ciphertext cannot
supply a strictly smaller constant recipe, so the constant-leaf size premise
must be retained.
PBT gate: bounded binary product trees with explicit and honest-projection leaves;
independently assembled message and nonce trees, raw E7 output and strict recipe
size comparisons. Seeds 1, 7, 42, 500 configured cases at size 40, inputs 0–255.
Trusted definitions: raw term size, substitution, E7, public recipes, historical
field layout and the supplied factor-origin certificate. Nonces in the certificate
are semantic values, not claimed public nonce recipes.
Reality oracle: source E7 and page 45's product of optional constructed ciphertexts
and honest projected components, retaining multiplicities and no implicit unit.
Residual scope: the product certificate does not prove that every ciphertext-valued
recipe has such an origin. That exhaustive provenance/classification remains open.

The ciphertext-product candidate is machine-checked in `CiphertextProducts.lean`.
The inductive certificate preserves the common key, complete message tree and
nonce multiplicities. Its soundness uses E7; publicness and strict raw-size
bounds follow separately by certificate induction. The minimum decryption
result derives a smaller public plaintext from any reached E5/E6 match and
then applies the checked normal-form composition theorem.

`HistoricalCiphertextProducts.lean` proves that no initial handle is E-equal to
any ciphertext, using pk/ballot structure. Every historical ciphertext recipe
therefore has at least two nodes, with no restriction on available names. This
discharges the honest constant-leaf bound for arbitrary component-equivalent
recipes. Substitution through drop/project and the existing field theorem also
supply certificates for actual indexed projections, for all positive counts,
either voter and both swaps. The historical normal-form corollary retains the
factor certificate and nonce-only recipe policy explicitly.

The PBT gate passed before the general proofs: seeds 1, 7, 42, 500 configured
cases, size 40, `gaveUp=0`, and all 256 deterministic inputs. It checks bounded
mixed product trees, separately assembled message and nonce expressions, raw E7
output and strict plaintext-recipe size. The duplicate-collapse control fails
at n=0, seed 1, zero shrinks. Checked controls preserve that full-E failure,
repeated factors in mixed products, a swapped component's actual bit/nonce,
wrong-key rejection and the one-node published-ciphertext size boundary. A
nonce-public repeated-component decrypt succeeds with one+one and is nonminimum.
The existing six-node minimum stuck decrypt instantiates the composition result.
One proof-engineering correction fixed the association of a publicness conjunction;
no semantics or theorem premise changed.

The [product ledger](helios-minimal-recipes.md#public-plaintext-reconstruction-for-ciphertext-products)
records the scope. Exhaustive historical ciphertext provenance and projection/tail
cases remain open; the new factor certificate is not silently assumed universal.

## Full-E multiplication inversion: candidate

Goal: derive ciphertext origins of both operands from a ciphertext-valued product,
so recursive factor certificates can eventually be justified rather than assumed.
Claim: if a*b is E-equal to penc(K,R,M), both a and b are E-equal to ciphertexts
under K. Their nonce composition is E-equal to R and their message sum is
E-equal to M. Inputs and target components may be reducible. No literal input
ciphertext shape or irreducibility premise is assumed.
Status: conjectured.
Formal oracle: a predicate saying every outer E0 factor has a ciphertext E-value
under a specified key; backward preservation across every modulo step/path;
`EqE` ciphertext inversion for multiplication, followed by the public axiom audit
and `lake build`.
Falsifier: a product can erase a non-ciphertext factor, fuse genuinely different
keys, or yield a ciphertext without both operand values being ciphertexts under
the output key. Expansion of a factor into a product must remain covered.
Positive control: products reached through nested projections and expanding
factors, repeated components and E0-equivalent keys. Preserve exact combined
nonce/message values in the conclusion.
Negative control: mismatching named keys and a surviving non-ciphertext factor;
raw fusion failure on E0-equal keys must not imply full-E inequality.
PBT gate: bounded product trees with projected wrappers around leaves/subproducts,
independently assembled nonce/message trees, and raw normalized outputs. Seeds
1, 7, 42, 500 configured cases at size 40, and inputs 0–255; a deliberately
incorrect cross-key fusion property must fail first.
Trusted definitions: E0 factor multisets, the proved exhaustive outer-fusion or
single-factor step split, full E, confluence, and ciphertext component paths.
Reality oracle: source E7 preserves the common key and all nonce/message factors;
there is no multiplication unit or rule discarding an unrelated outer factor.
Residual scope: this provides operand inversion, not yet exhaustive historical
ciphertext-recipe provenance or the complete minimum-recipe classification.

The multiplication gate passes seeds 1, 7, 42, 500 configured cases at size 40,
`gaveUp=0`, and all 256 deterministic inputs. The cross-key fusion control fails
at n=0, seed 1, zero shrinks. The initial general proof establishes backward
ciphertext-factor preservation and full-E operand/component inversion.

Additional product-head candidate for the same recipe induction: any path from
a product retains at least two outer factors or has a ciphertext E-value.
A single-factor step cannot remove the nonempty remainder; only an outer E7
fusion can reduce a two-factor bag to one, and that result is a ciphertext.
Consequently an irreducible E-equivalent product value has mul or penc shape;
products cannot be E-equal to arbitrary pair, partial-decryption, spk or pk terms.
The existing expanding-factor gate and fixed non-ciphertext-factor control test
the cardinality boundary; retain an explicit zero-as-factor control and checked
passive-head exclusions. No multiplication unit is introduced.

The multiplication inversion and product-head candidates are machine-checked.
`CiphertextFactorValues.lean` proves backward preservation of ciphertext values

## Non-ciphertext multiplication observations: result

Claim: minimum recipes with non-ciphertext multiplication values derive raw mul
origins and normal-form partitions in both worlds. Each final factor is the
value of a strictly smaller public recipe. Smaller public observations transfer
equality of these recipes, and exact source factor accounting reassembles
whole-recipe equality in both directions.
Status: machine-checked. Full static equivalence remains open.
Formal oracle: `MinimumMultiplicationOrigins.lean`,
`NormalMultiplicationFactors.lean`, `MultiplicationPartitions.lean`,
`MultiplicationLeaves.lean`, `MinimumMultiplicationPartitions.lean`,
`MultiplicationPartitionTransfer.lean`, `MultiplicationObservationInduction.lean`,
`MultiplicationObservationSPOT.lean` and their public checks in `Audit.lean`.
`lake build` passes 3525 jobs; the local full-build log is
`tmp/variable-overlap/multiplication-observation-full-build.log`.

Unlike addition/composition, a non-ciphertext whole product can contain
ciphertext factors that fuse. Plain unfused full-E factor-bag equality is not
the right observation relation. The proof first normalizes every raw leaf.
Exact minimum origins show that these normal representatives have non-mul
heads in both worlds, while still permitting ciphertext values. A factor's
E0 class is Normal when it has an irreducible representative. Products of such
factors may admit outer fusion, but cannot admit internal factor steps. Every
fusion preserves factor normality: the new ciphertext key is normal, its nonce
composes normal inputs and its message adds normal inputs modulo E0. Actual
modulo paths therefore induce only ciphertext-fusion paths on factor bags.
Every abstract finite fusion path is realizable by an actual modulo path with
an exact endpoint bag. Full-E equality of normal factor families is precisely
joinability of their bags by fusion.

MultiplicationPartition pairs public recipe occurrences with factor values.
Its fields retain the exact source recipe factor bag, exact target value bag,
each evaluated piece equation, publicness, whole-source equality, and the
identity sum(piece recipe size+1)=source recipe size+1. Fusion merges exactly
two occurrences into their product recipe and retains every other occurrence.
The budget measures original recipes even when normalizing values changes size.
For a non-ciphertext minimum product, value-shape reflection prevents a
destination ciphertext value. Both normal endpoints have mul heads and at
least two pieces, so every group recipe is strictly smaller than its original
source. These witnesses and bounds are derived in both worlds from source
minimum size, not assumed of destination minima.

Normal endpoint equality gives exact E0 factor matching. Each matched pair is
represented by smaller public recipes; their full-E comparisons transfer under
ObservationsBelow. Exact source factor accounting then reconstructs equality
under the destination substitution through a local quotient multiplication
fold. Its adjoined identity remains bookkeeping, not a public operation.
The final theorem retains both source minima, supplied source multiplication
E-values, absence of source ciphertext values, and the original total-size
smaller-observation premise. It covers every valid ground candidate assignment
and positive count; supplied values may reduce. No freshness, destination
minimum size or fixed factor-value premise is introduced.

Falsifier outcome: the generated positive family finds no counterexample.
Ignoring fusion and treating hidden products as already-normal single factors
are refuted. Finite search does not discharge the global observation premise.
Positive controls: same-key fusion beside an unrelated name produces the exact
combined nonce/message and a normal non-ciphertext product. The general fusion
join theorem is instantiated. A concrete public partition has exactly two
final pieces with strict original-recipe size bounds. Literal name products
attain exact three-node minima for arbitrary valid candidate assignments,
including repeated factors. Distinct permuted minima instantiate the complete
equality branch with a reducible supplied target.
Negative controls: the raw factor bag changes under valid fusion; a hidden
product violates NormalMulFactors; different keys cannot produce any
ciphertext; duplicates remain observable; fusion cannot delete the unrelated
remainder; zero is not a multiplication unit. Unequal multiplicities instantiate
the full minimum iff branch. A public nonminimum wrapper retains the need for
minimum size in exact origins. Complete-branch controls use diagonal candidate
assignments for the six-node bounded premise; the generic grouping controls
exercise fusion independently and do not prove different-vote privacy by tests.

PBT gate: unfused-bag and hidden-product defects fail at input 0, seed 1, zero
shrinks, before the general proof. The partition family passes seeds 1, 7 and 42
with 500 configured cases per seed, size 40, gaveUp=0, and 2048 deterministic
inputs. It partitions two through eight labelled ciphertext occurrences by
literal key, retains repeated nonce/bit values and an unrelated name, and checks
independently specified occurrence counts and raw recipe budgets. A literal
E7 fixture checks exact combined components and the retained outer factor
count. These are executable proxies, not an arbitrary full-E decision procedure.

endpoint rewriting, explicit quotient coercion types, a reserved identifier,

No semantic claim or load-bearing premise was weakened.
Trusted definitions: E/E0, actual modulo paths, E0/full-E quotients, public
recipes, raw node-count minima and the actual general initial frames.
Reality oracle: source E7 under AC multiplication, including equal-key fusion
with unrelated residual factors. No equation, public operation, custom axiom
or assumed confluence changed.

frames publishing partial decryptions and historical process matching remain
required. Full static equivalence stays unchecked in the canonical task list.

## Successful projection transport enquiry

Goal: close successful projection cases of local shared minimization without
assuming preservation of arbitrary observations.
Claim: honest component-proof selectors are minimum under freshness; aggregate
selectors are minimum above one candidate and have a shared shorter component
representative at one candidate. A projection with a minimum child either has
a shared minimum or yields a pair/ciphertext value. Explicit pairs use their
selected minimum child; honest proof fields and empty tails should close.

solved projection cases. Ciphertext-related projection transport stays open.
Falsifier: a shorter equivalent public component selector; a multi-candidate
aggregate aliasing a component proof; or a proof/empty-tail projection whose
source minimum representative does not retain its value in the other world.
Formal oracle: planned exact selector-minimum and projection-transport lemmas.
Reality oracle: the initial tuple field order, source indexed selectors, honest
nonce provenance, and the retained one-candidate component/aggregate equality.
Positive controls: indexed selector sizes, both worlds, explicit pair selection,
empty-tail output and different component values.
Negative control: the one-candidate aggregate is not minimum because its
component proof is equal and its selector is strictly shorter.
PBT gate: detect that known exception first; check canonical aggregate selectors
and explicit pair selection at varied positive candidate counts in both swaps.
Trusted definitions: public recipes, node-count minima, full EqE, tuple fields,
fresh names, actual candidate substitutions and SharedMinimum.
Residual: pair/ciphertext projection outputs and the other unresolved local
root cases remain open, as do final partial decryptions and process privacy.

Extension before proof: use the newly checked proof-selector minima to prove
minimum size of every nonempty proof-only ballot suffix, at positions
n+1 through 2*(n+1). A constructed equivalent pair must pay for a minimum
first proof field plus its other child and root; an honest-tail equivalent
has the same position under freshness. The one-candidate aggregate exception
uses the shorter component field in that lower bound. The gate now checks
canonical first-field values and these size budgets for every such suffix.
Ciphertext-prefix tails remain outside this extension.

Result: `minimum_component_proof_selector` gives exact component-selector
minima; `minimum_aggregate_proof_selector` gives aggregate minima at two or more
candidates. `aggregate_selector_shared_minimum` supplies the shorter component
representative at one candidate and the aggregate itself otherwise. Indexed
syntax counts are proved by general drop/project node-count lemmas. Fresh
nonce identity and existing proof-origin theorems rule out shorter public
aliases, including constructed proofs borrowing honest nonce values.

`minimum_proof_tail` proves minimum size for every nonempty suffix at positions
n+1 through 2*(n+1). A constructed pair must pay for its first minimum honest
proof field; an honest-tail alias has the same position. The one-candidate
aggregate exception uses its smaller component selector in this lower bound.
`proof_tail_shared_minimum` adds the empty suffix with a literal bottom witness.

`SharedMinimum.projection_of_minimum_pair` uses the selected minimum child.
`proof_chain_shared_minimum` covers all proof-valued honest handle chains,
including nonminimum inputs. `projection_shared_or_pair_ciphertext` handles
every projection with a minimum child: stuck projections, explicit minimum
pairs, honest proof fields, and proof-only/empty suffixes yield shared minima.
Its residual disjunction permits pair/ciphertext source outputs; in the proof,
those branches select ciphertext fields or retain a ciphertext-prefix tail.
The disjunction does not say such values cannot have shared minima.
`proof_projection_shared_minimum` extracts the complete proof-valued case.
No observation-induction premise, destination minimum or raw-normality premise
is assumed by these results.

Controls: seven public SPOTs check two-candidate minimum selector sizes 4, 5

and the one-candidate component/aggregate alias.

over varied positive candidate counts and both assignments.

minimum raw node count, tuple layout and SharedMinimum.

## Constructed ciphertext minimum enquiry

Goal: discharge the ciphertext-constructor root from local shared minimization.
Claim: a ciphertext constructor with three source-minimum public children is
minimum in the actual initial frame. A grouped assembly with a public nonce
cannot contain honest contributions, and its selected key plus grouped nonce
and payload fit within the original recipe size. Freshness is unnecessary
for this closure: protected nonce factors alone exclude the honest/mixed cases.
Status: machine-checked.
Falsifier: a public constructed ciphertext with minimum children has a smaller
public equivalent in an initial frame; or grouping loses the selected key's
size budget; or a public nonce equals a group retaining an honest nonce factor.
Formal oracle: group-plus-key size bound, public-nonce group origin and
minimum ciphertext constructor theorem.
Reality oracle: E7 reuses a common key and preserves every honest nonce factor;
the initial frame publishes a key and honest ballots under the full name policy.
Positive controls: constructed and mixed assemblies with nontrivial key recipes,
actual frame constructors, common E-equivalent keys and colliding names.
Negative controls: omitting child minimum permits shorter wrappers; omitting
the key from the regrouping budget undercounts the result; a frame directly
publishing an arbitrary public ciphertext invalidates general parent closure.
PBT gate: detect known minimum-child and key-budget defects before testing
assembled budgets and public-only fusion over varied tree shapes and both swaps.
Trusted definitions: EqE/E0, initial candidate frames, full public-name policy,
protected nonce factors, ciphertext groups and minimum syntax size.
Residual: successful decryption/checking and arithmetic transport, final public
partial-decryption frames, process matching and later backlog items.

Result: `CiphertextAssembly.key_group_budget` bounds the selected key plus
group budget by original node count plus one. For a constructed group this
is exactly the bound needed for a fused ciphertext. `CiphertextGroup.constructed_of_public_nonce`
excludes honest/mixed groups by a surviving restricted nonce factor, without
freshness or group-publicness premises. `minimum_penc_of_children` compares all
three minimum children against a minimum competitor's grouped components and
proves that the source ciphertext is minimum. It retains the actual initial
frame and full name restriction, with no freshness, normality or smaller-test
premise. The reduced `staticEq_of_destructor_arithmetic_transport` still needs
both orientations of successful decryption/checking and arithmetic transport.

PBT evidence: omitted child minimum and omitted key budget fail at input 0,
seed 1, zero shrinks. Seeds 1, 7 and 42 pass 500 configured cases each, size 40,
gaveUp=0; all 2048 backstop inputs pass. Five assembly forms include constructed,
honest and mixed trees with varying wrapped key sizes. Raw-normal-form fusion
checks retain E-equivalent keys in both assignments. These are bounded syntax
and evaluation fixtures, not unbounded minimum proofs. The pre-proof gate log
is `tmp/variable-overlap/constructed-ciphertext-gate.log`.

Seven SPOTs retain the 12-to-11-node regrouping with an eight-node component

## Composition minimum closure enquiry

Goal: discharge nonce composition from the remaining local transport cases.
Claim: a composition with minimum children is minimum in the initial historical
frame. More generally, minimum outer composition leaves force minimum size for
the whole recipe: semantic factor bags retain multiplicities, each matched
minimum leaf has the same cost, and the number of composition nodes is fixed
by the number of leaves. Freshness and smaller observations are unnecessary.
Status: machine-checked.
Falsifier: an E-equal public competitor has a smaller total composition cost
despite all leaves being minimum, or a minimum non-compose leaf acquires a
composition E-value in the initial frame.
Formal oracle: exact leaf/cardinality node-count identity, equal minimum-leaf
cost bags and minimum composition closure.
Reality oracle: composition has associativity and commutativity but no unit,
idempotence or arithmetic zero rule; initial handles expose keys/ballots.
Positive controls: rebracketing/permutation with repeated and non-atomic minimum
leaves, all original sizes and actual frame values, both swaps.
Negative controls: zero cannot disappear, repeated factors cannot collapse,
nonminimum wrappers permit smaller leaves, and directly publishing a composite
nonce invalidates closure for arbitrary frames.
PBT gate: detect zero-unit and multiplicity defects first, then exercise raw
leaf accounting, permuted factor bags and minimum-leaf fixture shapes.
Trusted definitions: EqE/E0, full-E classes, composition leaves and factors,
minimum syntax size, actual initial frame and the caller's public-name policy.
Residual: successful decryption/checking, addition/multiplication transport,
final partial-decryption frames and process privacy.

Result: `Term.composeLeaves_nodeCount` proves exact leaf-sum/cardinality
accounting. `MinimalRecipe.compose_leaf` preserves minimum size for each raw
outer leaf. `minimum_leaf_cost_bags_eq` pairs equal full-E classes of minimum
recipes and derives equal cost bags; `Term.nodeCount_eq_of_compose_leaf_costs`
recovers whole-recipe size. `minimum_compose_leaves_atomic` supplies semantic
indivisibility in the initial frame. `minimum_of_compose_leaves` derives minimum
size for the whole recipe, and `minimum_compose_of_children` instantiates it
for two minimum children. Both results retain any caller name policy, without
freshness or observation premises. The reduced static-equivalence criterion
retains successful decryption, successful checking, addition and multiplication
in both orientations; it does not assert those remaining premises.

PBT evidence: zero-unit and duplicate-collapse defects fail at input 0, seed 1,
zero shrinks. Seeds 1, 7 and 42 pass 500 configured cases each, size 40,
gaveUp=0; all 2048 backstop inputs pass with one through seven leaves and both
swaps. Checks use exact raw leaf counts/costs and normalized raw evaluated leaf
bags for permutations with non-atomic key, stuck-projection and ciphertext
fixtures. They do not decide arbitrary E equality or establish minimum size.
The successful pre-proof log is `tmp/variable-overlap/composition-minimum-gate.log`.
An initial attempt to compute quotient equality failed instance synthesis;
that log is retained as `tmp/variable-overlap/composition-minimum-nonexecutable-gate.log`.
The executable oracle was corrected to raw normalized bags before the proof.

Seven SPOTs retain eleven-node reassociated minima with repeated four-node
leaves, observable zero and multiplicity, a weaker caller policy with colliding
nonces, a removable nonminimum leaf, a frame directly publishing a composite,

blueprint B7-A. It does not close B7, final-frame equivalence or ballot secrecy.

`Term.addSyntaxSummary_cost_le` bounds raw recipe cost by the sum of nonnumeric
occurrence costs and optional numeric cost. `public_addition_minimum_cost_representative`
constructs a public raw-E0-equal term attaining this bound. `minimum_add_atoms_atomic`
uses the initial-frame origin theorem to derive semantic addition atoms from
source-minimum raw nonnumeric leaves. `minimum_add_summary_cost_eq` pairs equal
semantic classes of minimum leaves, preserving costs and numeric presence/count.

premises. `expanded_minimum_compose_form` derives source syntax under the
caller's policy. `accepted_expanded_minimum_compose_form_after_swap` derives
syntax from a destination value with the original recipe-only strict budget.
Actual handle exclusions cover the retained old values, partial constructors
and numeric results. Successful projections are restricted through pair-shape
reflection and honest-data origins; matching decryptions may return a borrowed
E6 numeric result, which cannot be composition-valued. No unsupported
recipe-only decryption failure hypothesis is introduced.

`accepted_expanded_minimum_compose_leaf_values` discharges semantic atomicity
of all raw leaves in both worlds. The complete composition-valued equality
branch reuses `Term.compose_leaves_substitution`, full-E class factor equality
and `composition_leaf_bag_transfer`. Minimum closure reuses the existing
`minimum_leaf_cost_bags_eq` and exact node-count identity. Every repeated factor
retains its occurrence and cost. Global observations and shared minimum
transport remain open; this is one local B8 value branch.

The shared `Frame.compose_form_of_paths` exposes only structural path and
output exclusions. It allows decryption success whose output is not a
composition. The initial-frame helper instantiates its old no-match premise,
preserving the two public origin theorem statements. No homomorphic equations,
composition laws, frame values or minimum-cost definitions change.

Eight controls retain actual handle atomhood, minimum composition of new
published children, noncollapse of repeated zero-result factors, the accepted
reassociated/permuted comparison with an inhabited diagonal observation
premise, a projection hiding composition with nonminimum size, an E5 wrapper
exposing composition, actual numeric E6 success, and an arbitrary-frame
countermodel to constructor closure without handle exclusion. These expected
behaviors follow from the source AC-only composition law and the independently
chosen published-value fixtures. The arbitrary-frame countermodel is not an
election attack.

The gate detects both duplicate deletion and hidden-composition mutations at
input 0, seed 1, zero shrinks. Seeds 1, 7 and 42 each pass 500 cases at size 40
with `gaveUp=0`; 2048 deterministic inputs pass over both candidates and
assignments, four published-value leaf forms, repeated occurrences and E5
wrappers. This tests executable behavior on the generated family, not full-E
equality or universal minimum size. Gate log:
`tmp/variable-overlap/expanded-compose-gate.log` (1023 jobs).

Targeted verification: generic origin helper and initial refactor 851 jobs;
expanded origins 940 jobs; factor equality and minimum closure 941 jobs.
Final controls, public theorem audits and integrated verification follow below.

## Expanded addition enquiry

Status: conjectured. Goal: close the B8 addition-valued equality branch with
published numeric handles. The initial-frame addition/zero/one origin form is
too narrow: a result handle is a one-node minimum with an arbitrary accepted
numeric value. Raw addition summaries also treat that handle as an atom, and
initial literal-only numeric costs cannot bound its semantic contribution.
Candidate replacement: retain result handles in the source/destination addition
origin form; summarize them by a shared accepted numeral while preserving
optional-zero presence and all other leaf occurrences. Source minimum raw
nonnumeric leaves are semantic atoms. Destination leaf origins use observations
below leaf size plus two, paid by the strict parent-leaf gap and the other
nonempty recipe in the comparison. This retains the explicit result-probe
allowance instead of assuming recipe-only decryption failure.
Falsifiers: treat result handles as atoms, erase a published zero, apply
literal-only numeric costs to a one-node result above one, or silently spend
an oversized leaf probe. Formal oracle: shared numeric-handle summary semantics,
expanded addition origins, leaf atomicity and conditional full-E equality.
Reality oracle: accepted common numeric tallies and the source E0 numeric laws,
including the distinction between no numeric contribution and present zero.
Minimum representative costs with cheap published numerals remain a separate
open problem; do not claim addition minimum closure from initial-frame costs.

## Expanded addition outcome

Status: machine-checked, conditional equality branch. The general claim
`accepted_expanded_minimum_addition_equality_swap` is proved with all its local
summary, origin and leaf-size obligations discharged. For fresh names, public
accepted submissions, valid ground candidates and arbitrary swap assignments,
source-minimum addition-valued recipes have the same full-E equality outcome
under strictly smaller public observations. Accepted common tally numbers are
derived internally; destination minimality is not assumed. The global
observation/shared-minimum induction remains open.

Formal oracle: `ExpandedAdditionOrigins`, `NumericHandleAddition`,
`ExpandedAdditionSummary` and `ExpandedAdditionTransport`. The shared
`Frame.add_form_of_paths` allows frame-specific additive handles. The initial
addition-origin proof reuses it with no change to its two public statements.
The numeric summary constructs an E-equivalent numeral-leaf value before
applying existing full-E addition summaries. Nonnumeric leaves are actual
proper subterms, and their two-node probe allowance fits the original pair's
size sum. The proof preserves optional numeric presence and atom multiplicity.
No trusted cryptographic syntax or equation was changed.

Positive/negative controls: ten kernel SPOTs cover zero/result equality and
distinct result inequality in actual unequal-voter elections; mixed additive
minimum representatives; an accepted tally of two available at one node;
handle-aware summary expansion; present zero; repeated slots and atoms;
nonminimum addition of minimum numeric children; successful projection/E5
wrappers excluded by minimum size; and successful numeric E6. The shared
numeral table does not make all outputs constant, erase zero, saturate sums at
one, remove duplicates, or forbid legitimate destructor success.

Refuted claims remain recorded: literal numeric recipe costs do not bound a
published numeral's minimum size, and minimum numeric children do not imply
minimum addition. The accepted result-two SPOT and the zero-result plus
one-result collapse are checked counterexamples. These claims are not weakened
and relabelled as proved; addition minimum transport remains open.

PBT gate: the original pre-proof gate detects all three mutations (numeric
handle as atom, erased published zero, literal cost at a published two), each
at input zero with seed 1 and zero shrinks. It passes seeds 1, 7 and 42, 500
cases per seed at size 40, `gaveUp=0`, plus 2048 deterministic inputs in both
assignments. The final gate also checks the new handle-aware summary against
independently prescribed numeric counts and repeated atom bags; all checks
pass (1044 jobs, `tmp/variable-overlap/expanded-add-gate-final.log`). Reachable
fixtures cover both candidates, zero through four repeated numeric slots and
projection wrappers. These tests are refutation evidence within this scope,
not a security proof or complete E-normalization decision procedure.

Reality oracle: the existing accepted common-tally theorem and independent
0/1/two fixtures retain the source E0 numeric laws and full E6 ciphertext
binding. The increment changes proof accounting, not the protocol model.
No new external implementation or cryptographic-library validation is claimed.

## Expanded addition minimum enquiry

Status: conjectured. Goal: close addition shared minimum transport for actual
accepted expanded frames. Candidate claim: replace literal-only numeric cost
with the least node-count-plus-one among pure additive expressions built from
bits and marked numeric handles. This cost is attained, is subadditive under
numeric addition, and is at most two for every published numeral. Realizing
an outer summary at its atom costs plus that numeric cost gives a globally
minimum representative when the nonnumeric leaves are source minimum. The
representative remains equal in both frames sharing the accepted tally table.

Falsifier: a shorter equivalent minimum recipe with different numeric cost,
an atom leaf that reveals a hidden addition value, erasure of present zero,
or a greedy denomination choice that is not optimal. Formal oracle: least-cost
numeric expression existence and lower bounds, summary realization, global
minimum comparison and accepted shared-minimum transport. Reality oracle:
independent finite denomination enumeration, accepted one-node result-two and
zero/one fixtures, and existing full-E addition summaries. Positive controls
must use cheap published numerals and repeated nonnumeric atoms. Negative
controls must preserve zero presence, reject literal costs and reject greedy
choice (denominations 3 and 4, target 6). No finite search result substitutes
for the global minimum proof. Shared tally numbers and source minimum atom
origins are load-bearing premises, and full-frame equivalence remains open.
