identify the exact remaining final-frame transport obligation. Candidate:
source minimum recipes and strictly smaller public observations suffice for
forward equality preservation, with no supplied normal head or value-class
certificate. Reverse minimum transport then gives the full comparison step;
expanded, final and partial static equivalence become equivalent to shared
minimum transport in both directions. Acceptance in the reversed candidate
assignment must be derived from the proved initial-frame theorem.

Falsifiers: dispatching on a raw recipe head instead of its normal value,
classifying successful E6 or fused products as stuck/nonciphertext values,
using original acceptance in a reversed frame without proof, or removing
common-minimum transport from the final equivalence. Formal oracle: exhaustive
Lean cases on a common normal ground value and exact lifting through existing
minimum-transport/presentation theorems. Reality oracle: existing E5/E6/E3
rules, independently enumerated normal-head fixtures over published handles,
and the existing branch controls. The gate will check all fourteen ground
head classes and detect wrong raw-head, fusion and binding mutations. Kernel
controls must include real published values and a countermodel to dropping
shared minimum transport. Global shared minima, B9 and B10 remain open.

### Expanded minimum-observation assembly outcome

Status: machine-checked. `accepted_expanded_minimum_equality_forward` derives a
common normal ground value and exhausts all twelve operator heads plus names
and constants. Its public premises are fresh names, valid ground candidates,
public accepted submissions, source minimum recipes, smaller public equality
observations and source equality. Normal forms, value classes, destructor
failure certificates and destination minima are derived or unnecessary.

`accepted_sequence_reversed_candidates` transfers real sequential acceptance
using initial-frame static equivalence. With minimum recipes in both worlds,
the assembled proof gives the full equality iff. Exact lifting identifies
expanded, final and aggregate-partial static equivalence with two-way shared
minimum transport. Bounded two-way shared minima supply observations below the
same bound, ready for the remaining simultaneous transport induction. Local
transport in both directions also suffices without an observation premise.
These statements do not prove their remaining shared-minimum premises.

The initial gate failed at input zero in both swaps: fixture 15, candidate-one
result, had raw-normalized addition head 9 rather than the expected constant
head 1. The independently checked tally is one. Classification: inadequate
test oracle, not a false comparison theorem. Raw normalization does not finish
E0 numeric equivalence. The corrected oracle adds the existing top-level
numeric summary for zero/one aliases, retaining the original fixture and its
expected mathematical value. The minimized failure becomes a kernel theorem;
raw diagnostics remain in `tmp/variable-overlap/expanded-observation-falsifier.log`.
The proof uses checked full normal-form existence, not this executable oracle.

The corrected gate detects four defects at input zero, seed 1, zero shrinks:
raw result-head dispatch, nonciphertext classification of a fused product,
omitted E6 binding, and raw-normalization completeness for numeric sums.
Seeds 1, 7 and 42 each pass 500 cases at size 40 with `gaveUp=0`; all 2048
deterministic inputs pass, 21 fixtures each in both assignments. All fourteen
ground head classes are covered with actual partial/results, projections,
E5/E6 success and homomorphic fusion. These are bounded refutation checks.

Ten kernel controls check the numeric-head counterexample, raw E6/result head
change, ciphertext fusion, binding rejection, distinct minimum result/literal
aliases, cross-head distinctions, nonempty reversed acceptance, bounded
lifting, final/partial lifting and the necessity of shared transport. The
last is an existing finite size/equality countermodel, explicitly not a Helios
frame. Global lifting instances use diagonal candidates; different-vote
shared minima are not smuggled in through those controls.

The remaining build failures were proof engineering: a missing check-branch
import, a list-membership simplification, and a constructor-publicness proof.
The substantive theorem statements were unchanged. Targeted builds pass:
gate 1051 jobs, complete assembly/lifting 968 jobs, controls 1089 jobs. Nineteen
new public theorem audits are added. Trusted definitions remain the existing
symbolic theory, normality, frames, acceptance, minimum size and public
observations. The independent oracle is the existing E3/E5/E6 rules, checked
numeric tallies and explicit fixture-head expectations; no new implementation
or computational-security validation is claimed.

Two-way shared minima, including multiplication and remaining local/successful
transport cases, remain open. The exact final-frame reduction is conditional.
B8, B9 and B10 remain incomplete; milestone coverage stays seven of ten
(70% unweighted, not effort remaining). See the
[observation assembly record](helios-expanded-observation-assembly.md).


Integrated verification: full `lake build` passes 3713 jobs, including nineteen

## Expanded non-ciphertext multiplication minimum enquiry

Initial status: conjectured; outcome below: machine-checked. Goal: discharge the non-ciphertext multiplication case of
expanded shared-minimum transport. Candidate: minimum children and shared
minima of strictly smaller public recipes suffice for a shared globally
minimum product, for any destination frame over the same handles. Source
numeric result origins supply normal single-factor leaves. Existing fusion
partitions preserve occurrences, and shared minimum pieces reassemble with
exact costs. Normal-partition comparison must prove global minimality against
all public competitors, not just raw regroupings.

Falsifiers: omitting a duplicate piece, equating one-frame minimization with
shared minimization, using nonnormal unfused targets as factor partitions,
or assuming a minimum-child product is always minimum. Formal oracle: extract
the existing generic competitor-partition comparison and shared reassembly;
instantiate actual expanded source origins and prove the strict smaller-piece
case. Reality oracle: existing E0/E3 laws, actual published partial/result
fixtures, independent source/destination component summaries and exact syntax
costs. Gate: generated shared replacements over expanded handles with fusion,
duplicates and delayed recipes, mutation controls and multiple seeds. Kernel
controls must include a product of minimum children that has a strictly smaller
shared representative. Ciphertext-valued multiplication and the remaining
transport induction remain separate open obligations.

### Expanded non-ciphertext multiplication minimum outcome

Status: machine-checked. `accepted_expanded_minimum_children_non_ciphertext_mul_shared`
closes this local transport case for actual accepted expanded frames. Its
premises retain fresh names, valid ground candidates, public accepted
submissions, source-minimum children, absence of a source ciphertext value for
the whole product, and forward shared minima below the original product size.
Its conclusion supplies a globally source-minimum representative equal to the
original product in both frames. No observation, reverse-transport, destination
normality or destination-minimum premise is added.

Source numeric origins supply normal single-factor representatives for every
minimum raw leaf, even when the parent can shrink. Existing fusion partitions
retain exact occurrence costs. Every piece of a normal non-ciphertext product
is strictly smaller than the original recipe, so the induction premise
supplies shared representatives for all pieces. Generic reassembly preserves
the destination; minimum partition comparison proves source minimality against
all public competitors, under the caller's public-name policy.

The two generic arguments are extracted from the original minimum-partition
and shared-reassembly files; initial and expanded wrappers reuse them. The
public statements of `minimum_of_normal_partition`,
`sharedMinimum_of_partition_shared_pieces` and
`minimum_children_non_ciphertext_mul_shared` match their pre-refactor sources
exactly. Existing E3, fusion partitions, factor bags and piece costs are reused.
No new homomorphic equation or computational-library claim is introduced.

The gate detects all three mutations at input zero, seed 1, zero shrinks:
source-only replacement, duplicate-cost deletion and unfused target partitions.
Seeds 1, 7 and 42 each pass 500 cases at size 40 with `gaveUp=0`; all 2048
deterministic inputs pass. Fixtures use two through eight pieces in both
assignments, actual partial/result handles, duplicate pieces, delayed recipes
and constructed ciphertext fusion. Raw-normalized nonce/numeric component
summaries provide bounded refutation evidence; they do not establish global
minimality or full-E normalization completeness.

Eight kernel controls provide independent positive/negative evidence. A
published-result wrapper shrinks from four to one nodes in different-vote
frames. Two wrapped zero-result occurrences shrink from nine to exactly three
nodes, and the result is not equal to one factor. Actual partial/result
children yield normal partitions with at least two strictly smaller public
pieces. Minimum constructed ciphertexts can still fuse. The complete local
transport theorem takes minimum children of sizes four and six and produces
a shared minimum of at most eight nodes for their eleven-node non-ciphertext
product; diagonal candidates inhabit its smaller-minimum premise. A concrete
two-frame counterexample rejects source-only replacement. A hidden-product
wrapper is nonminimum and refutes omitting minimum-leaf origins.

The generic refactor passes 893 jobs; expanded minimum closure passes 944 jobs;
the gate passes 1052 jobs; all eight controls pass 1076 jobs. Seventeen new
public theorem audits cover the increment. The control elaboration failure was
proof engineering: an explicit product recipe was needed to infer publicness.
No candidate theorem was weakened. Trusted definitions remain the existing
symbolic theory, frame/acceptance semantics, full normality and public minimum
recipes. Independent checks use existing E3, numeric tally equations, explicit
syntax sizes and retained occurrence/separation controls.

Ciphertext-valued multiplication shared minimum transport, remaining local
constructor/selector and successful-case transport, and the global two-way

## Expanded constructed-ciphertext minimum enquiry

Initial status: conjectured; outcome below: machine-checked. Goal: close public ciphertext constructor minimum closure
and constructed-only ciphertext multiplication transport over published handles.
Candidate: opaque public nonce provenance excludes honest/mixed groups for a
public nonce; selected-key plus group costs then prove global constructor
minimality. A nontrivial constructed-only assembly compresses strictly under
its selected key. Existing syntax key transfer supplies a ciphertext value in
the destination even when the parent is nonminimum; smaller shared minima
then finish transport. No additional homomorphic or coherence axiom is allowed.

Falsifiers: a public partial exposing an honest nonce factor, loss of a
constructed nonce/payload occurrence, an incoherent product compressed under
one key, or claiming strict compression for one constructor. Formal oracle:
generic assembly bounds and opaque nonce classification, expanded constructor
minimum theorem, actual assembly value transfer and constructed-only shared
compression. Reality oracle: existing E3, independent raw component summaries,
actual published partial/result fixtures, and normal minimum competitor
classification. Gate: coherent trees with arbitrary published-handle and
delayed keys, multiple seeds and deterministic cases; wrong-key, singleton and
occurrence-deletion mutations. Controls must include an actual published key
and constructor arguments plus a strictly shrinking product. Honest-only and
mixed ciphertext multiplication remain subsequent obligations.

### Expanded constructed-ciphertext minimum outcome

Status: machine-checked. Public ciphertext construction now preserves global
source minimum size when its three components are minimum. Public submissions
and source numeric results suffice; the accepted wrapper derives numeric
origins from fresh names, valid ground candidates and sequential acceptance.
The local shared-minimum constructor case requires no smaller observations or
minima. Opaque public nonce provenance excludes honest/mixed competitor groups;
selected-key plus group costs bound all public competitors.

Constructed-only ciphertext products now compress strictly under their selected
key, retaining every nonce/payload occurrence. Existing syntax key transfer
supplies ciphertext values in the destination for nonminimum assemblies as
well; grouped interpretation derives common-key agreement from those values.
The exact two-way smaller-minimum hypotheses provide observations through the
checked bounded lifting theorem, then a smaller shared representative finishes
constructed-only product transport. No parent minimum, separate coherence or
additional observation premise is introduced in that final interface.

Source-minimum constructed-only assemblies have raw constructor syntax.
Together with opaque nonce provenance, this also derives constructor syntax
for minimum ciphertexts with a publicly denotable nonce. The public policy,
actual publication slots and full ciphertext equations remain explicit.
Existing E3, group merge laws, factor non-deducibility and syntax key transfer
are reused; no new cryptographic equation or computational-library result is
claimed.

The gate detects all three mutations at input zero, seed 1, zero shrinks:
incoherent-key compression, strict singleton compression and deletion of a
repeated public nonce occurrence. Seeds 1, 7 and 42 pass 500 cases each at size
40 with `gaveUp=0`; all 2048 deterministic inputs pass in both swaps. Trees
have two through seven constructors, actual partial/result keys and components,
reducible key aliases and duplicate nonces. The executable comparison uses
raw-normalized nonce/numeric summaries; it does not decide full E or establish
global minimum size.

Eight kernel controls establish a four-node published constructor minimum and
shared representative, public nonce provenance, exclusion of a cheaper honest
selector, the non-strict singleton boundary, a nine-to-six-node shared
compression retaining both nonce occurrences, the exact two-way transport
interface, wrong-key rejection and delayed-key twelve-to-eleven compression.
The exact transport control uses diagonal candidates to inhabit smaller-minimum
premises; direct constructor/shared-compression controls use different votes.
The six-node compressed representative is proved globally minimum.

The only initial elaboration failure was proof engineering: a selector-size
lemma was not imported at the generic layer. The proof instead uses the

Targeted builds pass: gate 1053 jobs; generic tools, constructor minima and

Twenty-two public theorem audits are added. Trusted definitions remain the

## Expanded honest ciphertext combination minima enquiry

Claim: with fresh honest nonces, public submissions and numeric result values,
every nonempty honest ciphertext selector combination remains globally minimum
in the actual expanded published frame. Every minimum equivalent retains its
indexed occurrence bag. A nonminimum ciphertext product of minimum children
therefore has a constructed or mixed assembly group.
Status: conjectured.
Formal oracle: planned `ExpandedHonestMinima` declarations and kernel SPOTs;
`lake build` and the public theorem/axiom audit.
Falsifier: a cheaper public recipe, including a new partial or result handle,
equal to a singleton honest selector or a repeated honest product.
Positive control: independently counted repeated/reassociated selectors in
actual different-vote frames, including nonliteral votes and accepted submissions.
Negative control: deleting duplicate occurrences, treating all selector indices
as equally expensive, and publishing the ciphertext product itself as a handle.
PBT gate: reachable honest selector trees; three seeds, explicit mutations and
a deterministic backstop; exact syntax counts and executable nonce occurrence
bags only, never a claimed full-E decision procedure.
Trusted definitions: existing E/E0, expanded public frames, names/freshness,
acceptance, ciphertext grouping and global minimum recipes.
Reality oracle: direct selector traversal costs, fresh indexed nonce occurrences
and the existing E3 homomorphic value equation. No new cryptographic semantics.
Residual assumptions and unsupported cases: mixed products, remaining local
transport and the simultaneous expanded-frame induction remain open; this
claim is not final static equivalence or process secrecy.

representative, equal in both worlds under the two smaller-minimum hypotheses.
Every minimum mixed assembly has exactly one constructor occurrence and an
exact-size grouped representative. Its minimum competitors retain the honest

Formal oracle: planned generic mixed handle tools, expanded mixed compression
and minimum-origin theorems, plus kernel SPOTs and the public axiom audit.
Falsifier: a coherent two-constructor mixed tree whose grouped representative
is not smaller or changes a nonce, payload or honest index occurrence.
Positive control: mixed trees over actual partial/result handles and repeated
honest selectors, with explicit node counts and E3 values.
Negative control: strict compression with only one constructor, omission of
honest duplicates, and incoherent public keys.
PBT gate: reachable mixed trees, three mutation checks, three fixed seeds and

Trusted definitions: E/E0, actual expanded frames, numeric origins, opaque
protection, ciphertext groups and global minimum recipes.
Reality oracle: existing E3 equations, explicit traversal/node counts and
fresh indexed nonce occurrences; no new homomorphic semantics.
Residual assumptions and unsupported cases: one-constructor mixed payloads
need global zero-padded minima with published numeric handle costs. Remaining
local/successful transport and the simultaneous induction stay open.

closes this case using the exact forward/reverse smaller-minimum premises;

`expanded_minimum_mixed_combination_origin` retains its honest index bag,

The existing `constructedCount` definition and public-key agreement theorem

uses the least available numeric-handle cost for positive totals, and never
uses an empty object-language recipe. The same representative preserves padded
values in both accepted vote assignments. This should close the one-constructor
mixed multiplication case and permit all multiplication transport to assemble.
Status: conjectured.
Formal oracle: planned padded numeric-handle cost/realization, expanded padded
minimum and single-mixed transport declarations; kernel SPOTs and axiom audit.
Falsifier: a cheaper padded-equal public competitor, especially a published
numeric handle above one or a payload containing only zero.
Positive control: actual published zero removal beside a nonnumeric atom,
repeated atoms, and cheap published positive numerals.
Negative control: literal-only numeric costs, free empty all-zero payloads,
unpadded zero deletion, and a greedy numeric-handle choice.
PBT gate: numeric-handle addition skeleton costs versus independent exhaustive
multiplicity enumeration; fixed seeds, mutations and deterministic backstop.
Trusted definitions: E/E0, numeric-handle summaries and realized costs,
PaddedMinimalRecipe, actual accepted expanded frames and global minimum recipes.
Reality oracle: independent counted syntax, existing E0 zero equations and
actual published tally fixtures. No new cryptographic semantics.
Residual assumptions and unsupported cases: arbitrary minimum-atom and
smaller-minimum premises must be discharged at their callers. Remaining local
and successful-case transport and the global induction are still open.

## Fresh bound-name representative enquiry (2026-09-11)

Claim: every current Named process is structurally equivalent, using legal
same-sort alpha and evaluation contexts, to a representative whose bound names
avoid any given finite set. Freshening must retain the entire process syntax
through permutations and not change input labels or discard private values.
Status: conjectured.
Formal oracle: finite bound-name support, permutation laws, explicit fresh-index
witnesses and structural-induction construction of fresh representatives.
Falsifier: a fresh binder remains in the forbidden set, a nested binder captures
a renamed occurrence, a base/channel sort is mixed, or freshening substitutes a
public input label rather than renaming only bound process names.
Positive control: freshen nested mixed binders away from all names in a compound
input label and retain a secret-bearing active frame.
Negative control: retain the prior fixed-policy alpha-input counterexample and
reject a fresh choice that collides with a nested binder or label occurrence.
PBT gate: general structural kernel proofs and independent controls; no new
randomized cryptographic campaign or security inference from search failure.
Trusted definitions: Named's existing same-sort alpha and evaluation-context
rules, complete allNames support and explicit bound names. No new structural
or operational constructor is added to make the claim pass.
Reality oracle: Figure 3 bound-name alpha conversion and Definition 2 matching
of the same visible label under fresh bound-name representatives.
Residual assumptions and unsupported cases: coherent paired-frame freshening,
full source converse, named observations/admissibility, outer voter construction
and final weak labelled bisimilarity/secrecy.

## Equational process behavior enquiry (2026-09-11)

Claim: replacing every payload and guard term by a full-E equivalent term,
including under input binders, preserves guard truth and matches finite plain
process internal and visible steps modulo equational process congruence.
Status: conjectured. This is a supporting obligation for the evaluated
active-substitution interpretation, not an arbitrary Extended/Named converse.
Formal oracle: new SourceEquationalFormula, SourceEquationalProcesses and
operational transport modules; targeted Lean build and integrated audit.
Falsifier: a negative guard flips truth, a nested input captures a variable,
a parallel rearrangement loses a matching step, or an output silently changes
to an inequivalent payload/channel. Literal output labels need only carry
E-equivalent payloads; exact syntactic payload equality is deliberately stronger
than the candidate claim. Inputs should also admit exact-message matching.
Positive control: projection-equivalent messages, negative/conjunctive guards,
and communication whose receiver reuses the message beneath another input.
Negative control: different channels, branch polarity, inequivalent constants,
and syntactically different output labels despite an E-equivalent message.
PBT gate: structural congruence/operational proofs with independent kernel
controls, not a new difficult cryptographic conjecture or randomized campaign.
Trusted definitions: existing full EqE, binder substitution, Formula.Holds,
CoreStep/CoreVisible and existing parallel structural laws. No source rule or
cryptographic equation will be weakened or added.
Reality oracle: Figure 3's active-substitution Rewrite/Subst and ground guards;
substitution must act on the complete continuation and all observation fields.
Residual assumptions and unsupported cases: active constraints/existential
locals, arbitrary name/variable structural paths and canonical targets,
named observations/admissibility, outer voters and final weak bisimilarity.

Extension before the structural-preservation experiment: use the checked
parallel/E composite equivalence to define Extended.Realizes. Active x=M means
EqE(env x)(M.subst env); a restricted variable existentially chooses a ground
value. Candidate claim: every existing Extended.Structural derivation preserves
Realizes for every environment and resulting process. A smallest falsifier is
Alias with a message depending on an old variable, New-Par capturing an outer
variable, or SubstPlain under an environment that fails its active constraint.
Positive controls will realize a concrete let and a rewritten active payload;
negative controls will retain the active constraint and the syntactically
nonclosed Rewrite example. No universal solvability or Named converse is claimed.

Operational extension before coding: if a Realizes env p and an arbitrary
Extended.Reduction takes a to b, there should be a genuine Agent.Tau p q with
b.Realizes env q. Structural preservation and EvalEq step transport are the
oracles. A vacuous zero-step match is excluded by requiring one Tau; controls
must retain a private communication and its complete receiver payload.
This remains an interpretation theorem, without a Named alpha/label converse.

fst(pair(50,40)) dead-field collision while excluding essential-name collision.

## Concrete computational library validation (2026-09-12, in progress)

Goal: discharge section 4's library prerequisite before implementing the concrete
Helios attack and repair.
Claim: a pinned computational library can express adaptive ballot submission,
stateful acceptance and public observations, provide an exact probability theorem,
and supply reusable ElGamal/proof interfaces with audited assumptions.
Status: **machine-checked** selected interfaces, algebra adapter and finite
probability controls; **validated** fit for the initial development. VCVio is
selected. No computational attack or secrecy theorem is claimed.

Formal oracle: selected native-toolchain module builds and kernel axiom reports
in isolated archive copies under `tmp/concrete-helios/{VCVio,CatCrypt-core}`;
then a minimal ballot-game prototype in each framework.
Falsifier: a required imported theorem reaches an undeclared axiom, a public
transcript exposes prover randomness, the proposed game omits adaptive input or
rejection, or its probability is disconnected from the library semantics.
Positive control: an independently constructed accepted honest ballot and a
checked distinguishing observation. Negative control: replay rejection and a
non-distinguishing honest continuation, excluding universal rejection and
constant output. These prototype controls are planned, not yet checked.

Reality oracle: pinned VCVio ElGamal/SigmaProtocol and CatCrypt ElGamalDDH/
ChaumPedersen source; Smyth, *Replay attacks that violate ballot secrecy in
Helios*, sections 2.1–2.3 and 3.1.

Source findings: VCVio uses Mathlib module/group structures and separates public
commitments from private prover state. CatCrypt's Chaum–Pedersen message carries
private randomness internally; its visible-transcript theorem explicitly projects
it out. CatCrypt ElGamalDDH uses `CyclicGroup`, while its Chaum–Pedersen uses
`GroupParam`; `groupParamCyclic` and `elemPow_eq_groupExp` now connect them with checked
proofs. Both inspected encryption algorithms
sample all scalars, while Smyth's honest encryption samples nonzero scalars.
That distribution difference must be accounted for, not silently normalized away.
Smyth's verification hash covers proof commitments; adding voter/context binding
would change the vulnerable construction. The neutral-ciphertext attack concerns
at-most-one voting including abstention, with component weeding against earlier
ballots. Its collision conditions must appear in the probability calculation.

Pins: VCVio `6d5c7d502ad97f676293a84c3d364c518cbde117` (Lean 4.33.1);
CatCrypt-core `91410d23b34a886fcc35765d59a93565906bbe17` (Lean 4.30.0).
Copies are made with `git archive HEAD`; upstream tracked files and revisions,
main Lean 4.32.0, and the completed symbolic theorem remain unchanged.
Validation completed: native selected-module builds pass in both archives. The
four probe files in `docs/research/computational-probes/` check existing
cryptographic theorems and the group adapter, plus adaptive two-token board
experiments. Replay acceptance is 1 without weeding and 0 with it; an independently
chosen fresh token is accepted with probability 1; a blind fixed token is accepted
with probability 1/2. Rejection preserves state and fresh input updates it.
These are interface controls, not encrypted-ballot or Helios security claims.
CatCrypt callbacks use `SDistr` and cannot directly modify the board's private
heap. Kernel reports contain only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`,
or no axioms. The pinned CatCrypt build emits existing linter warnings; the
final local probes emit none. Logs: `tmp/concrete-helios/*-build.log`,
`*-interfaces.log`, `*-game.log`.

Decision: choose VCVio for its Mathlib algebra, adaptive oracle reductions,
random-oracle execution and explicit backend-relative efficiency interface.
CatCrypt's Chaum–Pedersen reuse is real, and its group integration obstacle is
now discharged; neither library supplies the complete Helios disjunction and
ballot privacy reduction. VCVio's convenient final ElGamal bound quantifies its
hardness premise over unrestricted adversaries, so it cannot be used unchanged
as a small PPT hardness assumption. Use explicit reductions and prove their
complexity. Structural query counts alone are not polynomial-time evidence.
The separate `computational/` package pins VCVio and Lean 4.33.1; the main
symbolic package stays on Lean 4.32.0.

Failures: concurrent Mathlib cache clients collided on `curl.cfg`; a sequential
retry passed. CatCrypt's first probability proof over-unfolded the semantics;
its replacement uses `prTrue_bind_sample`. A broad `eq_comm` simplification
looped and was scoped to the final heap marginal. These are infrastructure and
proof-engineering failures, not false security claims. The initial package name
needed Lake's manifest Name encoding; a plain identifier fixes it.
Residual: exact protocol model, attack, repair and computational secrecy remain
outstanding; integrated project/PDF validation follows this increment.

## Actual ballot Σ-protocol results (2026-09-12)

Claim: the actual historical nonzero-coin disjunctive proof has perfect
completeness, special soundness, and honest-verifier simulation within
statistical distance `3/|F|`. Status: **machine-checked** in the root build;
integration and PDF audit recorded separately below.

construction to the current repaired ballot constructor. The extractor takes
two accepting transcripts with a common statement and commitments and distinct
total challenges, selects a branch with distinct challenges, and recovers its
bit and nonce. It is installed in VCVio's actual `SigmaProtocol` interface.

The simulator uses full-field challenge and response draws.
`ballotSigma_full_hvzk` proves exact equality for the full-field reference
prover. `nonzeroRefill_eq` derives the actual nonzero marginal from a uniform
draw with refill at zero. `sampleNonzero_uniform_tv_le` and

changing that prover's sampling distribution.

nonce; literal commitments and responses match modulo-23 exponentiation.

invalid witness. `nonzero_transcript_ne_full_simulator` retains the false-claim

### Next quantitative candidate, not a checked bound

For `repairedSubmission_joint_extract_le`, the proposed route is a small-mass
bound for original paths whose selected context has low conditional acceptance.

conditional acceptance is below delta should be at most delta. Union-bound the
three families of Q ordinals, then retain the uniform equal-challenge loss in
each independent completion conditional on the same original path.

selection theorem alone does not supply these. The pinned VCVio

are the first falsifiers; preserve the disjoint-marginal counterexample and a
reachable positive shared-context case. No generic transfer framework or new
library dependency is proposed. Keep this under the existing extraction item in

attacker-submission acceptance probability and ℓ=9/(q−1)+90/q. The concrete bound
retains this honest-rejection and simulation loss. δ is any ENNReal analysis

Goal: derive the concrete finite replay cache size from its miss log and expose

supported execution preserves

empty initialization therefore gives equal cache/log lengths and at most n+15
entries each for the actual source. A complete full hash key packs into exactly
eight group elements and decodes back exactly, in documented field order.
Status: conjectured, before formal edits.
Falsifier: a preloaded one-entry cache with empty log disproves unqualified
cache/log equality even for an empty program. A repeated hit must not increase
either count. Dropping or swapping the generator/public-key fields must fail an

could pass a round trip.

source storage corollaries, full-key pack/unpack and fixed-size theorems.

sizes; directed duplicate-hit and dropped-state mutations; literal full key
[1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8]. This is an element-record layout, not yet a bit codec or cost
certificate. Primitive group/scalar encodings, local costs and machine adequacy
remain separate obligations; do not silently assume them.

submission-history enumeration preserving rejection and finite bit-length
fixtures around powers of two. Positive controls must retain accepted board
append, rejected unchanged board, and a small uniform tag; negative controls
must detect appending on rejection, dropping a prefix entry, and treating every
uniform tag as one bit. A codec/cost theorem is not to be assumed from these

## Uniform operand codec enquiry and narrow backend comparison

The previous goal turn was progress: output bounds and the tape-width
counterexample were integrated and audited. The next obstacle is concrete
operand representation, not another event-count bound.

Re-read pinned `VCVioComplexity/Backend/TuringMachine.lean` and its README against
the current need. Its closed grammar has fixed-width BitVec and unary natural
representations, but no binary-natural constructor; it has individual exact
machine certificates and lacks generic machine composition and oracle-machine
adequacy. Importing the optional package would not discharge these obligations.
Its pair codec also differs from the upstream machine pairing. No dependency,
reference checkout or upstream pin is changed.

Comparison: extending that optional backend now would require representation
and machine-composition work before an operand can be encoded. A narrower root
implementation can use Mathlib's existing binary-natural conversions and an
explicit delimiter/length prefix for the actual uniform range/answer pair.
This chooses binary operand records on words and preserves the existing typed
oracle semantics. A later machine adapter must implement these exact words and
operations; no arbitrary encoder or cost/adequacy certificate is supplied by a
caller. This is an operand codec, not a new execution framework.

Candidate: encode natural n as a unary prefix for the *binary width*, a zero
delimiter and the little-endian binary digits of n. Length is 2*Nat.size n+1.
A prefix decoder must recover n and the untouched suffix and accept only this
canonical encoding. A uniform event encodes the range index n and answer a≤n
in sequence; its complete decoder must reject leftover data, noncanonical
padding, truncation and a>n. Round trips alone are insufficient: successful
decoding must reconstruct the exact input encoding.
Status: conjectured before edits.
Falsifiers: leading-width truncation, a trailing zero in a positive binary
payload, a forged answer above the declared range, and ignored trailing bits.
Positive controls: literal empty-range event (n=0,a=0), coin replies and wide
power-of-two tags. Formal oracle: Mathlib Nat.bits and Nat.bit, prefix reconstruction,
actual `unifSpec` dependent event round trips and exactness. Reality oracle:
independent Python bit fixtures, malformed-word enumeration and mutated decoders.
Local machine costs, scalar/group codecs, full tape encoding/execution and
adequacy remain outstanding even if these codec claims check.

### Checked canonical uniform-event bit codec

Status: machine-checked in targeted builds; final integrated audit follows.
`uniformNatEncode` prefixes Mathlib little-endian binary digits with one true
bit per digit and a false delimiter. The prefix represents binary width, not
the natural number in unary. The reader folds Mathlib's Nat.bit constructor;
`bitsValue_bits` proves inversion by existing binary induction. The initial
candidate notation `ofBits` was replaced by this explicit fold after inspection
showed that no such named conversion was present in the imported Nat interface.
No noncomputable finite enumeration or assumed codec is used.

`uniformNatRead_encode` preserves every supplied suffix. `_exact` proves that a
successfully read word is exactly the canonical encoding plus that suffix.
Truncated width/payloads and noncanonical padded digits reject. `UniformEvent`
is the actual dependent uniform index/answer type from pinned unifSpec.
`uniformEventDecode_encode` and `_exact` establish complete event round trips
and accepted-word canonicality; the decoder checks the answer range and rejects
trailing data. `uniformNatEncode_length` and `uniformEventEncode_length` derive
2*size(n)+1 and 2*size(n)+2*size(a)+2 bits respectively. These are the lengths of
actual executable bit-list encoders, not synthetic operation counters.

Controls: literal zero and both coin replies fix the framing and operand order;
a natural-prefix fixture keeps the exact suffix. Empty/truncated frames, padded
zero, an answer above its declared range and a trailing bit reject. The existing
supported wide-tag tape family now has a corresponding event encoding of exactly
2k+4 bits and an exact decode. It retains rather than removes the operand-width
dependence exposed by the checked count-only counterexample.

Independent gate `scripts/check-helios-uniform-codec.py`: all 2,145 events with
range indices 0–64 and valid answers, three suffix fixtures per natural read,
and all 8,191 words of lengths 0–12. Exactly 58 enumerated words are accepted and
each equals the independently re-encoded event. Padding, trailing-input and range
mutants are detected before the main gate. Deterministic, no seeds, zero failures
and zero gaveUp. This validates finite parser fixtures, not Lean extraction,
cryptographic distributions or computational cost.

Failures were proof engineering: Nat.bits_append_bit argument order, overloaded
Option monadic bind normalization, and redundant simplifier arguments after
reducing the codec's imports to OracleSpec and Nat.Size. Explicit bind reduction
and the minimal imports resolve these; no statement or malformed-input policy
was weakened. The codec does not import protocol/control modules. Its controls
separately connect to the actual supported tape counterexample.

Trusted definitions: bit framing, existing Nat binary operations, unifSpec's
range/answer type, and Lean's list/Option semantics. This is an internal uniform
operand record, not a changed ballot wire format or random-oracle distribution.
The pinned optional backend comparison is recorded above; no Lake dependency,
upstream checkout or revision changed. Scalar/group codecs, full saved-tape
framing and execution integration, concrete local costs and machine adequacy
remain required. Neither termination nor exact decoding gives a PPT certificate.
Full public election/trustee integration, earlier/interleaved queries, DDH and
parametrized all-PPT ballot secrecy remain open.

coinSpec provides fair Bool draws. OracleComp is an inductive, terminating free
monad; its coin response type is finite. Candidate obstruction: every such coin
program has a finite maximum query bound, and every output probability times
2^bound is a natural. Consequently no such program samples a prime-sized range
q>2 exactly, since a uniform point would have probability 1/q.

This is a falsifiable representation claim, not a privacy claim. Formal oracle:
actual OracleComp coinSpec induction, its total-query predicate, VCVio probability
semantics and Nat prime divisibility. Reality oracle: exhaustive small binary
trees and literal two-bit modulo/rejection tables, detecting a claimed uniform
modulo sampler and a false bounded exact sampler before general proof work.
Controls must retain fair coin sampling and exact power-of-two sampling, so the
obstruction cannot be explained by an inability to sample anything uniformly.
Status: conjectured before edits.

Narrow alternatives: an exact rejection sampler with potentially unbounded
running time needs a representation beyond terminating coin-only OracleComp;
a finite cutoff sampler remains in that representation but adds an explicit
failure/statistical-distance term. The pinned coinductive DynSystem API describes
finite trajectories and probabilistic handlers; source inspection does not yet
supply an exact rejection sampler, first-hitting-time proof or bit-machine cost
adapter for this protocol. No framework migration or new dependency is proposed.
First check the obstruction, then choose and prove a local realization while
preserving the ideal protocol law and accounting for approximation/runtime
explicitly. Do not silently add an abort to the historical public observations.

### Checked finite-program obstruction and selected adapter

The intervening migration-status turn revalidated the root build but discharged
no further secrecy obligation (no progress on the active proof). This turn
resumed the failed targeted fair-bit check and changed the authoritative proof.

Claim/status: machine-checked. `coinProgram_has_bound` derives a finite maximum
coin count for every actual terminating OracleComp coinSpec program. For any
such bound n, `coinProgram_dyadic` derives a natural numerator k with
Pr[P=x] * 2^n = k. `coinProgram_not_prime_uniform` quantifies over every program,
point and prime q>2 and excludes mass 1/q, deriving the bound internally. It
therefore excludes an exact coin-only realization of the historical scalar
sampler. It does not exclude unbounded rejection in another execution model.

Formal oracle: `CoinDenominators.lean` and `CoinDenominatorsControls.lean`, built
with `lake build ExplainableCrypto.Helios.Computational.CoinDenominatorsControls`.

pairs, actual modulo-three masses 1/2 and 1/4, and impossibility for every
coin-only Fin 3 program. Standard axiom reports only; no caller runtime or
correspondence premise. The first failed proof was proof engineering:
typeclass inference for classical equality and ENNReal inverse normalization.
Explicit local equality and arithmetic lemmas close it without raised limits.

Independent reality/refutation oracle: the deterministic rational fixture script
checks all distinct binary-tree point masses through depth four (2,3,5,9,17

zero-cutoff-failure mutations. Failures=0, gaveUp=0; no random seeds or discards.

Failure classification: representation obstruction / false exact finite-sampling
claim. OracleComp's inductive finite-branching structure is load-bearing. No
cryptographic equation, attack capability, public observation, rejection policy
or freshness condition changed; symbolic B1–B10 and prior independent controls
are retained.

Narrow comparison and decision: exact rejection requires potentially unbounded
tails beyond this coin-only representation. A finite rejection cutoff needs a
loss and specified fallback. The selected next route is extra fair bits followed
by modulo reduction, with explicit statistical error. It returns an in-range

This closes the representation decision, not the fair-bit adapter or secrecy.

## Extra-bit modulo sampler enquiry

Previous goal turn: progress; the fair-bit obstruction and controls were
integrated and audited. Candidate next construction: actual independent fair
bits, mapped by Mathlib's computable binary-digit equivalence to Fin(2^w), then
reduced modulo positive range q. For M=2^w and residue y<q, the conjectured mass
is (M/q + indicator(y<M%q))/M. This exposes the bias rather than asserting exact
uniformity. A refill of the incomplete final block with an independent ideal
uniform q draw should have exactly the ideal law and couple the actual sampler
to it with error at most (M%q)/M. Width q.size+λ should bound error by 2^(-λ).
These candidates are unproved before edits.

Formal oracle: the actual coin-only sampler, pinned VCVio's Fin.mOfFn probability
lemma, Mathlib finFunctionFinEquiv, residue sums and existing TV bind/event
bounds. Reality oracle: exhaustive rational masses from literal fair-bit words,
all finite outcome events for small ranges, and adversarial boundary widths.
Smallest falsifiers: two bits modulo three for exact uniformity; duplicated
bits or a missing high bit for the proposed law; too few bits for the selected
security-parameter bound. Detect these mutants before general proof work.
No protocol equation, ideal sampler, public observation or rejection behavior
changes. Contextual/adaptive transfer and actual local execution costs must be
proved, not made caller premises. This enquiry remains inside task list §4.

### Checked sampler, adaptive transfer and actual fair-bit extractor

Status: machine-checked. `FairBitSampler` implements actual independent fair
bits through VCVio's Fin.mOfFn and Mathlib's computable finFunctionFinEquiv.
The power-of-two index distribution is exact. For M=2^w and positive q, the
actual modulo sampler's residue mass is (M/q+indicator(y<M%q))/M. A proof-only
refill of the last incomplete block has exactly the ideal uniform law; coupling
bounds TV by (M%q)/M. Width q.size+s gives error ≤2^(-s), after any common SPMF
continuation, and uses at most q.size+s actual coin requests. No arithmetic or
machine-cost claim follows from that query count.

`FairBitUniformOracle` replaces actual adaptive finite-range requests. For any
original total bound N it proves complete-output TV ≤N*2^(-s). Independent
support induction derives reachable-output preservation. The same law gives
Boolean event error and an ENNReal truncated-subtraction bound. No range-size or
caller-supplied correspondence premise is introduced. A local proof-only sum
of the two oracle specifications reuses VCVio's lift-preservation and convex TV
lemmas; there is no new probability semantics or runtime backend.

The actual extractor was still OracleComp(wrappedSpec(ZMod q)), not ProbComp.
The first direct application failed by representation mismatch. The existing
ballotForkEntropyImpl and ballotFork_entropy_eval already lower its separate
index/scalar requests with exact whole-output law. The computable prime scalar
sampler derives one query per handler step, retaining the 16(m+19) total bound.
`PrimeFairBits` reuses this adapter rather than assuming a missing correspondence.

`repairedSubmissionFairBits_extract` now implements all those requests with
actual fair bits. `_tv_le` compares its full output law, including failure, to
the proved ideal extractor within 16(m+19)*2^(-s). `_valid` derives acceptance,
all three covered witnesses and supported original ideal source origin (g≠0).
`_consistent` retains aggregate nonce addition and integer at-most-one under
generator injectivity and prime q>2. `_le` retains the original lower bound with
its honest-rejection, simulation and challenge-collision losses, then subtracts
ofReal(16(m+19)*2^(-s)). Hash budget n, total budget m and δ have the same roles
as before; s is the explicit implementation slack. Returned results/witnesses
are the actual algorithm's outputs. No new public abort, rejection, crypto
equation, freshness policy or cryptographic assumption is added. The ideal
historical game remains fixed; implementation approximation stays explicit.

Independent controls: literal binary digit order, exact range-four uniformity,
range-three/slack-three probabilities 11/32 and 10/32 (still biased), and its
five-bit/1/8 bounds. An actual two-request adaptive program retains its first
answer, selects the next range from it, meets the two-step error bound and
preserves that selected range. Earlier obstruction, nonce/state/rejection and
replay controls remain in the root build.

Refutation/reality oracle: `check-helios-modulo-sampler.py` checks 1,377 actual
finite-word point masses, 4,590 distinguishing events, six adaptive full-pair
cases and 3,341 range-width/slack boundaries. It detects exact-modulo,
reused-bit, missing-high-bit and unspent-slack mutants before the main finite
checks. All failures=0 and gaveUp=0; the deterministic fixtures use no random
seeds or discarded implications. These checks supplement, not replace, the
quantified Lean law and adaptive proof.

Proof failures: explicit finite-sum instantiation, dependent Fin.cons typing,
classical finite support, ENNReal coercion/finiteness and arithmetic normalization
were proof engineering. The TV convexity helper requires a probability monad
with a support lift; attempting to use raw SPMF/PMF directly lacked that API.
Reusing the existing sum-oracle lift resolves it without adding an instance or
weakening the conclusion. No limits, axioms or upstream APIs were changed.

## Concrete key-comparison execution enquiry

Previous goal turn: progress; complete output records and actual runtime data
bounds were integrated and audited. Computational milestones remain 2/3; Step 3
is active. The next named obligation is local execution for finite cache lookup.

Current source inspection confirms the optional pinned VCVio backend has no
inhabited general machine composition or oracle compiler/adequacy theorem. Its
pairing differs from the upstream machine pairing. Adding that dependency would
not itself implement the present cache operations. Mathlib already provides the
concrete TM2 stack-machine semantics and its TM1 translation. A narrow alternative
is to implement required bit operations directly in that existing machine model,
with finite alphabets/control and actual transition-count proofs. This does not
supply a quantitative TM0 translation or a whole-extractor PPT certificate.

Candidate: a two-stack bit comparator reads one head from each stack, continues
only on matching nonempty heads, and halts on a mismatch or end marker. Its
actual run halts within left-word length plus one transitions, and its terminal
finite control gives exactly word equality. Canonical full-key injectivity then
connects this execution to original typed-key equality; the prior key-size theorem
derives a modulus-width bound. No callback can inspect a whole word in one step:
all transition functions range only over the finite pair of optional bits.

Falsifiers: a strict prefix accepted as equality, a late differing bit ignored,
an empty pair rejected, a transition count independent of equal-prefix length,
or hidden unbounded state computation. Formal oracle: Mathlib TM2.step and
iteration, then the existing actual full-key encoder and size theorem. Reality
oracle: independent list equality and longest-common-prefix accounting on all
short Boolean words, first detecting a prefix-accepting mutant. Positive and
negative Lean controls must include equal, differing and strict-prefix words.
Status before formal edits: conjectured execution/correspondence. Cache parsing,
iteration/insertion, arithmetic, saved-context execution, whole-machine adequacy
and the full-election secrecy reduction remain open. Pins remain unchanged.

## Concrete natural-prefix parser: checked result

Status: machine-checked, integrated and audited.
`NatPrefixMachine.total_run` covers every raw word: some fuel ≤3*word.length+3
reaches halted control, and output equals the original `uniformNatRead` result
mapped to literal binary digits and untouched suffix. There is no well-formedness,
accepted-decoding or structural-presentation premise. Rejected inputs return no
readout. Successful output consists of bit stacks, not a free Nat-decoding step.

`encoded_run` has exact full final configuration for every natural n and suffix,
with sufficient fuel 3*n.size+3: suffix retained, binary digits in original order,
count/scratch empty, successful halt. General `no_delimiter_run`, `truncated_run`
and `noncanonical_run` prove the three rejection families. `NatPrefixFormat`
connects the last-bit canonicality check to the original reader using its existing
encode/exact theorems; the original codec source is unchanged. The all-word proof
classifies every word into these cases, so the rejection controls are not the
only evidence for malformed-input handling.

`cache_header_run` extracts the actual encoded cache's outer count prefix and
parses it while preserving every remaining entry/framing bit. `source_cache_header`
derives fuel ≤3*(n+15).size+3 from supported execution of the explicit-nonce finite
logged source and its per-view hash-query bound n. It returns exactly the binary
digits of the actual entry count. No cache-size, parser-correctness or cost
certificate is supplied by a caller.

The machine has four binary stacks, three labels and optional-bit local memory.
It pushes one width marker per header bit, consumes one payload bit per marker,
checks the final payload bit, and reverses scratch into output. All local
callbacks have finite domains. Any interpretation of output bits as a Nat is only
a semantic specification, not a hidden machine instruction.

against separately implemented integer prefix decoding, preserving suffixes and

rewrites. Literal configuration controls use the general run theorem rather than

## Linked length-controlled field-reader enquiry

Previous goal turn: progress; counter integration and visual review completed.
Milestones remain 2/3 complete; Step 3 active. The next named obligation is
execution of a length-controlled field read on the existing four bit stacks.
Candidate: retain a canonical binary count, consume one input bit per decrement,
reject exhausted input immediately, and restore the collected field in order.
Successful runs must return exactly the requested prefix and unchanged suffix;
short inputs must halt in time polynomial in input length and counter bit width,
not in the numeric declared length. Empty fields must succeed without consuming
input. Counter scratch must be cleared between iterations.

The existing counter theorem ends at halt. A data handoff alone does not execute
its caller. The narrow alternative is a syntax-directed label/return redirection
on the same TM2 stacks and local memory, with a checked bounded-run transfer.
This is required to link the counter into the field loop and subsequently the
prefix reader; it does not introduce a new machine representation or dependency.
A halted source run may contain padded steps, so the transfer must derive a
possibly shorter run rather than incorrectly execute the caller during padding.

Falsifiers: reversed field, lost suffix, zero consuming an input bit, short input
accepted, or a huge declared length forcing unary expansion before rejection.
Formal oracle: actual TM2 transitions, complete final configurations and derived
fuel bounds. Reality oracle: independent integer length checks and list slicing,
with reversed-output and padded-truncation mutants. Status before edits:
conjectured. Whole-record parsing, cache scans and all-PPT secrecy remain open.

## Archive accumulation enquiry

Previous goal turn: progress; explicit outer-state preservation and one executed
record iteration were integrated and audited. Milestones remain 2/3; Step 3
active. The archive is currently unchanged, so another iteration would lose the
previous field unless a boundary-preserving accumulation operation is supplied.

Choose to record the consumed original input bits, including each existing
length prefix, in reverse on the archive stack. This retains the original
framing instead of introducing a second field codec or recomputing lengths from
parsed payloads. Each successful input pop copies its bit to archive; failed
pops copy nothing. The actual parser's input-pop callbacks store the popped head
in finite local memory, so copying needs no unbounded callback or extra memory.

input nor reads/writes archive and that input-pop callbacks store the head.
Derive that check for the concrete program; do not leave it as a caller premise.

Candidate: every recorded run matches the original complete work state and
control with the same TM2 fuel; original input equals a consumed prefix followed
by residual input, and archive becomes reverse(consumed)++oldArchive. Instantiate
this on successful/rejected field iterations. A successful iteration must append
exactly E(|field|)++field, then clear output in charged control flow so all work
stacks are empty for reuse. Malformed input must retain the original rejection.

Falsifiers: recording an absent input bit, omitting the length prefix, reversing
field order, letting recorded archive influence original control, or clearing
output before preserving field boundaries. Formal oracle: actual TM2.step,
structural program checks and complete configuration equalities. Reality oracle:
independently decoded consumed-prefix lengths and literal six-stack fixtures,
with missing-prefix and erased-archive mutants. Status before edits: conjectured.

open; this recorder alone is not the full record parser or all-PPT secrecy proof.

## Cache insertion: original framing writer enquiry

Previous goal turn: progress; complete source-cache lookup was integrated and
audited. Milestones remain 2/3; Step 3 active. Source inspection confirms that
AList.insert prepends the new pair and erases the first old pair with that key;
it is not in-place replacement. The actual finite raw/logged/programmed handlers
insert only in their cache-miss branches. Retain exact AList semantics when
connecting a resulting machine to these source branches; any specialized
fresh-insertion premise must be derived from actual lookup, not supplied as an
adequacy certificate. General replacement is not itself a secrecy requirement.

Concrete current obstruction: lookup only consumes existing record prefixes.
Constructing a new entry/cache requires computing field lengths and emitting
E(n)=1^size(n)++0::bits(n), including an incremented outer count. No existing
machine writes this format. Treating a complete pre-encoded entry or new count
as an uncharged callback would leave the insertion cost gap open.

Candidate: a five-stack TM2 consumes a loaded payload and builds its original
length-framed encoding on a destination suffix. During payload collection it
increments a canonical binary counter through actual carry/restore operations;
then restores payload order, writes the binary digits, delimiter and width ones.
Its prefix-only entry point writes E(n) from n.bits. Both runs clear workspace
and charge the complete traversal, carry operations and control transfers.
This writer is required by the named CacheInsertMachine obligation. Do not
introduce a generic encoder compiler or a replacement cache representation.

Formal oracle: BitIncrementMachine.run and FrameWriteMachine.run/prefix_run
(planned), then original typed field bounds. Falsifiers: incorrect carry at a
power-of-two boundary, reversal of a nonpalindromic payload or suffix, counting
bits in unary rather than binary, omission of the zero-length delimiter, or
incorrect workspace after a linked increment. Reality oracle: independent
integer bit_length/binary-digit framing and full literal stack snapshots.

the general proof. Status before edits: conjectured. Whole insertion, initial

## Scalar range-reduction execution enquiry

Previous goal turn: progress; cached-answer parsing and the existing source
handler were integrated/audited. Milestones 2/3; Step 3 active.

Source inspection: sampleFairBitIndex reads width-many coins into a finite
function; sampleFairBitModulo applies x.val % q as host arithmetic. The cache
writer's a.val.bits input therefore is not yet derived from executed sampling.
This is a missing implementation/cost correspondence, not a false sampler law.
The existing TV bound and exact ideal protocol remain unchanged.

Candidate route: binary long division processes the sampled word from most
significant to least significant bit, retaining remainder r<q. Each step forms
2r+b<2q and needs at most one guarded subtraction of q. Repeated subtraction
of q from the whole sampled value would require up to 2^width/q iterations and
is unsuitable for the required polynomial bit cost. No framework migration or
new cost-certificate assumption is justified.

Immediate candidate: a finite-control binary stack program computes guarded
subtraction on little-endian words, preserving the right operand and retaining
the original left operand on underflow. A successful difference is canonical;
all scratch stacks clear. This is the arithmetic step needed by that named
range-reduction obligation, not complete modular sampling or a PPT theorem.
Formal oracle: planned BinarySubtractMachine.run and numeric interpretation law.
Falsifiers: borrow propagation across zeros, zero/equal operands, asymmetric
lengths, noncanonical high zeros, loss/reversal of the retained modulus, or
returning wrapped underflow. Reality oracle: independently computed integer
subtraction and binary strings. Run exhaustive mutation fixtures before proof.
Residual: link repeated long-division steps to actual sampled bits, derive
width/remainder invariants and costs, then scalar loading/driver correspondence;
all broader execution and all-PPT obligations remain in task list.md.

Status of this formal increment: machine-checked, integrated/audited;
independent fixtures validated on the stated scope. `BinarySubtractMachine.run` covers every pair of
raw little-endian bit words. It performs binary borrow, retains the right word,
clears scratch and returns canonical X-Y digits when Y≤X, otherwise the exact
original left word. The full transition bound is 3*(|x|+|y|)+5, independent of
represented integer magnitudes. A private balance identity derives the borrow
flag; the proof also derives canonical trimming, rather than assuming it.

`remainder_step` includes the actual shift/zero handling followed by subtraction.
For loaded canonical r/q and r<q, it returns bits((2r+b)%q), retains q and clears
workspace within 6*q.size+9 transitions. Its flag records whether subtraction
was taken; false is a valid division-update outcome. This discharges C6's first
local arithmetic acceptance condition only. The repeated division loop,
coin-to-word loading, scalar handoff, total cost and broader machine adequacy
remain open. No sampler/game definition or sampling-loss theorem changed.

this extension passed before the remainder-step theorem was attempted. Expected
values use independent integer subtraction/modulo and binary strings. Six Lean
controls cover borrow, padded underflow, padded equality, nonpalindromic six,
17 mod 11 and zero. Failures/gaveUp are zero, exhaustive with no random seeds.
Trusted semantics: Mathlib TM2, ordinary binary value/encoding and its finite
Boolean carry callbacks. No arithmetic host callback chooses the subtraction.

### Same-original-path extraction failure: next enquiry

Status: conjectured; no failure or polynomial-time theorem is claimed yet.
The next named C10 obligation is `ElectionDDHSource.prefix_failure_le`.
For a fixed original path outside the existing low-context event, the checked
three-attempt theorem gives success at least ε³, where ε = (δ-1/q) with
truncated subtraction. Repeat only those residual attempts k times, retaining
the original prefix regardless of success. Candidate accepted-prefix failure
bound: 3(N+1)δ + (1-ε³)^k. The construction must account for missing probability
mass as well as an explicit `none` result; prove losslessness where used.
Its witness correctness must still reference the same retained output, and its
cost must include preparation and all replayed requests.

Falsifiers: resample the original path; condition its output distribution on
success; reuse dependent residual randomness as if independent; silently drop
nontermination; omit the low-context event. A finite exact-probability control
must separate same-path repetition from independent-original resampling.
The formal oracle is the actual finite repetition of `ballotJointReplayAtPath`,
using the existing conditional bound and context loss. Reuse pinned VCVio bind
probability lemmas; no new cryptographic library or oracle model is needed.

Quantitative boundary: choosing negligible δ does not automatically give a
polynomial repetition count, since ε may then be negligibly small. The eventual
security argument must choose δ and k with explicit advantage and cost bounds
(for example against a hypothesized inverse-polynomial distinguishing gap).
No uniform negligible extraction-failure claim with polynomial cost is assumed.

### C5 oracle-port replacement: enquiry

Previous goal turn: progress (finite-control interface/canary integrated/audited).
Goal: replace the atomic raw-port update's unimplemented word movement with

Concrete obstruction: BitCopyMachine prepends to an existing destination; it

representation/adapter mismatch, not a false cryptographic theorem. Retain a
literal checked counterexample. The copy also uses Option Bool local memory,
whereas the caller's Fin-valued memory must survive. A small product-memory
frame and the existing stack/return adapters address these exact mismatches.

that duplication; reuse the checked copy run and keep one implementation.

Formal oracle intended: BitPortTransfer.run, its negative append control, a
memory-frame run theorem, and an actual-resume theorem for arbitrary caller
configuration/destination/answer with the layout and frame derived internally.
Smallest falsifiers: nonempty old destination, nonpalindromic answer, nonempty
other caller stacks, or changed caller memory. Independent oracle: direct
three-stack finite-state runs over bounded words, detecting append-instead-of-
replace and order/erasure defects. Empty scratch is initialized in the constructed
private transfer workspace; the response is the word delivered by the oracle
on its dedicated input port. This proves TM2 word movement only. Standard
open-oracle tape translation, its quantitative adequacy and scalar/codec handler
integration remain C5/C8 obligations; do not claim a TM0 bound from TM2 ticks.


### C5 actual request/response transfer and successor workspace

Claim: actual TM2 request/response routines realize the raw interface's successor
state for arbitrary caller configuration, selected ports, return address and
answer, with all other caller stacks/memory preserved and private workspace empty
after completion. The request phase completes before the answer is selected.
Status: machine-checked in targeted builds; integration evidence follows below.
Formal oracle: `BitOraclePortTransfer.hash_transfer` and `.coin_transfer`.
`request_state` establishes the complete actual outgoing configuration; native
`deliver` hands its received word to the consuming response routine. No layout,
source-extraction, frame or transition-count premise is supplied by the caller.
`start_original`, `start_private` and `request_start` identify the constructed
physical stack contents. `run_resume` proves the exact high-level `resume` state.

Reuse and costs: `BitPortTransfer.run` clears the old destination and links the
existing BitCopyMachine run, costing at most |old|+2|word|+4 TM2 ticks.
`consume_run` additionally erases the private source, costing at most
|old|+3|word|+4. `TM2MemoryFrame.statement`/`.tick`/`.run` preserve saved finite
local memory with identical transition counts; the existing TM2StackFrame and
TM2ReturnLink supply stack placement and return linkage. One primary copy
implementation serves both outbound preservation and inbound consumption.
For a clean private I/O port, request preparation costs at most 2|request|+4.
Together with one native oracle event and response loading, the derived bound is
9*(1+|request|+|oldDestination|+|answer|); a coin similarly costs at most
9*(2+|oldDestination|). These are TM2 ticks plus native events, not TM0 steps.
Native oracle word delivery remains the external primitive; this does not
implement the cryptographic hash or its scalar encoding.

Failed approaches retained: (1) append-copy instead of replacement is a checked
representation mismatch, `BitPortTransfer.append_is_not_replacement`. (2) Keeping
a private answer copy across calls leaves an uncharged old-port length in the
next request. This is an insufficient workspace/resource invariant, demonstrated
by `BitPortTransferControls.uncleared_port_not_free`. The final inbound routine
erases that copy and derives empty workspace, enabling successive calls without
that assumption. This strengthens the private-state invariant; it changes no
public protocol field or cryptographic assumption. A dirty scratch word also
changes the copied value; every constructed start supplies empty scratch.

memory values), 3969 composed aliased-port hash cases and 126 coin cases.
It detects append, one-pass and source-erasure mutants and dirty scratch.
Failures and gaveUp are zero. These are bounded interpreter fixtures; they do
not validate arbitrary standard-machine compilation or the Helios scalar codec.

## C5 enquiry: compose the actual open-machine phases (2026-09-14)

Goal: assemble the checked port routines into one finite-control transition
system and connect successive source instructions to its execution.
Candidate claim: every finite raw source execution has the same ordered native
queries and complete boundary configurations in the assembled machine, with
linear transfer overhead in the existing raw charge. The transition function
must contain neither residual OracleComp programs nor host word-length loops.
Status: conjectured. First obligation: derive first-completion phase execution
inside the actual loop; padded halted subroutine ticks must not trigger another
native query. Then compose source instructions and their resource bounds.
Falsifier: an empty request that emits an extra query during padded preparation,
or two aliased hash calls whose second query reads stale private workspace.
Formal oracle: planned `BitOracleLoop.step`, `.run`, phase-execution and
source-correspondence declarations. Reality oracle: independent finite-state
execution with literal expected query traces, complete caller state and empty
private ports; mutate dispatch and response cleanup. Reuse the checked transfer
routines and their independent word fixtures.
Residual boundary: arbitrary raw hash responses have unbounded length. A fixed
micro-step budget cannot follow from the number of source instructions alone.
Use per-response execution bounds; do not assume a uniform response bound until
the actual scalar encoding derives it. Source correspondence and standard
oracle-tape quantitative adequacy remain distinct C5 obligations. C6–C8 and C12
remain open; this enquiry does not assert polynomial-time security.


C5 assembled-loop result: targeted machine-checked evidence

`BitOracleLoop.step` now dispatches fixed finite-control commands, advances the
actual request/response TM2 programs, issues native queries and returns to the
caller. Its state stores caller/transfer configurations and finite port indices;
it stores no residual program or unbounded host callback. The transition function
contains no word-length loop or fuel selection. `run` is external micro-step
observation. `request_run` derives a first-completion observation without issuing
a query; `response_run` proves empty private ports before projecting the exact
caller successor. `hash_issue`, `hash_cycle` and `coin_cycle` connect dispatch,
actual queries, answer-dependent continuation execution and the complete return.
Their bound includes dispatch/native/return steps: at most eleven times the
raw charge. Request and destination may alias.

steps gives exactly the source query tree with its complete caller-state output.

execution correspondence or a standard-machine certificate as a premise.

variable answer lengths, early-fuel and missing-halt mutations.

Representation comparison: the raw request/answer interface remains unchanged.
A proof-level bounded-answer adapter restricts native output words to the stated
encoded-response length, while preserving every raw request. This makes the
needed contract inspectable without changing machine instructions or dropping
malformed attacker requests. An alternative unrestricted-answer theorem would
need answer-dependent stopping/probability semantics or tail bounds, adding work
unneeded when the actual scalar codec has a deterministic width bound. Neither
route removes the obligation to derive that bound from the actual handler.

## C5 enquiry: quantitative reuse of Mathlib's stack-to-tape translation (2026-09-14)

Goal: derive execution costs for the existing TM2-to-TM1 translation, a required
part of standard oracle-tape adequacy. Preserve its program and upstream pin.
Candidate claim: a TM2 statement with maximum a stack actions on any branch,
starting with every stack length ≤H, executes in the existing translated TM1
program in at most 1+a(2(H+a)+2) TM1 ticks and preserves `TM2to1.TrCfg`.
Status: conjectured. The bound includes growth by earlier pushes, outward/top
handling, return and dispatch. TM1 statements still have fixed finite syntax;
conversion to primitive tape-step costs and native oracle I/O remain separate.
Falsifier: a long stack disproves constant per-stack-operation time; pushing
before a later operation disproves a bound that ignores within-statement growth.
Formal oracle: planned quantitative outward/return scans, complete translated
statement execution and source-step correspondence in `TM2TapeCost`.
Reality oracle: independent finite tape interpreter using reverse stack columns,
compared with direct stack semantics on generated statements and literal cases.

Reuse decision: use `TM2to1.tr`, `trStAct`, `trNormal`, existing stack-update
correctness (`tr_respects_aux₂`) and `TrCfg`. Add quantitative lemmas around that
translation rather than a second tape encoding/compiler. The current upstream
reachability theorems erase path length; treating them as cost bounds would be
an insufficient theorem, not evidence of polynomial-time execution. Initial
packing, finite reachable control support, native query/answer tape movement
and full algorithmic bounds still require connection before C5/C8 close.


C5 quantitative tape-translation result: targeted machine-checked evidence

`TM2TapeCost.scan_right` and `.scan_left` give exact n-tick executions of
Mathlib's existing go/return scans. `.top_action` reuses
`TM2to1.tr_respects_aux₂`, retaining every other tape column; `.roundtrip`

for n+n'+2 actual TM1 ticks. No second compiler or tape encoding was introduced.

`TM2TapeCost.statement` covers the entire translated statement, including local
loads, both branches and multiple stack operations. `accesses` counts the maximum
stack accesses on a branch. A statement starting with all stack lengths ≤H needs
at most a(2(H+a)+2) ticks after its initial translated entry, where a is its
access count. `source_step` includes that entry tick, deriving
1+a(2(H+a)+2) and preserving the complete existing `TM2to1.TrCfg` relation.
The H+a term accounts for preceding pushes within the same statement.

`BitOracleTapeCost.request_accesses` and `.response_accesses` derive a≤3 for the
actual lifted/framed request and consuming response programs, including saved
finite memory. `.request_step` and `.response_step` instantiate the complete
translation theorem: at most 6H+25 TM1 ticks for each actual port-program
transition, preserving every caller/private column through `TrCfg`. Height and
an existing related tape configuration are explicit simulation hypotheses;
complete initial packing and loop-level composition are not assumed discharged.

These bounds count TM1 ticks. The generic preservation theorem allows arbitrary
local-memory types; finite-domain and finite-reachable-syntax conditions are
still needed for primitive execution costs and are not hidden in this theorem.
C5's selected programs have finite data/control fields, but the actual uniform

## C5 enquiry: finite tape runs with derived growth and initial presentation (2026-09-14)

Goal: compose the checked statement translation over complete finite deterministic

Candidate claim: fixed finite code with maximum A stack accesses per statement,
initial stack height H and n source ticks has a corresponding actual translated
run of at most n(1+A(2(H+nA)+2)) TM1 ticks. Final height is at most H+nA.
Construct canonical reversed columns from the source configuration and derive
`TrCfg`; do not leave that presentation as a caller-supplied certificate.
Status: conjectured. Initial packing here is a data representation; an efficient
physical input loader remains a separate obligation.
Falsifier: repeated pushes refute a total bound computed from unchanged initial
height; unreversed columns refute a canonical packing claim on a nonpalindrome.
Formal oracle: planned `TM2TapeCost.statement_height`, finite-run composition,
canonical packing and its exact-output corollary, then actual port-region use.
Reality oracle: an independent persistent tape interpreter over generated finite
programs, compared with direct source execution, with long growing self-loops,
empty configurations, early halt, both branches and multiple occupied columns.
Residual scope: deterministic regions, not native oracle I/O; finite control and
primitive costs, input-loading execution and full oracle-loop integration remain
