### Resolution: finite deterministic runs and actual port regions

Claim/status: **machine-checked** and **validated** on the bounded independent
fixture scope below. `TM2TapeCost.statement_height` derives H+accesses(q) from
each actual statement. `TM2TapeRuns.run` composes the existing translated ticks
with derived intermediate height, including source halt padding. It proves
n(1+A(2(H+nA)+2)) ticks and final height ≤H+nA from an initial relation/bound.
`columns_nth`, `columns_presentation` and `pack_related` construct the canonical
reversed-column relation from actual finite stack data; `related_unique` shows
that the complete source configuration determines its related boundary tape.
`run_packed` derives both finite maxima and gives exact final packed-state
equality without caller-supplied presentation, height or code-bound premises.
Empty maxima are zero. Symbols/local memory remain generic.

`BitOracleTapeCost.request_run`/`.response_run` apply these results to the
existing complete framed transfer programs. At initial maximum height H and
source-fuel bound B, the actual TM1 run takes at most B(6H+18B+7) ticks.
Request B is |oldPort|+2|request|+4; response B is |oldDestination|+3|answer|+4.
The outgoing result is the exact copied-request configuration; the response
returns the actual resumed caller and derives both empty private columns.
This advances C5's deterministic regions, not merely a convenient unused class.

Positive controls: `TM2TapeRunsControls.derived_growing_run` applies the general
result to four pushes with no initial certificate. `actual_growing_run` checks
28 literal persistent-tape ticks and complete relevant columns. `early_halt`
uses the general theorem with zero-access code. Negative controls:
`frozen_height_fails` proves that no run of at most 20 ticks reaches the correct
four-push result; `packing_order_matters` distinguishes the correct source top
from unreversed nonpalindromic columns and retains a different caller column.
All five controls are kernel-checked; no native evaluation shortcut is used.

It checks full words, local memory, label/halt, returned head and accumulated
height/time bounds. It retains the same tape across source transitions.
Repeated-push and wrong-order mutants are detected; failures=0 and gaveUp=0.
These are bounded semantic fixtures, not a proof of the actual cryptographic
handler or physical oracle I/O.

Frozen initial height is a **false cost claim**, retained as a checked
counterexample. Unreversed packing is a **representation error**, also retained.

No additional cryptographic assumption or protocol restriction was introduced.

## C5 enquiry: physical outgoing oracle-tape transfer (2026-09-14)

Goal: connect the actual packed private request column to a separate native
query tape without a bulk host-language copy or reversed raw request.
Candidate claim: from a packed source stack word w and blank query tape, a
fixed three-phase, two-tape head-local program reaches a query tape containing
w in ordinary list order, restores the work head and retains the entire work
tape, in 2|w|+2 transitions. Each transition reads/writes current cells and moves
each head by at most one. The query tape is written leftward while the work
column is scanned rightward; this reverses the physical column order exactly
once. This is the narrow adapter to the existing Mathlib tape representation;
a new deterministic compiler or a bulk native stack operation is unnecessary.
Status: conjectured. This is an outgoing-region obligation; response loading,
blank-query restoration across calls and actual native query dispatch remain
separate integration work, not hidden premises of a completed C5 claim.
Falsifier: a nonpalindromic private word, a longer occupied caller column,
empty word, or stale nonblank query suffix. A rightward-writing mutant should
reverse the raw request; skipping the work-head return should fail full-state
equality even if query bits match.
Formal oracle: planned head-local outgoing program, exact run theorem and
application to `BitOracleTapeCost.request_run`'s actual packed output.
Reality oracle: independent two-head finite-tape interpreter compared with
ordinary source word and unchanged caller cells, retaining both mutants.
Trusted boundary: the local program uses Mathlib tapes and standard two-tape
read/write/move transitions. Its eventual oracle semantics and complete
standard-PPT interpretation are still open; native queries must not inspect
the work tape or invoke this whole transfer as one step.

Enquiry refinement before integration: the stale-query control confirms that
freshness cannot remain a per-call caller premise. Add a head-local clearing
phase for any prior canonical native word u. It writes blanks and advances
right, deriving a blank tape in |u|+1 transitions before export. Candidate
combined bound is |u|+2|w|+3; the whole work tape is untouched. This closes
query-tape reuse for canonical previous outputs. Native dispatch and response
loading remain separate; arbitrary malformed physical tapes are not admitted
as reachable native words without an invariant.

### Resolution: outgoing export and query-tape cleanup

Claim/status: **machine-checked**, with **validated** bounded fixtures.
`OracleTapeOutput.run_packed` exports every actual selected source stack in
ordinary bit order, in exactly 2|word|+2 head-local two-tape transitions. It
derives the selected column and bottom-marker laws from `TM2TapeRuns.pack`.
The conclusion restores the entire work tape, not merely selected observations.
`clear_run` physically clears every previous canonical query in |previous|+1
transitions. `run_replacing` composes them at |previous|+2|word|+3, including
empty and shorter replacement words. No per-call blank-tape premise remains
for canonical prior native outputs at their first bit.

`BitOracleTapeOutput.request_run` derives the actual input to this region from
`BitOracleTapeCost.request_run`, retaining the saved caller configuration and
complete prepared work tape. Its TM1 preparation bound B(6H+18B+7) is separate
from the head-local outgoing bound. This proves two actual region executions;
it does not yet define a complete native-dispatch machine or justify summing
mixed tick units as standard-PPT time. The transition definition traverses no
list: four finite phases read current cells, write at most one query cell and
move each head by at most one. Mathlib's two-way tapes, bottom marker and
existing deterministic compiler are reused without changes or dependencies.

Positive controls: `OracleTapeOutputControls.derived_export` applies the full
state theorem to [true,false,false] with a longer neighboring column;
`actual_export` checks literal head/cell results, and `empty_export` covers the
empty word. `rightward_write_fails` detects reversal independently of head

### Enquiry: standard tape transitions in the existing source interface (C5)

Goal: establish the converse local-computation component of attacker coverage.
Inspection: Mathlib supplies TM2-to-TM1-to-TM0 and TM0-to-TM1 translations;
its bundled polynomial-time interface uses finite TM2 machines. The inspected
pinned VCVioComplexity TuringMachine backend explicitly excludes oracle-TM
adequacy and leaves generic composition uninhabited. These results do not yet
admit every intended tape attacker into the current raw-oracle source model.
Representation obstacle: source words have explicit ends, whereas ordinary
binary tapes have a distinct blank and extend indefinitely in both directions.
Treating a missing cell as false would conflate blank and a data bit.

Candidate claim (conjectured): a three-symbol tape (blank, false, true) is
represented by two existing bit stacks, two bits per stored cell, and a
three-valued finite current-cell register. Every transition of an arbitrary
fixed finite-label Mathlib TM0 machine is implemented by one finite source
statement of local charge at most seven. Complete tape contents, head position
and halt status agree after arbitrary finite runs; a returned source halt keeps
the final tape. Formal oracle: proposed `BitTapeCoverage` transition/run/cost
theorems against pinned `TM0.step`. Falsifiers: moving left into blank tape,
writing false versus blank, returning over a previously written cell, or
swapping directions. Reality oracle: independently executed sparse integer-index
tape versus encoded left/right stacks, followed by literal Lean controls.

Narrow route: reuse TM2 push/pop/load/branch and the existing bit-source/physical
compiler; this adds no new execution backend or dependency. A framework
migration would still leave oracle I/O and quantitative correspondence and is
out of scope. This increment addresses ordinary tape transitions only. Raw
oracle suspension/query/answer transport, input conversion and full intended
PPT coverage remain separate C5 obligations. Do not report this local component
as all-attacker coverage or computational secrecy.

Result: machine-checked local coverage. `BitTapeCoverage.source_step` and
`.source_run` derive actual TM2 execution for every fixed TM0 machine over
Cell=Option Bool and a nonempty finite label set. `.native_step` identifies each
live transition with pinned Mathlib `TM0.step`; when it returns none the source
records its terminal label and retains the final tape. `.advance_tape` checks
native moves/writes exactly. `.represents_every_tape` covers every tape of that
model using finite side representatives; it is proof-side existence, not an
executable input conversion. `.cells_length` gives two bits per stored cell.
Encoding uses 00 for blank, 10 for false and 11 for true. Two bit stacks store
cells nearest the head first, and Fin 3 stores the current cell. Native moves
push its two bits on one side and pop two bits from the other; empty sides yield
blank. The compiled source has two fixed head-selection branches and no
unbounded host callback. `.local_cost` bounds every statement by seven source
operations; `.charged_run` derives total charge ≤7f and the exact complete
represented output after f steps. No query occurs in this deterministic local
program.

`.within` derives the original source halt/charge contract from actual native
termination. `.primitive_run` composes it with the existing primitive compiler
and clock: with B=7f, initial source height H and empty initial query/answer,
650*G*B*(H+B+1)^2 primitive ticks return the full represented native result.
The only termination premise is the native program's halt by f; there is no
caller-supplied source cost/presentation/correspondence certificate. Starting
from represented data remains explicit; this does not silently use proof-side
packing as physical input conversion.

Six `BitTapeCoverageControls` theorems independently check a complete write/
left/right run, the still-live preceding step, direct pinned TM0 execution on
that fixture, movement left into empty storage, a blank-versus-false branch,
and the derived whole-run charge. The native fixture ends with blank at the
head, false one cell left and true two cells left. PBT: 1,200 paths /48,000
transitions, seeds 7/19/41, initial lengths 0–12, 40 actions per path, checked
54 cells on both sides after every action. A sparse integer-index tape is
compared against encoded two-stack execution. Explicit missing-cell-as-false
and dropped-push-on-return mutants are detected. Failures/gaveUp: zero. The
campaign tests representation moves/writes, not arbitrary machine programs or
oracle I/O. Reproduction: `python3 scripts/check-helios-bit-tape-coverage.py`;
`bit-tape-coverage-fixtures.json` and `bit-tape-coverage-controls.log` under
`tmp/concrete-helios/`.

### Enquiry: executable raw input-to-cell conversion (C5)

Goal: remove the represented-cell entry premise from the local tape coverage
component. Candidate claim (conjectured): a fixed two-stack, three-register-value
source prelude consumes an arbitrary raw input on port 1, reverses its bits onto
port 0, encodes them back onto port 1, then extracts the current head. In exactly
2|word|+3 source transitions it returns the native input representation: empty
left stack, current head equal to the first bit (blank for empty input), and
right stack containing tagged cells for the remaining bits in original order.
The existing physical loader supplies its raw entry; source linking must return
to the actual native program without a free conversion or caller correspondence
certificate. Native computation and conversion must have derived source costs.
Falsifiers: non-palindromic input, losing a false data bit as blank, leaving
scratch data, skipping the final head extraction, or restarting input conversion
on the native return label. Formal oracle: proposed `BitTapeInput` run/link
and physical-startup theorems. Reality oracle: independent raw-word expectations
and literal source/primitive controls; bounded stack interpreter fixtures.
Reuse existing TM2 operations, return linking and physical loading. Do not add
another execution backend. Native oracle I/O, full attacker coverage and the
actual scalar policy remain C5; all-PPT secrecy remains open.

Result: machine-checked. `BitTapeInput.run` executes exactly 2|word|+3 source
transitions, returning the represented native input with blank left side,
first-bit head (blank on empty input), correctly ordered tagged remaining cells
and no scratch data. Its finite register needs no saved unbounded input. The
first pass reverses raw bits, the second inserts each present-cell tag, and
the final step extracts the head. `.local_cost` bounds each statement by five.
`BitTapeStart.program` links these three phases to arbitrary fixed native TM0
code via the existing `TM2ReturnLink.redirect`/`.run`. Label 3 is a separate
halt point; native labels start at 4. `.convert_run` derives the actual handoff;
`.run` reaches the original native result and halts within 2|word|+f+4 source
transitions when that native program halts by f. `.local_cost` bounds the linked
statements by seven. `.charged_run` derives B=7(2|word|+f+4) and complete source
output. No input-conversion, source-cost or correspondence premise is supplied
by the caller.

`BitOracleMachine.compute_run_cost` factors the necessary deterministic charge
induction over the existing source interpreter. `BitTapeCoverage.charged_run`
now derives its unchanged result from that lemma; its duplicate specialized
induction was removed. This is reuse for the conversion/link cost obligation,
not a parallel backend. All prior native tape controls remain checked.

`BitTapeStart.physical_run` starts with blank working storage and the actual
native raw input tape. It derives a startup u≤4|word|+8 and, with the B above,
returns the complete native result after u+650*G*B*(|word|+B+1)^2 prelude/primitive
steps under the existing bounded raw-oracle adapter. Only native termination
by f is assumed. The full source Within/Allowed contract, initial source
presentation and maximum word height are derived. The linked source contains
only local computation, so its complete query tree is pure; no oracle event is
introduced by conversion. Full caller observation and packing remain proof-side.
This result closes raw input-to-cell conversion and its physical/native linking
for local computation, not native oracle I/O or complete attacker coverage.

### Enquiry: exact native oracle reference interface (C5)

Goal: make the remaining attacker-coverage correspondence concrete before
extending the compiler. Current obstruction (insufficient representation): the
checked local TM0 component has one tape, whereas an ordinary oracle attacker
can move/read/write work, query and answer tapes independently. Reusing its
work tape as the answer tape loses private workspace. Treating native buffers
as abstract word stacks would need its own normalization theorem; it cannot
silently establish standard-PPT coverage.

Chosen narrow reference: fixed finite labels and three ordinary Option Bool
tapes. Code receives only the three current cells. A local transition selects
at most one move/write per tape, or no action. A native hash reads the contiguous
query word at its head through the existing `OracleTapeDispatch.readWord`;
a coin uses the existing raw coin event. Both preserve full work/query tapes
and replace the full answer tape, then resume at an explicit finite label.
Use the existing dispatch operation to retain exactly the current raw oracle
semantics. No Lake dependency, framework migration or upstream edit is needed.

Candidate claim (conjectured): `NativeOracleTape.step` selects local behavior
only from finite labels/current cells, preserves exactly the existing native
query/answer tree, and derives full work/query frame preservation at native
calls for every raw answer. Literal controls must distinguish query heads and
embedded blanks, retain private work and stale query data, replace old answers,
and let received answers affect subsequent local actions. Formal oracle:
proposed native event/frame/run theorems and controls. Reality oracle: opened
`OracleTapeDispatch` definitions plus independent literal tape/trace fixtures.
These are reference semantics and correspondence to existing dispatch, not yet
a source compiler or all-PPT theorem.

Remaining compiler declarations are intended to discharge these separate
obligations: a three-tape presentation using six cell stacks and finite current-
cell registers; local-action simulation using the existing single-tape/frame
proofs; physical prefix extraction from the represented query tape; response
conversion with work/query preservation; successor-invariant and complete
query-tree matching; and an input/answer-length polynomial clock from native
termination. Keep these within C5 in the sole task list. Do not call native
interface agreement itself completed attacker coverage.

Result: machine-checked reference interface and agreement with existing native
semantics. `NativeOracleTape` has a fixed finite transition table over labels
and three current cells. `.heads_finite` / `.commands_finite` establish finite
input and output domains. A local command performs at most one move/write per
tape, including optional no-action entries. `.hash_step` / `.coin_step` identify
the actual complete raw OracleComp event and successor with the existing native
dispatch. `.oracle_successor` derives, for every supported native reply, the
selected next label, unchanged full work/query tapes and a canonical replacement
answer tape. Query heads, left cells and data beyond an embedded blank require
no canonical-query premise. `.run_add` and `.run_halted` retain bounded query-tree
composition and absorbing terminal states.

The semantic adapter invokes existing dispatch with an unused constant work
component, then retains the reference machine's actual work tape. Existing
dispatch never inspects its work field, and the exact native event equations
are checked. This is not a runtime work conversion, source compiler or new
cryptographic operation. The original raw hash/coin spec, word interpretation,
public query events and handler semantics remain unchanged.

Six `NativeOracleTapeControls` theorems check an embedded-blank query with stale
cells and a displaced old answer, a private-frame counterexample to work/answer
aliasing, query-head motion changing the next request, both answer-driven coin
branches, and complete halted-state retention. In the alias counterexample the
work and returned answer have the same visible word prefix but different cells
to the left of the head. This is an insufficient-representation counterexample,
not a cryptographic attack or a failure of the existing dispatcher.
Independent fixtures: 3,000 native events, seeds 7/19/41, sparse cells at -4..4,
heads -3..3, hash reply lengths 0–12; work-alias and query-reset mutants detected.
Failures/gaveUp: zero. These fixtures validate native event/frame behavior on
that scope; they do not test source compilation. Proof-engineering failure:
the constructor named `local` required quoting in one cases alternative; an
explicit reduction resolved a native query bind's presentation. No admits,
axioms, raised limits, new dependencies or upstream changes.

Residual: this interface makes the compiler target precise but is not completed
standard-PPT coverage. The current single-tape source entry must be extended to
six cell stacks/three finite head registers. Planned `NativeOracleCompile`
declarations must prove `.local_step`, `.query_run`, `.answer_run`, `.run` and
`.within`, deriving local action matching, exact raw requests, framed response
replacement, successor/query-tree correspondence and a polynomial bound from
native termination/answer widths. Any normalization needed to justify coverage
of the intended standard-PPT class must be proved rather than silently assumed.
The actual scalar policy and full algorithm runtime obligations remain separate.
Main/supporting counts stay 2/3 (Step 3 active) and 6/12; computational secrecy is
open. Targeted controls and `python3 scripts/check-helios-native-oracle.py` pass;
results are in `tmp/concrete-helios/native-oracle-controls.log` and
`native-oracle-fixtures.json`. Integrated audit evidence follows.

## Completion prototype enquiry: polynomial accuracy and asymptotic assembly (2026-09-14)

User steering: first test an end-to-end completion prototype before further
low-level execution construction. Preserve the full computational goal and all
completed evidence. The preceding turn made progress by finishing the native
interface integration audit and recording its precise residual compiler gap;
the discussion then selected this endpoint-first route.

Goal: compose the actual finite prepared-election reduction into negligible
advantage with feasible accuracy choices, exposing unfinished DDH efficiency
and family/correspondence obligations explicitly. Candidate claim: for each
fixed degree k choose e(n)=(n+1)^(k+1); negligible actual DDH advantages for each
such reduction, negligible reciprocal field size and polynomial query budgets
imply negligible original prepared-game bias. The conclusion concerns the
existing fixed election game, with its actual public observations and rejection.
It is a conditional prototype, not standard-PPT secrecy or goal completion.

Smallest falsifier: treating one fixed inverse-polynomial accuracy as negligible,
or using exponential accuracy while claiming polynomial replay count. The
quantifier order must be for every fixed degree a corresponding polynomial-time
reduction, not one reduction with superpolynomial accuracy. Formal oracle:
planned `ElectionSecrecyPrototype.prepared_negligible_of_ddh`, linked directly to
`ElectionDDHSource.prepared_ballot_secrecy_ddh_bound`. Reality oracle: independent
rational checks of scaled extraction slack and the published source repetition
formula 3456*(N+1)^3*e^4; retain the existing queried attack/repair/reduction
controls. No cryptographic hardness claim will be tested on a small toy group.

Trusted definitions: existing prepared shared-oracle game, exact two public DDH
tests and pinned VCVio negligibility. Residual: DDH security for the exact
reductions requires the unfinished runtime proofs; intended standard-PPT
coverage, scalar sampling transport, security-family/election policy and
historical attack transport stay open. C5–C9/C12 stay incomplete. No admits or
new global axioms are authorized. Status: conjectured before implementation.


### Prototype result: conditional original-election negligibility

Status: machine-checked conditional theorem; root build and exact-name axiom
audit complete, PDF integration pending. The prototype directly applies
`ElectionDDHSource.prepared_ballot_secrecy_ddh_bound` to each instance of
`ElectionSecrecyPrototype.PreparedFamily`. This family retains the original
game, all preparation/casting/guessing callbacks and public observations. Its
fields include generator injectivity and actual preparation/casting hash-query
bounds. It does not include a PPT, semantic correspondence or local-cost
certificate.

`prepared_negligible_of_ddh` proves negligible original prepared-game bias from
four explicit asymptotic premises: a natural polynomial bound on p+c,
negligible reciprocal (|F|-1), negligible exact main DDH advantage for every
fixed degree k, and negligible exact honest-rejection DDH advantage. The main
reduction runs e(n)=(n+1)^(k+1) and the original replay formula.
`accuracy_admissible` derives its eventual field-size constraint from the first
two premises; `replay_bounded` derives polynomial domination of the actual
family's repetition count. `negligible_of_polynomial_accuracy` proves the
quantifier-sensitive assembly: for any fixed k the scaled extraction allowance
is at most 2/(n+1), and the scaled algebraic/DDH errors tend to zero. VCVio's
negligibility, polynomial-loss and real/extended-real bridges are reused
unchanged; no new general complexity framework is introduced.

Four controls pass. Positive literals independently pin e(1,2)=9, the actual
replay count 612220032 at N=2, and scaled slack 4/9<2/3. Negative controls show
that fixed linear accuracy breaks the scaled bound and prove that 2/(n+1) is
not negligible. The existing nonvacuous, querying/view-dependent finite
prepared-election reduction controls remain imported, along with all independent
attack and repair controls in the aggregate. The new arithmetic fixtures test
3,000 cases (seeds 7/19/41; n 0..128, k 0..8, budget 0..64), with zero failures
and gaveUp; fixed-accuracy and linear-replay mutants are detected. This campaign
checks rational arithmetic, not DDH hardness or compiler correctness.

Failures were proof engineering: cast normalization, numeral polynomial
evaluation, one redundant solved-goal tactic and simplification orientation.
A proposed positive check that merely repeated its negligibility premise was
removed as non-informative. The fixed-accuracy shortcut is a false mathematical
claim, retained as a checked counterexample. Neither finding refutes the
historical security theorem. No admits, custom axioms, limit changes or upstream
changes were used.

The prototype does not assume that its extraction error is negligible, choose
exponential replay accuracy, or assume the original game's secrecy. Its two
DDH-security premises remain unproved from standard computational hardness.
Their discharge requires actual algorithm efficiency and sampler transport;
coverage of intended PPT election attackers and election/corruption policy
remain C5/C9. The planned declarations identifying these obligations are recorded
under C12 in the sole task list. This is a completed conditional assembly, not
completed all-PPT secrecy. Counts remain 2/3 main milestones and 6/12 checkpoints.

### Complete binary remainder result

Status: machine-checked full loaded-word division; root build and exact-name
axiom audit pass, PDF integration pending. `BinaryModuloMachine.program` uses
finite control and eight Boolean stacks. Raw input is little-endian. A physical
stack-reversal loop prepares its most-significant-first traversal. Each iteration
reads a bit, calls the existing `BinarySubtractMachine.remainder_step` through
`TM2StackFrame` and `TM2ReturnLink`, then moves output through two stack-transfer
passes back to the canonical remainder stack. No new arithmetic backend or
host modulo instruction is introduced.

`BinaryModuloMachine.run` quantifies over every raw Boolean word w and q>0.
Starting with w and q.bits loaded and the specified empty stacks, it derives
an actual halt within |w|*(8*q.size+13)+2 TM2 ticks, canonical remainder bits
for bitsValue(w)%q, the unchanged modulus, all input/scratch empty and memory
none. The loop proof maintains r<q and derives the next canonical width at
most q.size; `result_width` also exposes the final bound. Existing one-update
cost is at most 6*q.size+9; reading and the two return passes add at most
2*q.size+3 per bit. Initial reversal and final halt give the total. The bound
counts fixed-control TM2 ticks, not a completed physical oracle sampler.

Seven controls pass. Full-state literal executions cover six modulo five,
two modulo three, padded input, modulus one, empty input and a live reversal
prefix; the general theorem also instantiates at modulus three for every raw
word with bound 29*|w|+2. Nonzero/nonpalindromic outputs exclude immediate halt,
constant output, reversed input and one-pass return. The independent driver
fixtures ran before the general loop proof: 16,352 exhaustive cases (width
0..8, q=1..32) and 1,500 seeded cases (7/19/41; width 0..128, q=1..65536).
They reuse the validated subtraction interpreter, execute driver stack moves,
and compare with independently computed integer modulo and binary strings.
Both input-reversal and return-transfer mutants are detected; failures and
gaveUp are zero. Existing subtraction/attack/repair controls are retained.

identity. The parser failure produced downstream invalid-declaration errors;
no admits were inserted. A final literal specialization needed explicit size/
digit reduction. No mathematical claim or bound was weakened. No custom axioms,

### C6 enquiry: link actual coin loading to division

Goal: replace the loader's proof-side modulo observation with executed division
on the same output stacks, retaining the exact coin tree and polynomial cost.

`Option Bool` memory types; `BitOracleMachine` uses `Fin` coordinates. Existing
`TM2StackFrame` handles stack relocation and `TM2ReturnLink` handles call/return,
but neither changes the local-memory coordinates. A narrow executable
`BinaryModuloCode` translation will encode this fixed program into eight ports,
fifteen labels and three memory values, with a whole-transition proof. Reworking
the general oracle-machine definition would touch many existing interfaces;
this fixed-program adapter preserves them and introduces no new backend.

Candidate claims: the coordinate translation commutes with every division step
and run, retains the complete input/output frame and has local source cost at
most 32. Then a fixed program can load the chronological coin word, enter the
translated division and return canonical remainder digits, preserving its
modulus and clearing scratch. The intended final source clock combines 4*w+2
loader steps, w*(8*q.size+13)+2 division steps and the terminal return step.
Formal oracle: `BinaryModuloCode.run` and the planned combined program theorem.
Smallest falsifiers: aliasing raw and pending stacks, reversing a nonpalindromic
result, or returning to the coin loader after division. Independent reality
oracle: supplied deterministic coin streams and integer modulo; reuse the
independent loader/division interpreters and retain full-state Lean controls.
Status: conjectured. Width/modulus loading and scalar writer handoff remain
separate parts of C6 condition 3; no original secrecy premise is weakened.

Result: machine-checked in targeted builds, with all five combined controls.
`BinaryModuloCode.tick`/`.run` prove the executable finite coordinate translation
on every configuration, including intermediate scratch. `.local_cost` checks

bijections, not choice-based executable conversion. `CoinModuloMachine.code`
relocates the existing `CoinWordLoader.code` and enters the translated division
on those same eight stacks. Its safe-label invariant excludes the coin region
once division starts; the checked original return linker exits through one
terminal label. `load_run` derives the real call boundary; `divide_run` derives
the deterministic remainder run and local charge inside the combined program.

`CoinModuloMachine.run_source` gives a single fixed source program with clock
(4*w+2)+(w*(8*q.size+13)+3) and leaf charge at most
15*w+9+32*(w*(8*q.size+13)+3). The proof derives the output-dependent charges,
uses the actual coin-word support length, and preserves the full oracle query

## Executed modular multiplication prerequisite (2026-09-14)

Claim: **conjectured**. `BinaryModMultiply.run` must execute multiplication of
loaded canonical public coordinates modulo p with a cost polynomial in their
bit widths. The first honest proof request needs exponentiation, whose efficient
implementation requires this multiplication. Existing coordinate equations do
not execute either operation. Existing subtraction and remainder-step routines
are sufficient arithmetic subroutines; a finite outer controller and actual
operand transport are absent.

Smallest required inner claim: a scoped modular-add controller, for r,x<p and
retained c=p−x, executes guarded r−c. On success it returns r−c; on underflow it
executes c−r then p−(c−r). It preserves c and p, clears work and returns canonical
(r+x)%p with a derived linear width bound. The prepared complement is an explicit
inner interface: the multiplier must execute p−x itself before invoking it.
No full-source theorem may assume that missing preparation. Reusing subtraction
avoids introducing an independent carry adder/full-product development; the
alternative product-then-division route needs those additional algorithms.

Falsifiers: equality r=c must wrap to zero, zero operands must not become p,
borrow chains must preserve operand order, and either branch must retain the
original p/c and scratch policy. The full multiplier must distinguish p from
scalar modulus q and scan bits in the right order. Formal oracle: actual finite
TM2/bit-oracle execution and named run/cost theorems. Reality oracle: independent
integer modular arithmetic and the concrete p23/q11 encryption fixture recorded
in the task list. First test small moduli exhaustively and large borrow boundaries;
then test actual loaded execution before general proofs. The parallel agent owns
only the necessary arithmetic identities and their refutation controls; the main
agent owns executable controllers, state/cost proofs and source integration.

Arithmetic gate and proof: **machine-checked** identities in
`BinaryModMultiplyArithmetic` relate the complement branches to modular addition,
bound intermediate widths, and identify MSB-first double/add folding with the
integer product modulo p. The independent gate checks 11,952 additions and 9,216
folds, including seeded moduli/words through 128 bits, with zero discards/gaveUp.
Strict-threshold and reversed-subtraction mutations have minimized kernel controls.
Existing Nat modulo/distributivity and List fold/reverse lemmas suffice. These
results assert no machine execution or cost. Log:
`tmp/concrete-helios/modmultiply-arithmetic-target.log`; gate report:
`tmp/concrete-helios/modmultiply-arithmetic-gate.json`.

Executed reduced-add gate: **validated** on 1,808 full-state cases: 1,496 exhaustive
p=1..16 pairs, 192 seeded cases (118/606/20260914×64), and 120 directed borrow/width
cases through 64 bits. The actual finite code preserves complement/modulus,
clears work, and agrees with independent modular addition and proposed clock/
charge bounds. Four actual-code mutants are detected before candidate testing:
skipped underflow path, omitted complement copy, corrupted modulus and omitted
result restoration. No discards/gaveUp. Reproduce with
`python3 scripts/check_mod_add.py`; report `tmp/concrete-helios/mod-add-native.json`.
The general executed state/cost proof is in progress, not inferred from this gate.

The actual outer multiplier is built in `BinaryModMultiply`: it copies the
modulus, executes p−x preparation, reverses/reads multiplier bits, performs modular
doubling and conditional reduced addition, and clears the prepared complement
before returning the product with original p/x retained. Thus its executable
entry does not receive a precomputed complement. Its independent native gate
checks 792 loaded products (576 exhaustive small cases, 96 seeded raw words,
120 directed boundaries), including noncanonical high-zero padding and empty
multiplier words. All eleven ports, results, halt/memory and proposed clock/charge
bounds agree; five actual-code mutants are detected before candidate testing.

Checked transition and source boundary:

- `PrimeProgrammedInsertInputMachine.run`, `.padded_run`, `.charged` and
  `.charged_bounded` execute the cache copy and old-destination clear while
  retaining the arbitrary frame. Exact clock is `3*cache.length+4`; the bounded
  source instance uses `3*N+4`, with charge at most 32 times that clock.
- `CacheProgrammedInsertMachine.run`/`.charged_bounded` execute the unchanged
  insertion, capture collision before clearing residual work, and return the
  complete twelve-port state. With insertion bound `I`, initial height bound
  `H`, and the existing code access factor `A`, the derived clock is
  `I+3*(H+I*A)+5`, with charge at most 32 times that clock. The source wrapper
  derives `I` and `H`; they are not assumed execution certificates.
- `PrimeProgrammedInsertSource.source_fields`, `.source_work`,
  `.source_statement_widths`, `.source_payload_lengths` and `.source_input_bound`
  derive the actual key, sampled challenge, cache/flag/history, seven empty
  work ports and uniform bounds from the original typed source. In particular,
  each saved cache/history payload is at most the original raw length `N`,
  and the local input-height envelope is
  `1+3*N+keyRecordBitBound p+groupRecordBitBound q`.
- `PrimeProgrammedInsertMachine.charged_source` executes preparation and
  insertion on the reached 48-port state. `.source_state` identifies updated
  shadow 44 and flag 46; live 45 and old history 47 are preserved.
- `PrimeProgrammedHistoryMachine.run`/`.charged_bounded` build the actual nested
  statement, parse and increment the history count, and prepend the statement
  in place on 47. They clear work 23–29 and preserve every other word.
  `PrimeProgrammedHistoryMachine.charged_source` derives all loaded numeric,
  canonical history, workspace and size premises from the post-insertion state.
  `.source_state` identifies the exact original `state.program` successor.
- `PrimeProgramMachine.charged_source` combines those actual runs with derived
  full-state returns and charge addition. `PrimeProgramCaller.linked_run`,
  `.run_support`, `.execution_source`, `.source_state`, `.source_retained`,
  `.within` and `.physical_run` connect original raw input to the same nonce
  and transcript draw tree and final resident update. The new deterministic
  transition makes no new oracle queries. Its raw clock and cost are the sums
  of the checked extraction prefix and resident program bounds.

The history clock for public modulus `p` and history-size bound `H` is
`4*NatFieldWriterMachine.clock (p-1) + 2*FrameWriteMachine.cost (pairBound p)
+ FrameWriteMachine.cost (statementRecordBitBound p) + 5*H.size
+ 3*(H+1).size + 17`. Its charge is bounded by 32 times this clock. Numeric
coordinates are bounded by `p`, while sampled scalars and cache values use
`q`; the source proofs retain this distinction. The raw physical theorem
starts with one canonical raw word and blank work/auxiliary tapes. Writing
`B = PrimeProgramCaller.cost raw slack p q`, it derives startup at most
`4*raw.length+8` and the existing primitive simulation bound
`BitOracleTapeCap.unitCost (raw.length+B)*B*
BitOraclePrimitiveLoop.globalFactor PrimeProgramCaller.code`. This is a bound
for this concrete finite caller, not the unimplemented subsequent calls.

The typed source theorems assume prime `p` and `q`, typed group elements,
scalars, and arbitrary finite shadow/live states. They do not assume cache
freshness, an empty initial state, agreement between occupied values, or a
caller-supplied canonical-memory/cost correspondence. Local numeric theorems
state their canonical operand/work/size hypotheses; the source layer proves
those hypotheses. The exact original first-request factorization remains the
semantic origin. Returned proof serialization and subsequent source
continuations are still outside this executed prefix.

usable conservative composition bound. Polynomially many iterations of a

requires structural cache/history/replay-state growth, for which existing
`next_counts`, `next_outputBound`, `next_inputSize` and request-prefix bounds are
relevant pieces. The fixed two-call test cannot discharge that family obligation.

### Native compilation acceptance theorem and derived cost

Outcome: **proved for the fixed program**, integrated and audited. The final
build, axiom/claim audits, independent gate and reference review pass as recorded
below.
The wider standard-PPT coverage claim remains open.

`NativeAdaptiveRun.exact_run` proves execution of
`NativeWordCompiler.code NativeAdaptiveProbe.code`, with only four arbitrary
input/private/old-answer word arguments. Its exact 19-step result has the native
hash(input), coin, hash(dependent word) tree, all six terminal stacks, successful
halt/memory, and charge
`66 + |input| + |oldAnswer| + 2|firstReply| + |dependent| + |secondReply|`.
The dependent word is `[firstReply.headD false, coin] ++ input.drop 2`.
`.native_correspondence` identifies the complete native eight-step tree and
terminal tapes. The observation requires successful halt and memory zero, so a
partial run or explicit unsupported-operation halt cannot satisfy it.
`NativeAdaptiveCost.within` derives
`68 + 2|input| + |oldAnswer| + 3*limit` for every allowed reply branch.
`.physical_run` specializes existing `BitOraclePrimitiveBounded.run_source_bounded`
using that proved bound. The clock is the existing tape unit-cost factor at
`height(start) + bound + |previousQuery|`, multiplied by the bound and the
actual generated code's finite primitive factor. Both sides use the same bounded
reply adapter. No execution correspondence or cost certificate is assumed.

The complete-state premises are derived by the fixed path: each query move
crosses a cell established by its preceding write; the answer-left stack is
initially empty and remains empty before replacement. Independent private work
has arbitrary dense before/right words. The full first reply affects the cost
of replacement, and the complete second reply survives in the final answer.
The initial six-stack presentation is already resident. Startup serialization/
packing/loading, arbitrary native tapes with interior blanks, a general native
compiler and intended standard-PPT attacker coverage are not proved here.

Independent validation: `scripts/NativeAdaptiveCompilerGate.lean` executes the
actual generated code on all 810 cases from input words of length at most three,
each reply of length at most one, both coins, and three distinct private frames.
Three longer/empty directed cases and four actual source-code mutations also
run. The oracle specifies complete six-stack states, memory/label, event words
and order, and exact charge independently of the source evaluator. Each mutant
matches its independently predicted full outcome and is distinguished from the
original. No random seeds, discarded cases or gaveUp outcomes occur in this
finite enumeration. The source gate separately retains three kernel-checked
full-native-state positives and four instruction mutations. Handler replies
are chosen per query occurrence; no random-oracle caching law is silently added.

`NativeWordCompilerBoundary` retains five checked facts about valid native
blank-write/blank-move programs that the restricted translator explicitly rejects.
These are representation limits of the chosen fixed-program experiment, not
counterexamples to its accepted theorem. The source/target success observation

### Checked round-trip outcome

Status: machine-checked, integrated and audited; publication follows this record.
`NativeRoundTrip.execution_correspondence` proves equality of the complete free
oracle event tree with the actual hash/coin request and exact resident result.
`native_correspondence` supplies a common event tree for the actual native step
and represented execution, with `Represents` proved at every leaf.
`framed_correspondence` lifts that exact result to any finite number of arbitrary
private words. `framed_cost` bounds every allowed branch by `callCost`, derived
from the executed instructions; no caller supplies correspondence or cost.

For query word Q, hash reply limit L, export clock E = 2|query-after|+6 and
import clock I = 2|answer-before|+|Q|+2(L+1)+5, the observation fuel is E+I+4,
after one unconditional actual entry step. Total source charge is at most
8+6E+(2+|Q|+2|answer-after|+(L+1))+5I. Hash support is exactly all words of
length at most L, including empty; coin support is exactly both singleton bits.
Code is independent of the fuel and width bound. The result preserves work and
query heads and both complete cell halves, clears old answer-before, replaces
answer-after with the encoded reply tail, sets the reply head, empties raw-query
and scratch ports and restores the local register before the original live return.
